#include <andes_sim/roi.h>

#define HI ((volatile uint64_t *)0x7FFFF000ull)   /* 2 GiB - 4 KiB */

int main(void)
{
  HI[0] = 0x1122334455667788ull;
  HI[1] = 0xCAFEF00DDEADBEEFull;

  uint64_t a = HI[0], b = HI[1];
  if (a != 0x1122334455667788ull || b != 0xCAFEF00DDEADBEEFull) {
    printf("FAIL: nothing at 0x7FFFF000 -- not enough guest memory\n");
    return 1;
  }
  printf("store+readback at 0x7FFFF000 (2 GiB - 4 KiB): OK\n");

  andes_sim_roi_begin();
  a = HI[0]; b = HI[1];           /* on hybrid this read runs on the RTL */
  if (a == 0x1122334455667788ull && b == 0xCAFEF00DDEADBEEFull)
    printf("PASS: the ROI sees the pattern at 2 GiB - 4 KiB\n");
  else
    printf("FAIL: pattern lost\n");
  andes_sim_roi_end();
  return 0;
}'''

cells = [
md("""# andes-sim tutorial: guest memory (`--mem-size`)

Every model defaults to a small guest memory (128 MiB). This tutorial
shows how to request more with one flag, what each model does with it,
and where the bytes actually live.

You will:

1. build a program that needs 2 GiB of guest memory,
2. watch it fault under the default, then fix it with `--mem-size`,
3. learn the 2 GiB cap (the AE350 DRAM window) and how each model
   reports it,
4. see the hybrid model's backing-store tiers (`/dev/shm`, then
   `~/.cache/andes-sim`) and how to pin one,
5. check your machine with `andes-sim doctor`."""),

code("""import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andes-sim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)"""),

md("""## 1. A program that needs 2 GiB

The program writes a pattern at `0x7FFFF000` - 4 KiB below the top of
the 2 GiB DRAM window - and verifies it twice: once immediately, and
once inside the ROI markers (on a hybrid run that second check executes
on the RTL engine, after the handoff).

It links against the vplat runtime, so the same binary runs on every
model, and a `printf` inside the ROI is allowed (it bottoms out in a
UART both engines model):"""),

code("""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null      # sets HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > highmem.c <<'EOF'
""" + HIGHMEM + """
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -I build/runtime/include \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs highmem.c -o highmem.elf

echo "built:"; file highmem.elf"""),

md("""## 2. The default is small - watch it fault

`--model fast` is QEMU as-is: andes-sim does not inject any memory
setting, so QEMU's own 128 MiB default applies. A load at 2 GiB has no
memory behind it, and the runtime's trap handler reports a load access
fault (`Exception code: 5`) at exactly our address (`mtval:
0x7ffff000`):"""),

code("""!andes-sim run --model fast highmem.elf""", allow_fail=True),

md("""Request the memory and the same binary passes. On `fast` the flag
just forwards a plain `-m 2048M` to QEMU - nothing else changes (and a
`-m` you pass yourself after `--` would still win):"""),

code("""!andes-sim run --model fast --mem-size 2G highmem.elf"""),

md("""## 3. The cap: 2 GiB

The AE350 SoC decodes DRAM at `0x0 .. 0x80000000`, so 2 GiB is a hard
ceiling for any QEMU-backed model. Each model reports an over-ask in
its own way - `fast` lets QEMU say it:"""),

code("""!andes-sim run --model fast --mem-size 4G highmem.elf""", allow_fail=True),

md("""...while `hybrid` rejects it in the driver, **before** allocating
the (potentially huge) backing file - note there is no `[hsim mmap]`
line:"""),

code("""!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 4G highmem.elf""", allow_fail=True),

md("""(`--model cycle` has nothing to size - the RTL engine always
models its full DRAM window - so there `--mem-size` is validated and
declared a no-op on stderr.)

## 4. hybrid: one flag, three views of the same bytes

On a hybrid run `--mem-size` sizes one shared thing: a sparse file that
is at once

- the **mmap** both legs share,
- QEMU's **memory backend** (= guest RAM), and
- the RTL engine's **RAM window** after the handoff.

The `[hsim mmap]` status line shows where it lives. The file is sparse:
2 GiB of address space, but only pages the program touches cost RAM -
this run really uses a few MiB:"""),

code("""!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2G highmem.elf"""),

md("""Both checks pass: the pattern QEMU wrote at 2 GiB - 4 KiB is read
back by the RTL engine through the shared mmap, and the
`[marker window_cycles]` line prices the ROI on the real core.

### Where the file lives: backing tiers

The backing directory comes from a two-tier list, first fit wins
(fit = size + 256 MiB free):

1. `/dev/shm` - tmpfs, RAM speed;
2. `~/.cache/andes-sim` - disk-backed, for when the request exceeds
   tmpfs (hot pages still sit in the page cache, so the cost is
   background writeback only).

A fallback is never silent - the status line carries the reason, e.g.

    [hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andes-sim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))

`HSIM_MMAP_DIR` pins a single directory instead (no fallback past the
pin - too small is then a hard error):"""),

code("""%%bash
PIN=$(mktemp -d)
HSIM_MMAP_DIR="$PIN" \\
  andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \\
  --mem-size 256M highmem.elf 2>/dev/null | grep "hsim mmap"
rm -rf "$PIN\""""),

md("""## 5. Check your machine

`andes-sim doctor` ends with an `mmap tiers:` section: each tier with
its free space. On WSL2 it also warns when the repo or a tier directory
sits under `/mnt/` (drvfs - slow, and `MAP_SHARED` is not coherent
there) and reminds you that `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory
(`.wslconfig`, `memory=`):"""),

code("""!andes-sim doctor 2>/dev/null | sed -n '/^mmap tiers:/,$p'"""),

md("""## 6. Portability notes

The hybrid handoff needs both legs on **one Linux kernel**, with the
mmap on a filesystem local to that kernel:

| Host | How to run |
|------|-----------|
| Linux | native - everything in this tutorial as-is |
| Windows (WSL2) | as Linux; keep the repo and mmap dirs on ext4 (`~/...`), never `/mnt/c`; raise `memory=` in `.wslconfig` if tier 1 is small |
| macOS | run-only: `./andes-sim` re-execs inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image (podman machine VM); the mmap lives in the VM's `/dev/shm`. `brew install podman && podman machine init && podman machine start`, then use `./andes-sim` exactly as above. Knobs: `ANDES_SIM_IMAGE`, `ANDES_SIM_SHM_SIZE`. |

## Recap

| Model | `--mem-size SPEC` does | default | over 2G |
|-------|------------------------|---------|---------|
| `fast` | forwards a plain QEMU `-m` (only when given) | QEMU's own 128 MiB | QEMU's own error |
| `hybrid` | sizes the shared mmap = QEMU backend = RTL RAM window | 128 MiB | driver error, before allocating |
| `cycle` | validated, then a stderr note - the RTL always models its full window | full window | n/a |

Details: `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 2.5 (memory + tiers) and 2.5.1
(WSL2/macOS)."""),
]

# --- execute code cells and capture outputs -------------------------------
env = dict(os.environ)
env["PATH"] = f"{ROOT}/build:" + env["PATH"]
count = 0
for cell in cells:
    if cell["cell_type"] != "code":
        continue
    src = "".join(cell["source"])
    if src.startswith("%%bash"):
        argv = ["bash", "-c", src.split("\n", 1)[1]]
    elif src.lstrip().startswith("!"):
        script = "\n".join(l.lstrip()[1:] for l in src.splitlines()
                           if l.strip())
        argv = ["bash", "-c", script]
    else:
        argv = [sys.executable, "-c", src]
    proc = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=ROOT, env=env, text=True, timeout=400,
                          stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                          stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    if proc.returncode != 0 and not cell.pop("_allow_fail", False):
        print(f"CELL FAILED (rc={proc.returncode}):\n{src}\n---\n{proc.stdout}")
        sys.exit(1)
    cell.pop("_allow_fail", None)
    count += 1
    cell["execution_count"] = count
    text = proc.stdout
    if text:
        cell["outputs"] = [{"name": "stdout", "output_type": "stream",
                            "text": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}]
    print(f"cell {count} ok ({len(text)} bytes output)")

All five roadmap features are implemented, tested, and documented, plus the tutorial notebook. `mmap_portability.md` states are all `done`. Nothing is committed (say the word and I'll split it per Tidy First).

**What landed**

- **F1 tier resolver** - `driver/shm.cpp` rewritten: first-fit over `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` pin > `/dev/shm` > `~/.cache/andes-sim` (XDG-aware, created on demand), fit = size + 256 MiB. The status line names the tier and, on fallback, the reason. USER_GUIDE 2.5 rewritten (the old "no fallback chain" promise became "never silently").
- **F5 `--mem-size`** - one flag, three semantics: `fast` forwards a plain `-m` only when given (QEMU as-is otherwise; QEMU does its own validation), `hybrid` sizes the shared mmap and rejects `>2G` *before* allocating the file, `cycle` validates and says "nothing to size". `--mmap-size` stays as a hidden alias; `run -h` documents only the new spelling.
- **F2 proof** - a fixture writes a pattern at `0x7FFFF000` (2 GiB - 4 KiB) on QEMU and the ROI reads it back on vsim with `--mem-size 2G`. Passed on the first run, so the 2 GiB assumption holds across the whole stack.
- **F3 doctor** - new `mmap tiers:` section after Summary (so byte-parity with the Python golden is untouched), one row per tier with free space, plus WSL2 warnings (`.wslconfig memory=` hint, `/mnt/` drvfs warning) from a pure, unit-tested helper.

"I would like to set /dev/shm as a speedup alternative on linux and wsl. 1. need larger size 2. need to cross three OSs. propose the new solution" — proposal requested; via AskUserQuestion the PM decided: target size "Up to ~2 GiB", and "macOS is run-only, not build" (Mac users pull a prebuilt image; build stays on Linux CI).
   3. "the andes-sim should allow users to request the desired memory size." — added F5 (model-neutral flag) to the roadmap.
   4. "for QEMU-only fast mode, please don't set 128 MiB default. don't use shared mmap memory. use QEMU as-is" — fast mode: forward plain `-m` only when the flag is given; no injected default; never memory-backend-file; QEMU validates itself.
   5. "go ahead to finish all steps" — implement the whole mmap_portability.md roadmap (F1-F5).
   6. (mid-task) "then write a tutorial ipynb file to introduce this feature" — memory tutorial notebook.
   7. "commit this" — commit all outstanding work (this session AND the uncommitted prior gemm session), properly partitioned.
   
   Standing global rules: TDD hard gate (failing test visible before any non-test edit), Tidy First (never mix structural/behavioral in one commit; commit messages state which), simple English (ESL learner), ASCII only (no em dashes/smart quotes/ellipsis chars), answer on line 1/no preamble/no sycophancy, never speculate about unread code, read before edit, commit ONLY when asked, commit messages end with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>", JOBS=8 for run_e2e.sh on this 128-core host, complex-task roadmaps as task-named .md in repo root, project rule "Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed", zsh quirks: noclobber (use `>|`), `=word` expansion breaks bare `===` in echo.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Core design rule: hybrid handoff needs both legs (QEMU + vsim) on ONE Linux kernel; the mmap file on a filesystem local to that kernel. MAP_SHARED on any local file is page-cache coherent; tmpfs is only a speed tier.
   - Hard caps: QEMU AE350 DRAM window 0x0..0x80000000 (2 GiB; `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:1362` errors "Cannot model more than 2GB RAM" when ram_size > window); vsim standalone window RAM_BASE 0x0..RAM_END 0x8FFFFFFF (`verilator/src/platform/memory_map.h`); in hybrid mode vsim's ram_region = [shared_mem_base, base+size-1].
   - Tier resolver: first fit wins over HSIM_MMAP_DIR pin (single tier, no fallback) > /dev/shm > ~/.cache/andes-sim (XDG_CACHE_HOME-aware, created on demand); fit = size + 256 MiB margin (kMmapSafetyMargin); fallback never silent (status line carries reason); sparse file via mkstemp+truncate.
   - --mem-size per-model semantics: hybrid = mmap = QEMU backend = vsim window, early >2G rejection BEFORE allocating; fast = plain `-m <MiB>M` forwarded only when given (QEMU as-is; user's own `-- -m` wins because it comes later); cycle = validate + stderr "nothing to size" note. --mmap-size is a hidden alias (same Cli::mem_size field).
   - QEMU `-m` takes whole MiB (plain number = MiB, M/G suffixes) — qemu_m_args converts bytes→MiB, rejects non-whole-MiB.
   - Doctor parity constraint: pre-Summary sections must byte-match the frozen `hsim.py` golden; C++-only additions go AFTER Summary (`engines:` pattern, now also `mmap tiers:`).
   - WSL2: /dev/shm capped by WSL VM memory (.wslconfig memory=); /mnt/ drvfs is slow and MAP_SHARED-incoherent; detect via "microsoft" in /proc/version.
   - macOS run-only: Darwin wrapper re-exec into Linux runtime image via podman/docker; container /dev/shm (--shm-size, default 3g) is tier 1; HSIM_MMAP_DIR never forwarded; cwd bind-mounted at same path; image bakes a fully built repo at /opt/hybrid_sim (Dockerfile.runtime, CI-built, NOT validated locally; registry TBD).
   - Artifact env overrides exist: VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR.
   - vplat fixtures: printf inside ROI is allowed (MMIO UART); vplat_hello.elf carries NO ROI markers (hybrid marker tests need rt_c_hello.elf or a marker-built fixture with `-I build/runtime/include` + `<andes_sim/roi.h>`).

# mmap_portability -- larger shared mmap + Linux/WSL2/macOS support

Design rule: both legs (QEMU + vsim) must share ONE Linux kernel, and the
mmap file must live on a filesystem local to that kernel. `MAP_SHARED` on a
regular local file is coherent through the page cache; tmpfs (`/dev/shm`) is
only a speed tier, never a correctness requirement.

Decisions (PM, 2026-06-11):
- Target size: up to ~2 GiB. This matches the hard cap already in the stack:
  QEMU's AE350 DRAM window is 0x0..0x80000000 (2 GiB, machine errors above);
  vsim models 0x0..0x8FFFFFFF. Resolver-only change; F2 proves it end to end.
- macOS is run-only: Mac users pull a prebuilt Linux image with all artifacts
  and run simulations inside the podman machine VM. Building stays on Linux.
- Users request memory with one model-neutral flag (F5). model=fast stays
  "QEMU as-is": andes-sim never injects a memory default and never touches
  the mmap machinery there; the flag only forwards `-m` when given.

## F1: tiered backing-store resolver
State: done
Description: Replace the fixed `/dev/shm` default with a first-fit candidate
list (fit = size + 256 MiB free):
  Tier 0  HSIM_MMAP_DIR        explicit pin; hard error if it does not fit
  Tier 1  /dev/shm             skipped if absent or too small
  Tier 2  ~/.cache/andes-sim   disk-backed; ceiling becomes disk free space
Status line names the tier and the reason, e.g.
`[hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at ~/.cache/andes-sim (disk-backed; /dev/shm too small: 1.2 GiB free)`.
Note: tier 2 must be a real-disk dir, not /tmp (often tmpfs itself).
Tidy First: structural commit first (inject the free-space probe + candidate
list into select_mmap_dir so it is unit-testable), then the behavioral commit
(the fallback itself).
Doc contract change: USER_GUIDE 2.5 currently promises "no fallback chain --

## Report: Hybrid RISC-V Co-Simulator Verification & Orchestration

### 1. E2E Test Verification Strategy (Post-QEMU2 Removal)

**Answer:** Tests verify correctness through **cycle-count delta extraction** from `hybrid_state_v1` files, not through stdout or golden state comparison.

**Evidence:**
- **tests/e2e.sh lines 109–154**: Harness drains QEMU1 state → `STATE_QEMU`, runs vsim with `--resume-from-qemu` and `--handoff-out STATE_VSIM`, verifies both exit code 200
- **tests/e2e.sh lines 161–190**: Extracts `mcycle` and `minstret` at fixed offsets (624 and 632 bytes, locked by `state_abi_check.h`) from both state files; computes kernel cycles as `vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle`; prints result with optional monotonicity check
- **tests/e2e.sh lines 85–97**: No stdout validation; only cycle delta and optional monotonicity (`CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1`) are checked
- **tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.c lines 1–10**: Comment acknowledges removal of "old phase-3 QEMU2 print + independent re-verify"; fixture now "validates that the GEMM kernel runs and drains" (via cycle count alone)
- **tests/fixtures/rt_shared_mem.S lines 1–18**: Comment references "Phase C (QEMU2)" but this code is never executed (no QEMU2 leg); fixture validates via internal exit codes (50/51 on failure) embedded in the code, not checked externally by the harness

### 2. Behavior After StateDrain Completes at Exit Trigger

**Answer:** Simulation **terminates immediately** with exit code 200 (`kExitHandoffToQemu`). The drain sweep clobbers `vtype`, `vl`, `vstart`, and scratch GPRs `x5`/`x6`/`x7`.

**Evidence:**
- **verilator/src/simulator.hpp line 441**: In `step_cycles()`, `check_hybrid_handoff()` returns when handoff is detected
- **verilator/src/simulator.hpp lines 520–524**: State is written to file, then `return hybrid::kExitHandoffToQemu` (exit code 200); no further execution
- **verilator/src/hybrid/exit_codes.hpp line 7**: `kExitHandoffToQemu = 200`
- **verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp lines 96–104**: VSE8.V sweep (line 103-104 `pb_v_data_sweep(..., load=false)`) runs **LAST** and "clobbers vtype/vl/vstart, x5/x6/x7"; comment explicitly notes these are dumped AFTER all architectural reads so sweep's overwrites cannot corrupt drained values
- **No resume path**: After `StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` returns, the hart remains halted; no code un-halts it

### 3. QEMU Plugin Support for EXIT Marker Drains

**Answer:** The plugin **recognizes both ENTRY (0x5A0) and EXIT (0x5A1) markers** but **only drains on ENTRY**. The EXIT marker is parsed but ignored in the drain callback.

**Evidence:**
- **qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c lines 520–537**: Marker-mode detects both via `hybrid_match_handoff_insn()` (line 530) and creates `HandoffSite` with `kind` field
- **qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c lines 361–366**: `on_handoff()` callback registered for all matched markers; line 364: `if (site->kind != HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER) return;` – **immediately returns for EXIT markers** without draining
- **qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c lines 345–354**: `handoff_drain()` is only called for ENTER; exit code 200 returned there
- **qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c lines 547–607**: Plugin arg parsing supports:
  - `outfile=PATH` (required)
  - `enter_pc=0x...` (PC-mode, bypasses markers)
  - `icount=N` (instruction count; boundary insn is real code, not marker)
  - `drain_at_exit=1` (drains on natural program exit via atexit handler, not marker)
  - No `exit_pc=...` or marker-specific exit argument
- **Implication**: A pure-QEMU run with the plugin could generate a snapshot at ROI END only via `drain_at_exit=1` after the entire program finishes, not at the EXIT marker itself

### 4. Differential/Parity Tests Across Models

**Answer:** **No existing cross-model differential tests found.** Only driver-level parity (Python golden vs. C++ driver CLI) exists.

**Evidence:**
- **tests/andes_sim/parity.sh lines 1–79**: "Differential parity harness" compares golden `hsim.py` vs. C++ `build/andes-sim` on **driver CLI only** (lines 71–76): `list fixtures`, `doctor`, `build --dry-run` args; no simulation result comparison
- **scripts/run_e2e.sh lines 1–100**: Hybrid e2e harness runs two-phase tests only; `MODE` env controls `TRIGGER_MODE` (marker|pc) iteration, not cross-model comparison
- **No grep matches** for "compare fast cycle", "compare hybrid fast", or state-file diffing across models in tests/ or scripts/
- **Implication**: Correctness proof relies on: (1) QEMU1 cycle count reproducibility, (2) shared mmap memory survival, (3) StateDrain → ResumeDriver round-trip validation (via unit tests in `verilator/tests/hybrid/`), but **not** on oracle runs from pure-QEMU or pure-vsim as baseline

This is *stronger* than the handback flow: post-ROI verification code only checked whatever the author thought to assert (usually one output buffer). 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
13	#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
14	#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
15	#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
16	#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
17	#                   relies on this; ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly.
18	#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
19	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
20	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
21	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
22	#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
23	#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
24	#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
25	#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
26	#                              pair from the drained state file.
27	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
28	
29	set -euo pipefail
30	
31	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
32	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
33	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
34	
35	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
36	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
37	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
38	
39	hybrid_resolve_paths
40	
41	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
42	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
43	
44	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
45	  marker) ;;
46	  pc)
47	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
48	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
49	      exit 77
50	    fi
51	    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
52	    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
53	    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
54	    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
55	    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
#                              pair from the drained state file.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13):
  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@3392, minstret_at_measure_start@3400.
  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 3392 "$STATE_VSIM")
    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 3400 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- the C++ analog of runner.run_session, minus
2	// the dropped QEMU2 handback. run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
21	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
22	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
23	struct RuntimeCtx {
24	  std::string mmap_path;
25	  long long mem_size = 0;
26	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
27	  std::string plugin_path;
28	};
29	
30	// hw-config sync: the QEMU fast leg models the hardware the accurate-leg
31	// engine measures, so its -cpu vlen follows that engine's descriptor. 512 is
32	// the fallback for engines that report none. One definition, used by both the
33	// plan executor ({vlen} fill) and the hybrid banner.
34	inline long synced_vlen(long engine_vlen) {
35	  return engine_vlen > 0 ? engine_vlen : 512;
36	}
37	
38	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
39	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
40	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
41	// appended to its argv. marker contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
42	// themselves).
43	struct LegTriggerArgs {
44	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
45	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
46	};
47	
48	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. marker -> empty. pc -> qemu
49	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. icount -> qemu
50	// `,icount=<qemu_icount>` / vsim `--hybrid-icount <vsim_icount>`. Roles other
51	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
52	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
53	//
54	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
55	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
56	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
57	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
58	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
59	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
60	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
61	                                std::string& err);
62	
63	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
64	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
65	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
66	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
67	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
68	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
69	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
70	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
71	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
72	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
73	
74	struct PlanOptions {
75	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
76	  int expect_rc = 200;        // drain success code (kExitHandoffToQemu)
77	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
78	};
79	
80	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
81	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
82	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
83	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
84	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
85	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
86	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
87	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
88	
89	}  // namespace andes_sim
90	
91	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PC-trigger contract: the drained resume PC equals the --pc-start boundary.
#
# The drain callback fires BEFORE the trigger insn executes, so the captured
# state is pre-execution. A marker is an architectural NOP and may be skipped
# (resume at vaddr+size), but a pc boundary is real user code: if the plugin
# reports vaddr+size, the boundary insn executes on NEITHER leg (e.g. a
# skipped vsetivli leaves vtype.vill set and the vsim window faults on the
# first vector op). The plugin must report the boundary's own vaddr so the
# insn runs inside the measured window.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_ELF     any fixture with a `main` symbol (default: vplat_hello.elf)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-vplat_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
command -v "${NM:-nm}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || NM=nm
ENTER_HEX=$("$NM" "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$3 == "main" { print $1; exit }')
[ -n "$ENTER_HEX" ] || { echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: no main in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
ENTER=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$ENTER_HEX")

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-pcresume-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,enter_pc=$ENTER" \
  </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
  tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$ENTER)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: resume PC != pc-start boundary $ENTER:"
  grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
echo "[pc_trigger_resume_pc] PASS: drain resumes at the boundary insn ($ENTER)"

1	// Translation-time capture of a handoff trigger insn. The QEMU TCG plugin
2	// allocates one of these per matched insn during vcpu_tb_trans and forwards
3	// the pointer as exec-callback userdata. compute_handoff_pc(site) returns
4	// the PC at which vsim should resume (i.e. the architectural PC immediately
5	// after the trigger insn retires).
6	//
7	// This indirection exists because qemu_plugin_read_register("pc") inside an
8	// exec callback returns a stale PC when V instructions retire just before
9	// the trigger -- TCG defers PC writes for performance and the gdbstub
10	// readback observes the lag. vaddr/size are deterministic at translate time
11	// (qemu_plugin_insn_vaddr/size), so vaddr+size is a lag-free post-trigger
12	// PC. Same predicate, two consumers: the plugin (C) and a doctest unit
13	// test (C++).
14	//
15	// Lifetime: sites are heap-allocated in vcpu_tb_trans and never freed --
16	// the plugin has no "TB invalidated" hook and trigger sites are bounded by
17	// the fixture's text (typically 1-2 marker insns).
18	
19	#ifndef HYBRID_HANDOFF_SITE_H
20	#define HYBRID_HANDOFF_SITE_H
21	
22	#include "hybrid/insn_match.h"
23	
24	#include <stdint.h>
25	
26	#ifdef __cplusplus
27	extern "C" {
28	#endif
29	
30	typedef struct HandoffSite
31	{
32	  hybrid_handoff_kind kind;
33	  uint64_t            vaddr;
34	  uint32_t            size;
35	} HandoffSite;
36	
37	static inline uint64_t compute_handoff_pc(const HandoffSite* site)
38	{
39	  return site->vaddr + (uint64_t) site->size;
40	}
41	
42	#ifdef __cplusplus
43	}  // extern "C"
44	#endif
45	
46	#endif  // HYBRID_HANDOFF_SITE_H
47

1	// Pattern recogniser for the magic handoff marker convention. The same
2	// predicate runs in two places: the QEMU TCG plugin (C) and the vsim PC
3	// pre-scan (C++).
4	//
5	// The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions: SLTI with rd=x0 discards its
6	// result, so it is an architectural NOP on every conforming core. Marker
7	// binaries therefore run unmodified on real silicon and on every engine
8	// (fast/cycle/hybrid) -- unlike the retired `csrwi 0x7C0` markers, where
9	// CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on Andes cores and the exit marker enabled ILM at
10	// base 0, killing standalone runs. The 12-bit immediate carries the
11	// marker kind; rs1 is pinned to x0 so each marker is one exact 32-bit
12	// word. SLTI has no compressed form, so markers are always 4 bytes.
13	
14	#ifndef HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
15	#define HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
16	
17	#include <stdbool.h>
18	#include <stdint.h>
19	
20	#ifdef __cplusplus
21	extern "C" {
22	#endif
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_NONE  = 0,
27	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER = 1,  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A0
28	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT  = 2,  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A1
29	} hybrid_handoff_kind;
30	
31	// slti x0, x0, imm: OP-IMM (0x13), funct3=010, rd=rs1=x0, imm[31:20].
32	#define HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN 0x5A002013u
33	#define HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN  0x5A102013u
34	
35	// Returns true when `insn` is one of the two marker HINTs. On match,
36	// *out_kind is set to ENTER or EXIT.
37	static inline bool hybrid_match_handoff_insn(uint32_t insn,
38	                                             hybrid_handoff_kind* out_kind)
39	{
40	  if (insn == HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN) {
41	    *out_kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER;
42	    return true;
43	  }
44	  if (insn == HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN) {
45	    *out_kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT;
46	    return true;
47	  }
48	  return false;
49	}
50	
51	#ifdef __cplusplus
52	}  // extern "C"
53	#endif
54	
55	#endif  // HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
56

1	// andes-sim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andes-sim <cmd> [--model M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
9	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
10	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
11	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
12	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
13	#define ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
14	
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	struct Cli {
21	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
22	  std::string model;                      // --model fast|cycle|hybrid
23	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
24	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc|icount|simpoint
25	  std::string what;                       // --what <target> (build)
26	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
27	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the icounts/sizes stay strings here and
28	  // are parsed where they are used.
29	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
30	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
31	  std::string qemu_icount;                // --qemu-icount (trigger icount)
32	  std::string vsim_icount;                // --vsim-icount (trigger icount)
33	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
34	  std::string vsim_warmup_icount;         // --vsim-warmup-icount (vsim leg)
35	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
36	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
37	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
38	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
39	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
40	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
41	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
42	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
43	};
44	
45	// Parse argv[1..] (program name skipped). The vector overload is the testable
46	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().

48	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
49	
50	}  // namespace andes_sim
51	
52	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP

# verify_oracle -- QEMU-oracle differential verification (opt-in, default OFF)

Problem: with the QEMU2 handback removed, the post-ROI verification code in a
workload never runs, and the e2e suite only checks that a cycle figure exists.
Nothing proves the vsim leg executed the ROI *correctly*.

Solution (PM decision, 2026-06-12): differential check against QEMU as the
oracle. The same ELF runs twice:
  run A (oracle):  pure QEMU, plugin drains hybrid_state_v1 at the ROI exit
                   boundary (new plugin mode).
  run B (hybrid):  the normal QEMU1 -> vsim run; vsim already drains
                   hybrid_state_v1 at the same boundary.
The pre-ROI path is QEMU in both runs, so the ROI inputs are identical; any
architectural divergence inside the ROI (RTL bug, resume bug, drain bug) shows
up as a field mismatch. Verification is OPT-IN and default OFF everywhere:
`--verify` on `andes-sim run`, `VERIFY=1` on the e2e harness.

Compare policy (fixed, derived from what vsim's drain freshly reads --
state_drain.hpp drain_with_passthrough):
  strict:  pc, gpr[0..31]; fpr[0..31] (when FLAG_FP); vstart/vtype/vl/

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
#
# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.

# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
resolve_pc() {
  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
  case "$boundary" in
    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
  esac
}

# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (both REQUIRED), resolves
#   each against <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare
#   hex). Returns 1 and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if
#   either is unset or does not resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message.
roi_resolve_pair() {
  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
  local start="${ROI_START:-}"
  local end="${ROI_END:-}"
  if [ -z "$start" ] || [ -z "$end" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set (0x address or symbol name)"
    return 1
  fi
  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

# roi_markers_from_disasm <objdump_disasm>
#   Derives the two pc-mode switch PCs from the ROI marker HINTs a fixture
#   embeds, scanning `objdump -d` text:
#     ENTER = the entry marker     `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`  (encoding 5a002013)
#     EXIT  = the LAST exit marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`  (encoding 5a102013)
#   Both are the marker PCs themselves: the plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
#   (--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the trigger
#   (compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so feeding the marker PC reproduces
#   marker mode's switch points exactly -- no offset arithmetic here. EXIT
#   keeps the LAST marker so a fixture that jumps over poison exit-marker
#   padding (rt_pc_jump) resolves to the real, reachable exit, not the first
#   dead one. The raw-bytes match is mnemonic-independent, so no objdump
#   decode table is needed.
#   Prints "ENTER EXIT" as bare hex; returns 1 (prints nothing) if either
#   marker is absent. This lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no
#   per-fixture config; ./andes-sim run still passes explicit boundaries.
roi_markers_from_disasm() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
    $2 == "5a002013" && enter == "" { e = $1; sub(/:$/, "", e); enter = e }
    $2 == "5a102013"                { x = $1; sub(/:$/, "", x); exit_pc = x }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Oracle exit-drain contract (verify_oracle F1): a pure-QEMU run drains
# hybrid_state_v1 at the ROI EXIT boundary, producing the reference state the
# differential verifier compares against the vsim drain.
#
# Semantics: arm on the exit boundary's exec callback, drain on the NEXT exec
# callback. That callback fires before its own insn executes, so the captured
# state is "after the boundary insn retired" -- exactly what vsim's exit drain
# records (DPC = next insn to execute) -- and the reported pc is the next
# insn's vaddr, correct even for a branching boundary insn.
#
# Cases:
#   1. exit_marker=1  -- arm on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`; pc must be marker+4
#                        (NOT enter-marker+4: the ENTER marker must not drain).
#   2. exit_pc=0x...  -- arm on the boundary vaddr; same expectation when the
#                        boundary is the (fall-through) exit marker.
#   3. exit_marker=1,icount=N -- install error: oracle mode is exclusive with
#                        the other trigger modes.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   FIXTURE      a marker-carrying fixture (default: rt_c_hello)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[oracle_exit_drain]: no objdump"; exit 77; }

MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
  || { echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
EXIT_PC="0x${MARKERS##* }"
# The exit marker is a 4-byte NOP that falls through, so the first insn
# executed after it retires sits at marker+4.

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# state-diff dev command (verify_oracle F2): compares two drained
# hybrid_state_v1 files under the oracle policy. Uses the plugin's oracle
# exit-drain (F1) to produce a real state file, then checks:
#   1. a file vs itself        -> PASS, rc 0
#   2. vs a tampered GPR byte  -> FAIL, rc 1, mismatch line names the reg
#   3. vs a tampered mcycle    -> PASS (counters are masked)
#   4. usage / unreadable file -> rc 2
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

REF=$(mktemp)
GOT=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$REF" "$GOT"' EXIT

# A real drained state from a pure-QEMU oracle run.
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$REF,exit_marker=1" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e
[ "$RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "oracle drain run failed (rc=$RC)"
[ -s "$REF" ] || fail "oracle drain produced no state file"

# 1. identical files PASS.
cp "$REF" "$GOT"
expect 0 '\[state-diff\] PASS' "$BIN" state-diff "$REF" "$GOT"
ok "identical states PASS"

# 2. flip one byte of x5 (gpr[5] @ offset 32 + 5*8 = 72) -> named mismatch.
B=$(od -A n -j 72 -N 1 -t u1 "$REF" | tr -d ' ')
printf "\\$(printf '%03o' $(( (B + 1) % 256 )))" \
  | dd of="$GOT" bs=1 seek=72 conv=notrunc status=none
expect 1 '\[state-diff\] x5: ref=' "$BIN" state-diff "$REF" "$GOT"
expect 1 '\[state-diff\] FAIL: 1 mismatch' "$BIN" state-diff "$REF" "$GOT"
ok "tampered x5 caught and named"

# 3. flip a byte of mcycle (@624) -> still PASS (counters masked).
cp "$REF" "$GOT"
B=$(od -A n -j 624 -N 1 -t u1 "$REF" | tr -d ' ')
printf "\\$(printf '%03o' $(( (B + 1) % 256 )))" \
  | dd of="$GOT" bs=1 seek=624 conv=notrunc status=none
expect 0 '\[state-diff\] PASS' "$BIN" state-diff "$REF" "$GOT"
ok "mcycle difference masked"

# 4. usage errors.
expect 2 'usage: andes-sim state-diff' "$BIN" state-diff "$REF"
expect 2 'cannot open' "$BIN" state-diff "$REF" /nonexistent/state.bin
ok "usage and unreadable-file errors exit 2"

ok "state-diff dev command"

# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.

TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
fi

hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$TOP_ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# e2e harness VERIFY=1 (verify_oracle F3): opt-in differential verification.
#   1. VERIFY=1, marker mode -> oracle leg runs, "[FIXTURE verify] PASS".
#   2. VERIFY=1, pc mode     -> same through the exit_pc oracle path.
#   3. default (VERIFY unset) -> no verify leg, no verify output.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

run_e2e() {  # $1 = trigger mode, extra env via leading VAR=... in caller
  OUT=$(cd "$ROOT" && FIXTURE="$FIXTURE" TRIGGER_MODE="$1" VERIFY="${2-}" \
        bash tests/e2e.sh 2>&1)
  RC=$?
}

# 1. marker mode, VERIFY=1.
run_e2e marker 1
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker VERIFY=1 run failed (rc=$RC): $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q "\[$FIXTURE verify\] PASS" \
  || fail "marker VERIFY=1: no verify PASS line: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q "\[state-diff\] PASS" \
  || fail "marker VERIFY=1: no state-diff PASS detail: $OUT"
ok "marker mode: oracle verify PASS"

# 2. pc mode, VERIFY=1.
run_e2e pc 1
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc VERIFY=1 run failed (rc=$RC): $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q "\[$FIXTURE verify\] PASS" \
  || fail "pc VERIFY=1: no verify PASS line: $OUT"
ok "pc mode: oracle verify PASS"

# 3. default off: no verify leg, no verify output.
run_e2e marker ""
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "default run failed (rc=$RC): $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q "verify" \
  && fail "default run leaked verify output: $OUT"
ok "default: verification stays off"

ok "e2e VERIFY=1 differential verification"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#

# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
#                              pair from the drained state file.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi

    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi

    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()

  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13):
  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@3392, minstret_at_measure_start@3400.
  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 3392 "$STATE_VSIM")
    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 3400 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   VERIFY=1        opt-in differential verification (default off): re-run
#                   the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at the ROI
#                   exit boundary (the oracle), then `andes-sim state-diff`
#                   the oracle state against the vsim drain. Any divergence
#                   in what vsim freshly drains (pc/GPRs/FPRs/V) fails the
#                   test; counters and passthrough CSRs are excluded.
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
#                              pair from the drained state file.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
STATE_ORACLE=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$STATE_ORACLE" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13):
  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@3392, minstret_at_measure_start@3400.
  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 3392 "$STATE_VSIM")
    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 3400 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Oracle exit-drain contract (verify_oracle F1): a pure-QEMU run drains
# hybrid_state_v1 at the ROI EXIT boundary, producing the reference state the
# differential verifier compares against the vsim drain.
#
# Semantics: arm on the exit boundary's exec callback, drain on the NEXT exec
# callback. That callback fires before its own insn executes, so the captured
# state is "after the boundary insn retired" -- exactly what vsim's exit drain
# records (DPC = next insn to execute) -- and the reported pc is the next
# insn's vaddr, correct even for a branching boundary insn.
#
# Cases:
#   1. exit_marker=1  -- arm on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`; pc must be marker+4
#                        (NOT enter-marker+4: the ENTER marker must not drain).
#   2. exit_pc=0x...  -- arm on the boundary vaddr; same expectation when the
#                        boundary is the (fall-through) exit marker.
#   3. exit_marker=1,icount=N -- install error: oracle mode is exclusive with
#                        the other trigger modes.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   FIXTURE      a marker-carrying fixture (default: rt_c_hello)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[oracle_exit_drain]: no objdump"; exit 77; }

MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
  || { echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
EXIT_PC="0x${MARKERS##* }"
# The exit marker is a 4-byte NOP that falls through, so the first insn
# executed after it retires sits at marker+4.
WANT_PC=$(printf '0x%x' $((EXIT_PC + 4)))

STATE=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$STATE" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT

run_qemu() {  # $1 = plugin arg suffix
  set +e
  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -machine andes_ae350 \
    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE,$1" \
    </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
  RC=$?
  set -e
}

check_drain() {  # $1 = case label
  if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: $1: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
    tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ ! -s "$STATE" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: $1: no state file written"
    exit 1
  fi
  if ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$WANT_PC)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
    echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: $1: drain pc != exit-marker+4 ($WANT_PC):"
    grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
    exit 1
  fi
}

# Case 1: marker mode.
run_qemu "exit_marker=1"
check_drain "exit_marker"

# Case 2: pc mode, boundary = the exit marker's own vaddr.
: > "$STATE"
run_qemu "exit_pc=$EXIT_PC"
check_drain "exit_pc"

# Case 3: oracle mode is exclusive with the other trigger modes.
run_qemu "exit_marker=1,icount=100"
if [ "$RC" -eq 200 ] || ! grep -qi "exclusive" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
  echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: exit_marker+icount should fail install (got rc=$RC):"
  tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[oracle_exit_drain] PASS: oracle drains after the ROI exit boundary (pc=$WANT_PC)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Oracle exit-drain contract (verify_oracle F1): a pure-QEMU run drains
# hybrid_state_v1 at the ROI EXIT boundary, producing the reference state the
# differential verifier compares against the vsim drain.
#
# Semantics: arm on the exit boundary's exec callback, drain on the NEXT exec
# callback. That callback fires before its own insn executes, so the captured
# state is "after the boundary insn retired" -- exactly what vsim's exit drain
# records (DPC = next insn to execute) -- and the reported pc is the next
# insn's vaddr, correct even for a branching boundary insn.
#
# Cases:
#   1. exit_marker=1  -- arm on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`; pc must be marker+4
#                        (NOT enter-marker+4: the ENTER marker must not drain).
#   2. exit_pc=0x...  -- arm on the boundary vaddr; same expectation when the
#                        boundary is the (fall-through) exit marker.
#   3. drain_pc=0x... -- sample at a later, caller-chosen pc instead of the
#                        very next insn. The differential harness passes
#                        vsim's actual halt pc here: vsim's DMI halt lands a
#                        variable 0-3 insns past the trigger, and both sides
#                        must sample the SAME architectural point.
#   4. exit_marker=1,icount=N -- install error: oracle mode is exclusive with
#                        the other trigger modes; drain_pc requires oracle
#                        mode.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   FIXTURE      a marker-carrying fixture (default: rt_c_hello)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[oracle_exit_drain]: no objdump"; exit 77; }

MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
  || { echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }

# executed after it retires sits at marker+4.

STATE=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$STATE" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT

run_qemu() {  # $1 = plugin arg suffix
  set +e
  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -machine andes_ae350 \
    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE,$1" \

}

check_drain() {  # $1 = case label

    grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
