1	// andes-sim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andes-sim <cmd> [--model M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
9	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
10	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
11	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
12	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
13	#define ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
14	
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	struct Cli {
21	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
22	  std::string model;                      // --model fast|cycle|hybrid
23	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
24	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc|icount|simpoint
25	  std::string what;                       // --what <target> (build)
26	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
27	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the icounts/sizes stay strings here and
28	  // are parsed where they are used.
29	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
30	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
31	  std::string qemu_icount;                // --qemu-icount (trigger icount)
32	  std::string vsim_icount;                // --vsim-icount (trigger icount)
33	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
34	  std::string vsim_warmup_icount;         // --vsim-warmup-icount (vsim leg)
35	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
36	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
37	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
38	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
39	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
40	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
41	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --model hybrid)
42	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
43	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
44	};
45	
46	// Parse argv[1..] (program name skipped). The vector overload is the testable
47	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().
48	Cli parse_cli(const std::vector<std::string>& args);
49	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
50	
51	}  // namespace andes_sim
52	
53	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
54

1	// The phase-plan grammar driven by run_plan (F6) -- the C++ analog of
2	// orchestrator/plan.py's Session/Step model, minus the dropped QEMU2 step.
3	//
4	// A Plan is a list of Steps; each Step names an engine (by id, resolved against
5	// the F2 registry), the role to invoke it in (its `invoke` template key, e.g.
6	// "fast-leg" / "accurate-leg"), and a Trigger. run_plan spawns each leg in
7	// order, threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward, and returns each
8	// leg's mcycle/minstret. Under the no-QEMU2-handback design every F6 step
9	// drains, so the hybrid cycle figure is the vsim-leg mcycle minus the qemu-leg
10	// mcycle.
11	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_PLAN_HPP
12	#define ANDES_SIM_PLAN_HPP
13	
14	#include <map>
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	// The ROI delimiter for a step. `kind` is marker|pc|icount|simpoint; `params`
23	// carries kind-specific values (e.g. icount=N, enter_pc, exit_pc) that F9 maps
24	// onto trigger args. F6 only exercises the default marker case (no params).
25	struct Trigger {
26	  std::string kind;
27	  std::map<std::string, std::string> params;
28	};
29	
30	// One leg of a plan: which engine, which invoke role, under which trigger.
31	// `extra_args` are verbatim tokens appended after the filled template and the
32	// trigger args -- the seam for user-forwarded per-leg flags (e.g. the vsim
33	// leg's --vsim-warmup-icount / --kanata), which are orthogonal to the trigger.
34	struct Step {
35	  std::string engine_id;  // "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"
36	  std::string role;       // invoke-template key: "fast-leg" | "accurate-leg"
37	  Trigger trigger;
38	  std::vector<std::string> extra_args{};  // default-init: keeps 3-field Step{} literals warning-free
39	};
40	
41	// A whole hybrid run. Every step loads `elf`; the shared mmap (`mem_size`
42	// bytes, at `mmap_path` or allocated by run_plan when empty) survives across
43	// every leg so memory threads through.
44	struct Plan {
45	  std::string elf;          // path to the ELF every leg launches
46	  long long mem_size = 0;   // shared-mmap size in bytes
47	  std::string mmap_path;    // "" => run_plan allocates one (F5) and owns it
48	  std::vector<Step> steps;
49	};
50	
51	// What one drain step measured (read back from its state file), plus the
52	// leg's captured stdout -- the guest program's own output (UART/semihosting)
53	// rides the engine's stdout and must flow through to the user. `st` is the
54	// full drained record (verify_oracle F4: run --verify diffs the vsim drain
55	// against the oracle leg's in-process, after run_plan removed the files).
56	struct PhaseResult {
57	  unsigned long long mcycle = 0;
58	  unsigned long long minstret = 0;
59	  std::string out;
60	  hybrid_state_v1 st{};
61	};
62	
63	// Aggregate outcome. `error` empty => every step matched its expected exit and
64	// drained a valid state file; `phases` then holds one entry per step in order.
65	struct PlanResult {
66	  std::string error;
67	  std::vector<PhaseResult> phases;
68	  bool ok() const { return error.empty(); }
69	};
70	
71	}  // namespace andes_sim
72	
73	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_PLAN_HPP

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the andes-sim driver: driver/ -> build/andes-sim.
#
# Standalone C++20 target (no Verilator, SystemC, or QEMU). Depends only on
# the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header under include/. This is the
# bootstrap consumed by setup.sh and `andes-sim build --what driver` (wired in
# F14). Out-of-tree build under build/driver; the binary is redirected to
# build/andes-sim via CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
BUILD="$ROOT/build/driver"

cmake -S "$ROOT/driver" -B "$BUILD" \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$ROOT/build" \
  >/dev/null

cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)"

echo "built: $ROOT/build/andes-sim"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run --cosim contract (cosim_roi F4): opt-in checkpoint co-simulation.
#   1. hybrid marker --cosim --cosim-interval 500 -> >=1 checkpoint,
#      "[cosim] PASS", rc 0 (rt_c_v_matmul: ~1.7k ROI retires -> 3 ckpts)
#   2. hybrid pc --cosim                          -> same through cosim_pc
#   3. default (no --cosim)                       -> no cosim output
#   4. usage errors: model, trigger, interval, --verify exclusivity
#   5. dev-only help surface
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"

# 1. marker mode with a sub-ROI interval -> real checkpoints.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --cosim --cosim-interval 500 "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker --cosim rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[cosim\] PASS' || fail "marker: no [cosim] PASS: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '\[cosim\] PASS: [1-9][0-9]* checkpoint' \
  || fail "marker: expected at least one checkpoint: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' || fail "marker: cycle figure missing: $OUT"
ok "hybrid marker --cosim: checkpoints + final match the oracle"

# 2. pc mode (boundaries = the fixture's own marker PCs, like docs 4.2).
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
  || fail "no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"
OUT=$("$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --pc-start "0x${MARKERS%% *}" --pc-end "0x${MARKERS##* }" \
      --cosim --cosim-interval 500 "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc --cosim rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[cosim\] PASS' || fail "pc: no [cosim] PASS: $OUT"
ok "hybrid pc --cosim: checkpoints + final match the oracle"

# 3. default off: no cosim leg, no cosim output.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "default hybrid rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qi 'cosim' && fail "default run leaked cosim output: $OUT"
ok "default: co-simulation stays off"

# 4. usage errors.
expect 2 'cosim requires --model hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --model fast --cosim "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'cosim requires --model hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --model cycle --cosim "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'cosim supports --trigger marker\|pc' \
  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --qemu-icount 1000 \
  --vsim-icount 100 --engine "$ENGINE" --cosim "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'cosim-interval requires --cosim' \
  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --cosim-interval 500 --engine "$ENGINE" "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'positive integer' \
  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --cosim --cosim-interval 0 --engine "$ENGINE" "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'exclusive' \
  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --cosim --verify --engine "$ENGINE" "$VSIM_ELF"
ok "--cosim usage errors (model/trigger/interval/--verify)"

# 5. dev-only help surface.
expect 0 ' --cosim ' env ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" run --help
OUT=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q -- '--cosim' && fail "release run --help leaks --cosim"
ok "--cosim help is dev-only"

ok "run --cosim checkpoint co-simulation"

`--verify` tells you THAT the vsim leg diverged; `--cosim` tells you
roughly WHERE. It is a developer tool (hidden from the release help, like
`state-diff`): every N retired instructions inside the ROI, the vsim leg
halts via DMI, drains a resumable checkpoint to `<state>.ckpt<k>`, and
continues. The driver then re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin
draining at the SAME retire counts, and diffs checkpoint k against
checkpoint k (same compare policy as `state-diff`):

```sh
ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 ./andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker \
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --cosim --cosim-interval 500 my.elf
# ...
# [cosim] PASS: 3 checkpoint(s) + final state match the QEMU oracle (interval 500, 1692 ROI retires)
```

On a divergence, the first mismatching checkpoint brackets the bug:

```
[state-diff] x12: ref=0x2a got=0x2b
[cosim] FAIL: divergence in window 2 (retires 500..1000 after entry)
```

Re-run with a smaller `--cosim-interval` to shrink the window.

Alignment is by retire count, not pc: vsim restores `minstret` from the
entry state, so `checkpoint.minstret - entry.minstret` is the exact number
of post-entry retires (vsim's DMI halt overshoots a few instructions; the
overshoot is simply part of the measured delta, and the oracle counts to
the same number). In pc-trigger mode the boundary instruction itself
retires inside the window and is counted as retire #1 on both sides.

Costs and limits:
- `--trigger marker|pc` only, `--model hybrid` only, exclusive with
  `--verify` (the final-state check is included).
- Each checkpoint costs a DMI halt + drain + resume on the vsim leg, so
  `window_cycles` under `--cosim` includes that overhead -- treat the
  figure as approximate and re-measure without `--cosim`.
- Divergence is localized to an N-instruction window, not an exact
  instruction; intervals comparable to the halt overshoot (tens of
  instructions) are not meaningful.
- Memory is NOT compared -- only the architectural register state at each
  checkpoint (a memory bug surfaces indirectly, when a wrong value is
  loaded into a register).

---

ROOT = "/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim"

def md(text):
    return {"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {},
            "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

def code(text):
    return {"cell_type": "code", "execution_count": None, "metadata": {},
            "outputs": [], "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

nb = json.load(open(NB))
cells = nb["cells"]

# Sanity: insert right after 4d's code cell (index 30), before section 5.
assert "say_hello" in "".join(cells[30]["source"])
assert "## 5." in "".join(cells[31]["source"])

md_intro = md("""### 4e. Cross-check the run against a QEMU oracle (`--verify`)

There is no handback leg, so nothing after your ROI ever runs - what proves
the RTL executed the ROI *correctly*? `--verify` (default OFF) answers it
with a differential check: the same ELF re-runs on pure QEMU (the oracle),
the plugin drains the full architectural state at the ROI exit - sampled at
the exact pc where vsim halted - and the driver diffs the two drains field
by field:

- **compared**: pc, all 32 GPRs, the FPRs, the V CSRs and full vector
  registers;
- **excluded**: `mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count differently by
  design) and the passthrough M-CSRs/PMP (vsim copies those from the entry
  snapshot, so there is nothing fresh to compare).

Any divergence prints a `[state-diff] field: ref=... got=...` line per
mismatching field and the run exits non-zero. A clean run costs one extra
MHz-class QEMU pass - cheap next to the vsim leg.""")

run_cell = code("!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker "
                "--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify "
                "tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf")

md_after = md("""Same cycle figure as 4a, plus the two verification lines:
`[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match` is the field-by-field compare,
`[verify] PASS` the verdict. The oracle's stderr banner shows the sample
point (`pc=...` - vsim's actual halt pc).

For regression testing, the whole e2e suite takes the same check with
`VERIFY=1 JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Details (and the failure
anatomy) in `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.7.""")

roughly WHERE. It is a developer tool (hidden from the release help, like
`state-diff` - set `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1` to see it in `run --help`):

```

the vsim leg halts the hart over DMI, drains a full architectural
checkpoint, and resumes. The driver reads each checkpoint's
`minstret - entry.minstret` (the exact post-entry retire count), re-runs
the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at those same counts, and
diffs checkpoint against checkpoint with the `state-diff` policy. The two
runs never share memory: the oracle replays the same deterministic program
from boot on its own RAM, so the shared mmap needs no change.""")

---
name: cosim-roi
description: "Checkpoint co-sim shipped 2026-06-12: run --cosim (dev) drains vsim checkpoints every N retires, QEMU oracle drains at the same minstret deltas, state-diff per window; mmap stays Shared"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Checkpoint co-simulation (roadmap: cosim_roi.md in repo root, all F1-F4
done 2026-06-12). `run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc --cosim
[--cosim-interval N]` (dev tier, default N=10000): vsim drains a
RESUMABLE checkpoint every N retires (StateDrain::drain_checkpoint undoes
the V-sweep clobbers vtype/vl/vstart/x5-x7 before resumereq); the driver
re-runs the ELF on a pure-QEMU oracle (plugin cosim_marker/cosim_pc +
cosim_counts=minstret deltas) and diffs window by window.

Key design facts:
- Alignment is by minstret delta, not pc (loop-safe; halt slack absorbed).
  Empirically minstret is NOT contaminated by Program Buffer execution in
  debug mode (ckpt delta exactly 1000 on a V workload).
- mmap stays MAP_SHARED. Private COW is a trap (un-COW'd pages see the
  other process's writes); the oracle simply replays from boot on its own
  RAM. See [[vsim-halt-slack]] and [[hsim-cpp-rewrite]].
- pc-trigger mode: the boundary insn counts as retire #1 on both sides
  (the pc handoff resumes AT the boundary; marker is counted by neither).
- Known edge: a checkpoint whose halt slack crosses the EXIT marker loses
  the exit retire (the run loop is blocked inside the drain) -- tiny
  intervals on tiny ROIs can crash with cmderr=4. Documented limitation.

/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
 *
 * Phase rule:
 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
 *   to register/memory work only.
 *
 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
 */

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers: the HINT pair
 * `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (ENTER) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (EXIT). Match
 * insn_match.h. rd=x0 makes each marker an architectural NOP, so marked
 * binaries also run standalone on every engine.
 *
 * marker mode pattern-matches the HINT insns directly; the helpers do not
 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

/* A pure compiler memory barrier (emits no instructions): forces pending
 * memory writes to complete and bars reordering across it. enter_vsim /
 * exit_vsim already carry this clobber on their marker insn, so the markers
 * anchor a kernel's output stores; markerless builds (-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS)
 * call roi_anchor() to pin those stores instead. */
static inline void roi_anchor(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fixture ROI-content contract: a fixture whose phase-2 comment promises a
# kernel must actually carry that kernel BETWEEN the markers. The compiler
# may legally hoist an inlined kernel above enter_vsim() -- the markers'
# "memory" clobber does not cover statics whose address never escapes --
# which silently empties the ROI (rt_c_matmul shipped that way: markers
# back-to-back, window_cycles ~74 of pure drain overhead). Anchor rule
# (runtime/rt_c_helpers.h): kernels live in a noinline function called
# between the markers.
#
# Checks (static, objdump):
#   rt_c_matmul    span contains the GEMM: a kernel call (jal) or a mul
#   rt_c_v_matmul  span contains the kernel call (control: known-good)
#   rt_c_v_regs    span contains vector instructions (inline V kernel)
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[fixture_roi_content]: no objdump"; exit 77; }

FIXDIR="$SCRIPT_DIR"

# Instructions strictly between the ENTER and EXIT markers.
roi_body() {
  "$OBJDUMP" -d "$FIXDIR/$1.elf" \
    | awk '/5a002013/ { on = 1; next } /5a102013/ { exit } on'
}

check_roi() {  # $1 = fixture, $2 = required-content regex, $3 = description
  BODY=$(roi_body "$1")
  if [ -z "$BODY" ]; then
    fail "$1: ROI is EMPTY (markers back-to-back) -- kernel hoisted out?"
  fi
  if ! printf '%s\n' "$BODY" | grep -Eq "$2"; then
    echo "--- ROI body of $1 ---"
    printf '%s\n' "$BODY"
    fail "$1: ROI does not contain $3 (want /$2/)"
  fi
  ok "$1: ROI carries $3"
}

content.text:
Fixed and committed as `7022599`. The GEMM now provably runs inside the ROI: 4683 retires / ~45k cycles instead of 3 retires / 74 cycles of drain overhead.

## Root cause (two layers deep)

The obvious fix - `noinline` on the kernel like rt_c_v_matmul - was **not enough**. After adding it, GCC deleted the *call* entirely. The real cause: `A`/`B`/`C` were non-escaping `static` arrays and `C` was never read back, so

1. the markers' asm `"memory"` clobber did not cover them (GCC's clobber only orders accesses to *escaped* memory), letting the inlined kernel hoist above `enter_vsim()`, and
2. with `noinline`, IPA mod/ref still proved the kernel writes only dead memory and removed the call.

rt_c_v_matmul only survived because V intrinsics are opaque to that analysis.

## The fix

- `A`/`B`/`C` get external linkage (escaped, so the marker clobbers apply and the stores stay live) plus the `noinline` kernel call - the ROI is now exactly `jal matmul_kernel` between the markers.
- Sized down 16^3 to 8^3: with a real ROI, 16^3 costs ~322k vsim cycles (~56s wall), brushing the 60s/90s harness timeouts. 8^3 gives a real ROI at ~45k cycles, ~24s.
- New TDD guard, `tests/fixtures/test_fixture_roi_content.sh` (written failing first): statically asserts the marker span carries the promised kernel for rt_c_matmul, rt_c_v_matmul and rt_c_v_regs - so a future compiler upgrade re-hoisting a kernel fails loudly.

## Validation

- `--cosim --cosim-interval 1000`: `[cosim] PASS: 4 checkpoint(s) + final state match the QEMU oracle (interval 1000, 4683 ROI retires)` - the GEMM executes inside the ROI on vsim and matches QEMU architecturally at every checkpoint.
- e2e with `VERIFY=1`: all 14 rt_c-family tests pass (7 fixtures, marker + pc).
- `test_andes_sim_f9.sh` (which uses this fixture) still passes.

One consequence worth knowing: rt_c_matmul's hybrid `window_cycles` jumps from ~74 to ~45,000 - the old figure was never measuring the kernel.

---
name: rt-c-matmul-empty-roi
description: "FIXED 2026-06-12 (7022599): rt_c_matmul's ROI was empty (kernel hoisted/DCE'd past the markers); root cause = non-escaping statics; lesson: marker memory clobbers only cover ESCAPED memory"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e41bc0d4-d741-42b4-ba15-e56e60fb3e8e
---

FIXED in 7022599 (2026-06-12). rt_c_matmul shipped with an EMPTY ROI:
the compiler hoisted the inlined GEMM above enter_vsim(), and with
noinline alone it deleted the call as a dead store. window_cycles (~74)
measured drain overhead. Found by --cosim's "N ROI retires" line.

ROOT CAUSE (the durable lesson): GCC's asm "memory" clobber only orders
accesses to ESCAPED memory. A `static` array whose address never leaves
the TU is invisible to the marker asm, so kernel code touching only such
arrays can hoist, sink, or be DCE'd across the markers -- noinline alone
does not save it (IPA mod/ref still proves the call dead). Fix pattern:
external linkage (or otherwise escape the address) for ROI data + a
noinline kernel call between the markers. rt_c_v_matmul survived only
because V intrinsics are opaque to IPA.

Guard: tests/fixtures/test_fixture_roi_content.sh statically asserts the
marker span carries the promised kernel (run it after touching fixtures
or bumping the toolchain). Quick dynamic check: --cosim prints the true
ROI retire count. After the fix: 8x8x8 GEMM (16^3 was ~322k vsim cycles,
too close to harness timeouts), 4683 ROI retires, ~45k cycles. See
[[feedback-verify-codegen-with-objdump]] and [[cosim-roi]].

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fixture ROI-content contract: a fixture whose phase-2 comment promises a
# kernel must actually carry that kernel BETWEEN the markers. The compiler
# may legally hoist an inlined kernel above enter_vsim() -- the markers'
# "memory" clobber does not cover statics whose address never escapes --
# which silently empties the ROI (rt_c_matmul shipped that way: markers
# back-to-back, window_cycles ~74 of pure drain overhead). Anchor rule
# (runtime/rt_c_helpers.h): kernels live in a noinline function called
# between the markers.
#
# Checks (static, objdump):
#   rt_c_matmul    span contains the GEMM: a kernel call (jal) or a mul
#   rt_c_v_matmul  span contains the kernel call (control: known-good)
#   rt_c_v_regs    span contains vector instructions (inline V kernel)
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[fixture_roi_content]: no objdump"; exit 77; }

FIXDIR="$SCRIPT_DIR"

# Instructions strictly between the ENTER and EXIT markers.
roi_body() {
  "$OBJDUMP" -d "$FIXDIR/$1.elf" \
    | awk '/5a002013/ { on = 1; next } /5a102013/ { exit } on'
}

check_roi() {  # $1 = fixture, $2 = required-content regex, $3 = description
  BODY=$(roi_body "$1")
  if [ -z "$BODY" ]; then
    fail "$1: ROI is EMPTY (markers back-to-back) -- kernel hoisted out?"
  fi
  if ! printf '%s\n' "$BODY" | grep -Eq "$2"; then
    echo "--- ROI body of $1 ---"
    printf '%s\n' "$BODY"
    fail "$1: ROI does not contain $3 (want /$2/)"
  fi
  ok "$1: ROI carries $3"
}

check_roi rt_c_matmul   '\sjal\s|\smulw?\s' "the GEMM (kernel call or mul)"
check_roi rt_c_v_matmul '\sjal\s'           "the kernel call"
check_roi rt_c_v_regs   '\sv[a-z0-9.]+\.v'  "vector instructions"

ok "fixture ROI content"

name: cosim-roi
description: "Checkpoint co-sim shipped 2026-06-12: run --cosim (dev) drains vsim checkpoints every N retires, QEMU oracle drains at the same minstret deltas, state-diff per window; mmap stays Shared"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e41bc0d4-d741-42b4-ba15-e56e60fb3e8e
---

Checkpoint co-simulation (roadmap: cosim_roi.md in repo root, all F1-F4
done 2026-06-12). `run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc --cosim
[--cosim-interval N]` (dev tier, default N=10000): vsim drains a
RESUMABLE checkpoint every N retires (StateDrain::drain_checkpoint undoes
the V-sweep clobbers vtype/vl/vstart/x5-x7 before resumereq); the driver
re-runs the ELF on a pure-QEMU oracle (plugin cosim_marker/cosim_pc +
cosim_counts=minstret deltas) and diffs window by window.

Key design facts:
- Alignment is by minstret delta, not pc (loop-safe; halt slack absorbed).
  Empirically minstret is NOT contaminated by Program Buffer execution in
  debug mode (ckpt delta exactly 1000 on a V workload).
- mmap stays MAP_SHARED. Private COW is a trap (un-COW'd pages see the
  other process's writes); the oracle simply replays from boot on its own
  RAM. See [[vsim-halt-slack]] and [[hsim-cpp-rewrite]].
- pc-trigger mode: the boundary insn counts as retire #1 on both sides
  (the pc handoff resumes AT the boundary; marker is counted by neither).
- Known edge: a checkpoint whose halt slack crosses the EXIT marker loses
  the exit retire (the run loop is blocked inside the drain) -- tiny
  intervals on tiny ROIs can crash with cmderr=4. Documented limitation.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Insert the 4f --cosim subsection into docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb,
executing the new code cell for real (same pattern as add_verify_nb.py)."""
import json, os, subprocess

ROOT = "/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim"
NB = os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", "andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb")

def md(text):
    return {"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {},
            "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

def code(text):
    return {"cell_type": "code", "execution_count": None, "metadata": {},
            "outputs": [], "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

nb = json.load(open(NB))
cells = nb["cells"]

# Sanity: insert right after 4e's trailing markdown (index 33), before "## 5.".
assert "VERIFY=1" in "".join(cells[33]["source"])
assert "## 5." in "".join(cells[34]["source"])

md_intro = md("""### 4f. Localize a divergence with checkpoint co-sim (`--cosim`)

`--verify` (4e) tells you THAT the vsim leg diverged; `--cosim` tells you
roughly WHERE. It is a developer tool (hidden from the release help, like
`state-diff` - set `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1` to see it in `run --help`):

```
hybrid run:  QEMU1 -> vsim: ..N insns..|..N insns..|.. exit
                              ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final drain
oracle run:  pure QEMU, drains at the SAME retire counts
diff ckpt k vs ckpt k -> first mismatch = the bad N-instruction window
```

Every N retired instructions (default 10000, `--cosim-interval` overrides)
the vsim leg halts the hart over DMI, drains a full architectural
checkpoint, and resumes. The driver reads each checkpoint's
`minstret - entry.minstret` (the exact post-entry retire count), re-runs
the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at those same counts, and
diffs checkpoint against checkpoint with the `state-diff` policy. The two
runs never share memory: the oracle replays the same deterministic program
from boot on its own RAM, so the shared mmap needs no change.""")

run_cell = code("!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker "
                "--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --cosim --cosim-interval 500 "
                "tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf")

md_after = md("""The GEMM ROI retires 1692 instructions, so interval 500 gives three
checkpoints; `[cosim] PASS` means all three AND the final state match the
oracle. On a divergence you instead get the mismatching fields and the
window that contains the first bad instruction:

```
[state-diff] x12: ref=0x2a got=0x2b
[cosim] FAIL: divergence in window 2 (retires 500..1000 after entry)
```

Re-run with a smaller `--cosim-interval` to shrink the window.

**Limitations of this co-sim design**

- **Window granularity, not instruction granularity.** A divergence is
  bracketed to one N-instruction window; finding the exact instruction
  means re-running with a smaller N. Intervals near the DMI halt overshoot
  (tens of instructions) are not meaningful.
- **Registers only - memory is not compared.** Each checkpoint covers pc,
  GPRs, FPRs, V CSRs and vector registers. A wrong store is caught only
  later, when the bad value is loaded back into a register.
- **The cycle figure is polluted.** Every checkpoint adds a DMI
  halt + drain + resume on the vsim leg, so `window_cycles` under
  `--cosim` is approximate. Re-measure without `--cosim` for the real
  figure.
- **`--trigger marker|pc` only, `--model hybrid` only.** The oracle must
  arm on a code boundary; the icount trigger's window semantics differ
  between the legs. Exclusive with `--verify` (the final-state check is
  already included).
- **Single-shot, deterministic runs only.** The oracle replays the program
  from boot, so the pre-ROI path must be deterministic, and the ROI is
  assumed to be entered once (same assumptions as the hybrid run itself).
- **Counters are excluded from the compare** (`mcycle`/`minstret` differ
  between engines by design), as are the passthrough M-CSRs/PMP - same
  policy as `state-diff`.

Details in `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.8.""")

# Execute the run cell for real.
env = dict(os.environ)
env["PATH"] = f"{ROOT}/build:" + env["PATH"]
script = "".join(run_cell["source"]).lstrip()[1:]
proc = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script], cwd=ROOT, env=env, text=True,
                      timeout=600, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                      stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
if proc.returncode != 0:
    raise SystemExit(f"cosim cell failed (rc={proc.returncode}):\n{proc.stdout}")
assert "[cosim] PASS: 3 checkpoint(s)" in proc.stdout, proc.stdout
run_cell["outputs"] = [{"name": "stdout", "output_type": "stream",
                        "text": proc.stdout.splitlines(keepends=True)}]

cells[34:34] = [md_intro, run_cell, md_after]

# Cheat sheet: add the --cosim line after the --verify one.
sheet = cells[40]
assert sheet["cell_type"] == "markdown" and "Cheat sheet" in "".join(sheet["source"])
src = "".join(sheet["source"])
needle = ("andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> "
          "--verify ELF   # + QEMU-oracle cross-check\n")
assert needle in src
src = src.replace(needle, needle +
    "andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> "
    "--cosim ELF    # localize a divergence (dev)\n")
sheet["source"] = src.splitlines(keepends=True)

# Renumber execution counts so the notebook still reads as run top-to-bottom.
n = 0
for c in cells:
    if c["cell_type"] == "code":
        n += 1
        c["execution_count"] = n

with open(NB, "w") as f:
    json.dump(nb, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    f.write("\n")
print(f"inserted 4f at 34; {len(cells)} cells; cosim output "
      f"{len(proc.stdout)} bytes")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run --cosim contract (cosim_roi F4): opt-in checkpoint co-simulation.
#   1. hybrid marker --cosim --cosim-interval 500 -> >=1 checkpoint,
#      "[cosim] PASS", rc 0 (rt_c_v_matmul: ~1.7k ROI retires -> 3 ckpts)
#   2. hybrid pc --cosim                          -> same through cosim_pc
#   3. default (no --cosim)                       -> no cosim output
#   4. usage errors: model, trigger, interval, --verify exclusivity
#   5. dev-only help surface
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"

# 1. marker mode with a sub-ROI interval -> real checkpoints.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --cosim --cosim-interval 500 "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker --cosim rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[cosim\] PASS' || fail "marker: no [cosim] PASS: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '\[cosim\] PASS: [1-9][0-9]* checkpoint' \
  || fail "marker: expected at least one checkpoint: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' || fail "marker: cycle figure missing: $OUT"
ok "hybrid marker --cosim: checkpoints + final match the oracle"

# 2. pc mode (boundaries = the fixture's own marker PCs, like docs 4.2).
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
  || fail "no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"
OUT=$("$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --pc-start "0x${MARKERS%% *}" --pc-end "0x${MARKERS##* }" \
      --cosim --cosim-interval 500 "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc --cosim rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[cosim\] PASS' || fail "pc: no [cosim] PASS: $OUT"
ok "hybrid pc --cosim: checkpoints + final match the oracle"

# 3. default off: no cosim leg, no cosim output.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "default hybrid rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qi 'cosim' && fail "default run leaked cosim output: $OUT"
ok "default: co-simulation stays off"

# 4. usage errors.
expect 2 'cosim requires --model hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --model fast --cosim "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'cosim requires --model hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --model cycle --cosim "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'cosim supports --trigger marker\|pc' \
  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --qemu-icount 1000 \
  --vsim-icount 100 --engine "$ENGINE" --cosim "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'cosim-interval requires --cosim' \
  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --cosim-interval 500 --engine "$ENGINE" "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'positive integer' \
  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --cosim --cosim-interval 0 --engine "$ENGINE" "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'exclusive' \
  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --cosim --verify --engine "$ENGINE" "$VSIM_ELF"
ok "--cosim usage errors (model/trigger/interval/--verify)"

# 5. dev-only help surface.
expect 0 ' --cosim ' env ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" run --help
OUT=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q -- '--cosim' && fail "release run --help leaks --cosim"
ok "--cosim help is dev-only"

ok "run --cosim checkpoint co-simulation"

Alignment is by retire count, not pc: vsim restores `minstret` from the
entry state, so `checkpoint.minstret - entry.minstret` is the exact number
of post-entry retires (vsim's DMI halt overshoots a few instructions; the
overshoot is simply part of the measured delta, and the oracle counts to
the same number). In pc-trigger mode the boundary instruction itself
retires inside the window and is counted as retire #1 on both sides.

Costs and limits:
- `--trigger marker|pc` only, `--model hybrid` only, exclusive with
  `--verify` (the final-state check is included).
- Each checkpoint costs a DMI halt + drain + resume on the vsim leg, so
  `window_cycles` under `--cosim` includes that overhead -- treat the
  figure as approximate and re-measure without `--cosim`.
- Divergence is localized to an N-instruction window, not an exact
  instruction; intervals comparable to the halt overshoot (tens of
  instructions) are not meaningful.
- Memory is NOT compared -- only the architectural register state at each
  checkpoint (a memory bug surfaces indirectly, when a wrong value is
  loaded into a register).

---

## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)

Fixtures linked with `-lgloss_vh` (semihosting) can print only where a QEMU
intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no semihosting, which is
why the Phase-2 "no syscalls inside the ROI" rule exists. The **vplat
runtime** removes the per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff.

| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |

content.text:
Both test edits are reverted; nothing is changed. Discussion only:

## 1. window_cycles vs --cosim: agree, they should be mutually exclusive

The tutorial run is the proof: rt_c_v_matmul's ROI retires 1692 instructions but printed `window_cycles 22530` under `--cosim` - the figure is mostly checkpoint drain overhead (each checkpoint is hundreds of DMI operations, each burning simulated cycles). Printing a number that wrong invites someone to quote it.

The change is small, all in the driver layer: gate the print at `driver/cmd_run.cpp:238` on `!cli.cosim`, flip the contract in `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_cosim.sh:32` (currently it asserts the figure IS printed), update USER_GUIDE 4.8, the tutorial 4f limitation bullet, and re-execute the tutorial cell. Say go and I'll do it test-first.

## 2. Memory co-sim: yes to a new option, but I recommend a different mechanism

A separate opt-in flag (say `--cosim-mem`) is right regardless of mechanism - memory checking costs more than register checkpoints, so it should not be the default. On the mechanism, comparing every load/store's address+value has one hard blocker and three frictions:

- **Blocker: vsim has no load/store tap.** Today we only sample committed PCs from the WB retire wires. Committed address+data needs new probe wiring into the LSU, per CPU variant. (The QEMU side is easy - `qemu_plugin_register_vcpu_mem_cb` + `qemu_plugin_mem_get_value` exist in our fork; I checked `QEMU/include/qemu/qemu-plugin.h:592`.)
- Records do not line up 1:1: the RTL is dual-issue and splits vector/misaligned accesses into beats differently than QEMU does, so you must canonicalize both traces down to per-byte memory effects - which is reconstructing memory state anyway.
- Polled MMIO breaks it: vplat binaries poll the UART LSR inside the ROI, and the two engines poll a different number of times by design, so even the trace lengths differ.
- Wrong **loads** are already caught: a wrong loaded value lands in a register, so the next register checkpoint diffs. The real uncovered hole is silent wrong **stores**.

**Counter-proposal for `--cosim-mem`: compare memory state at each checkpoint, not each access.** Both sides' RAM is already a plain file - vsim's DRAM is the shared mmap, and the oracle runs on its own fresh mmap. At every checkpoint, hash (or snapshot) the ELF's load segments on both sides; diff per window; on mismatch, byte-diff and print the bad addresses. That catches a wrong store in the window it happens, with the same window granularity as the register compare, no RTL tapping, no giant traces, and MMIO is naturally excluded.

One question I must verify before committing to this design: the AX45MPV L1 D-cache is real write-back RTL, so dirty lines may not have reached the mmap when we halt for a checkpoint. The checkpoint would then need a D-cache writeback (Andes CCTL ops through the Program Buffer, while halted) before hashing - I need to confirm CCTL works under debug halt in vsim. The old rt_shared_mem QEMU2 roundtrip suggests stores do reach the mmap, but I have not verified whether that was write-through behavior or just eviction luck.

If you accept the checkpoint-hash direction, I'll write a `cosim_mem.md` roadmap with that verification as F1. If you specifically need instruction-level localization of a bad store, the trace design is the only way, and the vsim LSU tap is the price - my recommendation is window-level first, since `--cosim-interval` already shrinks windows on demand.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run --cosim contract (cosim_roi F4): opt-in checkpoint co-simulation.
#   1. hybrid marker --cosim --cosim-interval 500 -> >=1 checkpoint,
#      "[cosim] PASS", rc 0 (rt_c_v_matmul: ~1.7k ROI retires -> 3 ckpts)
#   2. hybrid pc --cosim                          -> same through cosim_pc
#   3. default (no --cosim)                       -> no cosim output
#   4. usage errors: model, trigger, interval, --verify exclusivity
#   5. dev-only help surface
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"

# 1. marker mode with a sub-ROI interval -> real checkpoints.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --cosim --cosim-interval 500 "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker --cosim rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[cosim\] PASS' || fail "marker: no [cosim] PASS: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '\[cosim\] PASS: [1-9][0-9]* checkpoint' \
  || fail "marker: expected at least one checkpoint: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' || fail "marker: cycle figure missing: $OUT"
ok "hybrid marker --cosim: checkpoints + final match the oracle"

# 2. pc mode (boundaries = the fixture's own marker PCs, like docs 4.2).
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
  || fail "no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"
OUT=$("$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --pc-start "0x${MARKERS%% *}" --pc-end "0x${MARKERS##* }" \
      --cosim --cosim-interval 500 "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc --cosim rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[cosim\] PASS' || fail "pc: no [cosim] PASS: $OUT"
ok "hybrid pc --cosim: checkpoints + final match the oracle"

# 3. default off: no cosim leg, no cosim output.

ok "default: co-simulation stays off"

  "$BIN" run --model fast --cosim "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'cosim requires --model hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --model cycle --cosim "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'cosim supports --trigger marker\|pc' \
  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --qemu-icount 1000 \

expect 2 'exclusive' \

ok "--cosim usage errors (model/trigger/interval/--verify)"

# 5. dev-only help surface.
expect 0 ' --cosim ' env ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" run --help
OUT=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q -- '--cosim' && fail "release run --help leaks --cosim"
ok "--cosim help is dev-only"

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# cosim_roi -- checkpoint co-simulation between QEMU and vsim inside the ROI

Status: ACCEPTED (PM decision, 2026-06-12): Option A (checkpoint co-sim).
  1. Dev tier (debug tool, hidden from release help like state-diff).
  2. Default checkpoint interval N=10000; `--cosim-interval <N>` overrides.
  3. Trigger scope: marker|pc only (same as --verify).

## Problem

`--verify` (verify_oracle.md) compares only the FINAL state at the ROI exit.
When it fails, we know the vsim leg diverged somewhere inside the ROI, but not
where. Checkpoint co-sim drains and compares the architectural state every N
retired instructions, so a divergence is localized to the first bad
N-instruction window. Rerun with smaller N to narrow it.

## Flow

```
Run 1 (hybrid):  QEMU1 -> vsim: ..N insns..|..N insns..|.. exit
                                  ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final drain
Run 2 (oracle):  pure QEMU from boot: arm at ROI entry, drain at the SAME
                 retire counts ->     ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final
diff ckpt k vs ckpt k (existing state_diff policy); first mismatch = window k.
```

Alignment is by RETIRE COUNT, not pc: vsim's DMI halt overshoots 0-3
instructions (halt slack, see verify_oracle.md "Boundary semantics"), and pc
alignment is ambiguous inside loops. vsim restores minstret from QEMU1's
drained value at entry, so `ckpt.minstret - entry.minstret` is the exact
number of post-entry retires; the oracle plugin counts exec callbacks after
arming and drains at those exact deltas. pc then matches by construction
when execution is correct, and diverges loudly when it is not.

## Memory: keep the mmap Shared, do NOT flip to Private

- Today: QEMU writes guest RAM through `-object memory-backend-file,share=on`;
  vsim maps the same file `MAP_SHARED | MAP_POPULATE`
  (verilator/src/platform/mmap_backing.hpp:34). This stays unchanged.
- vsim Private, QEMU shared: Linux private file mappings are copy-on-write
  PER PAGE; un-written pages still show the live file, so the other engine's
  stores leak in until the first local write. Nondeterministic contamination.
- QEMU Private (share=off): pre-ROI writes never reach the file; vsim resumes
  on stale memory. The handoff breaks.
- Resolution: the two runs never share memory at all. The oracle is a
  separate QEMU process re-running the same ELF from boot on its own RAM
  (exactly like --verify); pre-ROI determinism is already proven by the
  VERIFY=1 gate (35/35 identical entry states).

## Design notes (from code reading)

- vsim exit drain today: simulator.hpp check_hybrid_handoff -> on_retire(pc)
  -> StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough -> write file -> exit 200. Abstract
  reads are non-destructive, BUT the trailing V data sweep (vse8.v via the
  Program Buffer) clobbers vtype/vl/vstart and x5/x6/x7. The exit drain never
  resumes, so the clobbers are free. A CHECKPOINT drain resumes, so it must
  undo them from the freshly drained values (vsetvl restore staging x5/x6,
  then vstart, then rewrite x5/x6/x7), then resumereq + poll allresumeack.
  All primitives exist (resume_driver.hpp, program_buffer.hpp).
- Known risks (empirical, the F4 gate decides):
  - minstret during debug mode: if Program Buffer instructions (V sweep +
    clobber undo) increment minstret, later checkpoints' deltas inflate and
    the oracle drains late. Fix if observed: set dcsr.stopcount at halt.
    Non-V fixtures are clean either way (abstract commands only).
  - mcycle during the checkpoint halts may inflate window_cycles; --cosim is
    a debug tool, the figure is documented approximate under it.

## F1: vsim resumable checkpoint drain
State: done
Description: `StateDrain::drain_checkpoint(input)` -- drain_with_passthrough,
then (V flag only) undo the sweep clobbers using the drained values:
stage x5=vl, x6=vtype, exec `vsetvl x0,x5,x6` in the Program Buffer, write
vstart (after vsetvl: vsetvl zeroes it), rewrite x5/x6/x7 from the drained
GPRs; finally resumereq + poll allresumeack. Hart continues where it halted
(DPC untouched). Unit tests on the recording-bus double assert the write
sequence and that the returned state equals the plain drain.
Key files: verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp,
verilator/tests/hybrid/state_drain.test.cpp
Dependencies: none

## F2: vsim --hybrid-cosim N (checkpoint loop + numbered files)
State: done
Description: HandoffController counts retires; every N (monotonic target, not
modulo) it calls drain_checkpoint and hands the state to a sink callback;
the exit trigger still wins on the same retire and keeps today's semantics.
simulator.hpp provides the sink: V-merge from scratch (read_v_from_scratch)
then write `<handoff_out>.ckpt<k>` (k from 1). New CLI arg `--hybrid-cosim
<N>` (main.cpp), valid only with --resume-from-qemu + marker/pc trigger
(error with --hybrid-icount). Controller unit tests with a fake trigger +

`--verify` tells you THAT the vsim leg diverged; `--cosim` tells you
roughly WHERE. It is a developer tool (hidden from the release help, like
`state-diff`): every N retired instructions inside the ROI, the vsim leg
halts via DMI, drains a resumable checkpoint to `<state>.ckpt<k>`, and
continues. The driver then re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin
draining at the SAME retire counts, and diffs checkpoint k against

```

---
name: cosim-roi
description: "Checkpoint co-sim shipped 2026-06-12: run --cosim (dev) drains vsim checkpoints every N retires, QEMU oracle drains at the same minstret deltas, state-diff per window; mmap stays Shared"
metadata:

---

Checkpoint co-simulation (roadmap: cosim_roi.md in repo root, all F1-F4
done 2026-06-12). `run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc --cosim
[--cosim-interval N]` (dev tier, default N=10000): vsim drains a
RESUMABLE checkpoint every N retires (StateDrain::drain_checkpoint undoes
the V-sweep clobbers vtype/vl/vstart/x5-x7 before resumereq); the driver
re-runs the ELF on a pure-QEMU oracle (plugin cosim_marker/cosim_pc +
cosim_counts=minstret deltas) and diffs window by window.

Key design facts:
- Alignment is by minstret delta, not pc (loop-safe; halt slack absorbed).
  Empirically minstret is NOT contaminated by Program Buffer execution in
  debug mode (ckpt delta exactly 1000 on a V workload).

name: cosim-roi
description: "Checkpoint co-sim shipped 2026-06-12: run --cosim (dev) drains vsim checkpoints every N retires, QEMU oracle drains at the same minstret deltas, state-diff per window; mmap stays Shared"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e41bc0d4-d741-42b4-ba15-e56e60fb3e8e
---

Checkpoint co-simulation (roadmap: cosim_roi.md in repo root, all F1-F4
done 2026-06-12). `run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc --cosim
[--cosim-interval N]` (dev tier, default N=10000): vsim drains a
RESUMABLE checkpoint every N retires (StateDrain::drain_checkpoint undoes
the V-sweep clobbers vtype/vl/vstart/x5-x7 before resumereq); the driver
re-runs the ELF on a pure-QEMU oracle (plugin cosim_marker/cosim_pc +
cosim_counts=minstret deltas) and diffs window by window.

Key design facts:
- window_cycles and --cosim are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE (d0b9481, PM decision
  2026-06-12): checkpoint drains pollute the mcycle delta (22530 for a
  1692-retire ROI), so the driver suppresses the figure under --cosim.
- Register-only compare is final: PM rejected per-load/store and
  per-checkpoint memory co-sim (vsim has no LSU tap; L1D write-back vs
  mmap snapshot was the open question).
- Alignment is by minstret delta, not pc (loop-safe; halt slack absorbed).
  Empirically minstret is NOT contaminated by Program Buffer execution in
  debug mode (ckpt delta exactly 1000 on a V workload).
- mmap stays MAP_SHARED. Private COW is a trap (un-COW'd pages see the
  other process's writes); the oracle simply replays from boot on its own
  RAM. See [[vsim-halt-slack]] and [[hsim-cpp-rewrite]].
- pc-trigger mode: the boundary insn counts as retire #1 on both sides
  (the pc handoff resumes AT the boundary; marker is counted by neither).
- Known edge: a checkpoint whose halt slack crosses the EXIT marker loses
  the exit retire (the run loop is blocked inside the drain) -- tiny
  intervals on tiny ROIs can crash with cmderr=4. Documented limitation.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tutorial 4f follow-up: --cosim now suppresses window_cycles.
Rewrite the limitation bullet and re-execute the --cosim cell."""
import json, os, subprocess

ROOT = "/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim"
NB = os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", "andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb")

nb = json.load(open(NB))
cells = nb["cells"]

run_cell = next(c for c in cells if c["cell_type"] == "code"
                and "--cosim --cosim-interval 500" in "".join(c["source"]))
md_after = next(c for c in cells if c["cell_type"] == "markdown"
                and "The cycle figure is polluted." in "".join(c["source"]))

old = """- **The cycle figure is polluted.** Every checkpoint adds a DMI
  halt + drain + resume on the vsim leg, so `window_cycles` under
  `--cosim` is approximate. Re-measure without `--cosim` for the real
  figure.
"""
new = """- **No cycle figure.** Every checkpoint adds a DMI halt + drain + resume
  on the vsim leg, which pollutes the vsim `mcycle` delta, so `--cosim`
  suppresses `window_cycles` entirely. Re-run without `--cosim` to
  measure.
"""
src = "".join(md_after["source"])
assert old in src, "bullet not found"
md_after["source"] = src.replace(old, new).splitlines(keepends=True)

env = dict(os.environ)
env["PATH"] = f"{ROOT}/build:" + env["PATH"]
script = "".join(run_cell["source"]).lstrip()[1:]
proc = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script], cwd=ROOT, env=env, text=True,
                      timeout=600, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                      stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
if proc.returncode != 0:
    raise SystemExit(f"cosim cell failed (rc={proc.returncode}):\n{proc.stdout}")
assert "[cosim] PASS: 3 checkpoint(s)" in proc.stdout, proc.stdout
assert "window_cycles" not in proc.stdout, proc.stdout
run_cell["outputs"] = [{"name": "stdout", "output_type": "stream",
                        "text": proc.stdout.splitlines(keepends=True)}]

with open(NB, "w") as f:
    json.dump(nb, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    f.write("\n")
print(f"bullet rewritten; cosim cell re-run, {len(proc.stdout)} bytes, "
      "no window_cycles")

# cosim_roi -- checkpoint co-simulation between QEMU and vsim inside the ROI

Status: ACCEPTED (PM decision, 2026-06-12): Option A (checkpoint co-sim).
  1. Dev tier (debug tool, hidden from release help like state-diff).
  2. Default checkpoint interval N=10000; `--cosim-interval <N>` overrides.
  3. Trigger scope: marker|pc only (same as --verify).

## Problem

`--verify` (verify_oracle.md) compares only the FINAL state at the ROI exit.
When it fails, we know the vsim leg diverged somewhere inside the ROI, but not
where. Checkpoint co-sim drains and compares the architectural state every N
retired instructions, so a divergence is localized to the first bad
N-instruction window. Rerun with smaller N to narrow it.

## Flow

```
Run 1 (hybrid):  QEMU1 -> vsim: ..N insns..|..N insns..|.. exit
                                  ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final drain
Run 2 (oracle):  pure QEMU from boot: arm at ROI entry, drain at the SAME
                 retire counts ->     ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final
diff ckpt k vs ckpt k (existing state_diff policy); first mismatch = window k.
```

Alignment is by RETIRE COUNT, not pc: vsim's DMI halt overshoots 0-3
instructions (halt slack, see verify_oracle.md "Boundary semantics"), and pc
alignment is ambiguous inside loops. vsim restores minstret from QEMU1's
drained value at entry, so `ckpt.minstret - entry.minstret` is the exact
number of post-entry retires; the oracle plugin counts exec callbacks after
arming and drains at those exact deltas. pc then matches by construction
when execution is correct, and diverges loudly when it is not.

## Memory: keep the mmap Shared, do NOT flip to Private

- Today: QEMU writes guest RAM through `-object memory-backend-file,share=on`;
  vsim maps the same file `MAP_SHARED | MAP_POPULATE`
  (verilator/src/platform/mmap_backing.hpp:34). This stays unchanged.
- vsim Private, QEMU shared: Linux private file mappings are copy-on-write
  PER PAGE; un-written pages still show the live file, so the other engine's
  stores leak in until the first local write. Nondeterministic contamination.
- QEMU Private (share=off): pre-ROI writes never reach the file; vsim resumes
  on stale memory. The handoff breaks.
- Resolution: the two runs never share memory at all. The oracle is a
  separate QEMU process re-running the same ELF from boot on its own RAM
  (exactly like --verify); pre-ROI determinism is already proven by the
  VERIFY=1 gate (35/35 identical entry states).

## Design notes (from code reading)

- vsim exit drain today: simulator.hpp check_hybrid_handoff -> on_retire(pc)
  -> StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough -> write file -> exit 200. Abstract
  reads are non-destructive, BUT the trailing V data sweep (vse8.v via the
  Program Buffer) clobbers vtype/vl/vstart and x5/x6/x7. The exit drain never
  resumes, so the clobbers are free. A CHECKPOINT drain resumes, so it must
  undo them from the freshly drained values (vsetvl restore staging x5/x6,
  then vstart, then rewrite x5/x6/x7), then resumereq + poll allresumeack.
  All primitives exist (resume_driver.hpp, program_buffer.hpp).
- Known risks (empirical, the F4 gate decides):
  - minstret during debug mode: if Program Buffer instructions (V sweep +
    clobber undo) increment minstret, later checkpoints' deltas inflate and
    the oracle drains late. Fix if observed: set dcsr.stopcount at halt.
    Non-V fixtures are clean either way (abstract commands only).
  - mcycle during the checkpoint halts inflates window_cycles (observed:
    22530 for a 1692-retire ROI); the driver therefore suppresses the
    window_cycles line under --cosim -- the two are mutually exclusive
    (PM decision 2026-06-12). Re-run without --cosim to measure.

## F1: vsim resumable checkpoint drain
State: done
Description: `StateDrain::drain_checkpoint(input)` -- drain_with_passthrough,
then (V flag only) undo the sweep clobbers using the drained values:
stage x5=vl, x6=vtype, exec `vsetvl x0,x5,x6` in the Program Buffer, write
vstart (after vsetvl: vsetvl zeroes it), rewrite x5/x6/x7 from the drained
GPRs; finally resumereq + poll allresumeack. Hart continues where it halted
(DPC untouched). Unit tests on the recording-bus double assert the write
sequence and that the returned state equals the plain drain.
Key files: verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp,
verilator/tests/hybrid/state_drain.test.cpp
Dependencies: none

## F2: vsim --hybrid-cosim N (checkpoint loop + numbered files)
State: done
Description: HandoffController counts retires; every N (monotonic target, not
modulo) it calls drain_checkpoint and hands the state to a sink callback;
the exit trigger still wins on the same retire and keeps today's semantics.
simulator.hpp provides the sink: V-merge from scratch (read_v_from_scratch)
then write `<handoff_out>.ckpt<k>` (k from 1). New CLI arg `--hybrid-cosim
<N>` (main.cpp), valid only with --resume-from-qemu + marker/pc trigger
(error with --hybrid-icount). Controller unit tests with a fake trigger +
recording bus; manual two-leg smoke (QEMU1 then vsim --hybrid-cosim) checks
.ckpt files appear with ascending minstret.
Key files: verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp, verilator/src/simulator.hpp,
verilator/src/main.cpp, verilator/tests/hybrid/handoff_controller.test.cpp
Dependencies: F1

## F3: plugin cosim oracle mode (counted multi-drain)
State: done
Description: new plugin args, exclusive with all other trigger modes:
  cosim_marker=1      arm on the ENTER marker `slti x0,x0,0x5A0`
  cosim_pc=0x...      arm on an explicit entry boundary vaddr
  cosim_counts=a:b:c  ascending post-entry retire deltas (colon-separated);
                      each but the last drains to `<outfile>.ckpt<k>` and
                      continues; the LAST drains to `<outfile>` and exits 200
Counting: exec callbacks fire pre-execution; at the m-th post-arm callback
exactly m-1 post-entry instructions have retired, so drain when the running
count equals the target (check-then-increment), capturing pc = next-insn
vaddr -- the same point as vsim's DPC. The entry marker itself is counted by
NEITHER side (QEMU1 drains pre-marker, vsim resumes past it).
Key files: qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c,
tests/plugin/test_plugin_cosim_drain.sh (new)
Dependencies: none

## F4: andes-sim run --cosim (default off, Dev)
State: done
Description: `--cosim` on `run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc` (+
`--cosim-interval <N>`, default 10000; --cosim-interval without --cosim,
--cosim with fast/cycle/icount, and --cosim with --verify are usage errors;
--cosim already subsumes the final-state check). Flow: hybrid plan runs with
the vsim leg carrying `--hybrid-cosim N` (Trigger param -> leg_trigger_args);
run_plan collects `<outfile>.ckpt<k>` into PhaseResult.checkpoints before
workdir cleanup; the driver computes minstret deltas vs the entry state,
runs the one-step oracle plan (fresh mmap, cosim_marker/cosim_pc +
cosim_counts), diffs ckpt k vs ckpt k then final vs final via diff_states,
and reports `[cosim] PASS: <K> checkpoints + final state match` or the first
diverging window `[cosim] FAIL: divergence in window <k> (retires <lo>..<hi>
after entry)` plus the field diffs, rc 1.
Gate: cosim e2e green on rt_c_hello (no V), rt_c_matmul (FP), rt_c_v_regs +
rt_c_v_matmul (V) -- this empirically settles the minstret/debug-mode risk.
Key files: driver/cli.hpp/.cpp, driver/plan.hpp, driver/run_plan.cpp,
driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/main.cpp (dev help),
tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_cosim.sh (new)
Dependencies: F1, F2, F3 (and F2's state-diff core from verify_oracle)

## Docs
Each feature updates docs/USER_GUIDE.md in its own change set: F3 adds the
plugin-arg rows (2.3), F4 adds the dev-facing --cosim subsection next to
--verify (what it localizes, the masking rule, why window_cycles is
approximate under --cosim).

## Rejected: Option B (streaming trace-compare)
Both engines stream per-retire records into shm rings; exact localization but
vsim's retire hook is pc-only (`on_retire(uint64_t pc)`, simulator.hpp:504; no
RVFI/writeback trace), so full value compare needs new RTL probing. Revisit
only if window-bracketing proves too coarse.
