1	# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations
2	
3	What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
4	hang, or crash on a real workload. Written 2026-05-28 from a direct read of
5	the current code (not just the older audit notes).
6	
7	How this file relates to the others:
8	
9	- `ROADMAP.md` (top level) - the master feature roadmap. Every open
10	  limitation below is absorbed there as an `F-ENG-*` feature; that file is
11	  the *plan to fix*. This file stays the *plain-English "do not do this"
12	  list* and the source of the L-ids.
13	- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - the older failure-mode backlog (`F-T*`) and the
14	  gem5-parity bug-audit wave (`B1-B20`, fully closed), both superseded by
15	  `ROADMAP.md`. Kept for history.
16	
17	Each entry below was checked against the code on 2026-05-28. The `Where`
18	line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow
23	
24	This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
25	consequence of it.
26	
27	When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
28	part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:60-145`: it restores GPRs,
29	FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
30	`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
31	`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.
32	
33	So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`) MUST
34	be:
35	
36	- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
37	- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
38	- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
39	- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
40	- No system calls / semihosting
41	- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
42	- No MMIO (UART, PLIC, timer, ROM)
43	
44	If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
45	wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.
46	
47	---
48	
49	## State coverage: what the wire format carries
50	
51	Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
52	`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
53	(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
54	and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).
55	
56	### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`
57	
58	- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
59	- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
60	  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
61	- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
62	- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
63	- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
64	- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed
65	
66	### NOT in the wire format at all
67	
68	- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
69	  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
70	- `fcsr / frm / fflags` (FP rounding mode + sticky flags). See L20.
71	- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
72	  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
73	- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
74	  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.
75	
76	### Carried but NOT restored into vsim
77	
78	The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
79	writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:
80	
81	- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
82	  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).
83	
84	Only four CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
85	mcycle, minstret` (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`).
86	
87	### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free
88	
89	Three surfaces, three ceilings:
90	
91	| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
92	|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
93	| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
94	| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
95	| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |
96	
97	Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":
98	
99	1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[216]` fits about 27 more
100	   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
101	2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
102	   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
103	   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
104	   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
105	   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
106	   the cycle figure.
107	
108	Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set (`fcsr`, S-mode trap
109	CSRs, a chosen Andes microarch subset) in a v2 layout is feasible.
110	"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
111	redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload
116	
117	### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)
118	
119	- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
120	  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
121	- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
122	  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
123	  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
124	  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
125	- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
126	  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
127	- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg, before the
128	  ROI). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.
129	
130	### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)
131	
132	- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
133	  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
134	- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
135	  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:292-295`), but the resume step writes none of
136	  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
137	  silently disappears.
138	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
139	- Status: OPEN.
140	
141	### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI
142	
143	- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
144	  almost anything under an OS.
145	- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
146	  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
147	  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
148	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:32-42` (CSR constant list has no satp);
149	  `resume()` never writes it.
150	- Status: OPEN, and only partly documented (CLAUDE.md mentions trap-free +
151	  PMP-static but not paging).
152	
153	### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)
154	
155	- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
156	  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
157	- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
158	  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
159	  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values. Also `mepc`/
160	  trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap handling inside
161	  the ROI starts from reset values.
162	- Where: `state_drain.hpp:71-109` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
163	  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
164	- Status: OPEN.
165	
166	### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)
167	
168	- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
169	  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
170	- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
171	  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
172	  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
173	- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
174	- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
175	  at the trigger.
176	
177	### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)
178	
179	- When it bites: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
180	  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
181	  it, while running FP code inside.
182	- What happens: `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and `fflags[4:0]`) is not
183	  in `hybrid_state_v1`. The plugin does not drain it; the resume step
184	  does not restore it; the drain does not read it back. vsim sees the
185	  reset value (RNE, no flags). FP results inside the ROI use the
186	  wrong rounding;
187	  sticky flags after the ROI are wrong.
188	- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no `fcsr` field);
189	  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no `fcsr` handle in `VcpuRegs`);
190	  `resume_driver.hpp` (no `fcsr` restore).
191	- Status: OPEN. Concrete next move: add `uint64_t fcsr` from
192	  `reserved[]`, drain alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is
193	  enabled, and drain it back at vsim exit.
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up
198	
199	### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)
200	
201	- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at the
202	  trigger boundary.
203	- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
204	  `state_drain.hpp:51` and `hybrid_handoff.c:264`. On the vsim side DCSR.prv
205	  is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. S/U code then raises
206	  illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
207	- Where: `state_drain.hpp:51`, `hybrid_handoff.c:264`.
208	- Status: OPEN.
209	
210	### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)
211	
212	- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default 128 MB
213	  shared memory.
214	- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
215	  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
216	  corruption.
217	- Where: orchestrator mmap sizing; `--mmap-size` exists but nothing validates
218	  ELF size against it.
219	- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mmap-size` large enough by hand.
220	
221	### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)
222	
223	- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
224	  sync.
225	- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
226	  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
227	  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
228	  both.
229	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
230	  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
231	- Status: OPEN.
232	
233	### L9. MMIO inside the ROI is not handled  (F-T2.5)
234	
235	- When it bites: the ROI touches UART (`putchar`), PLIC, the timer, ROM, or
236	  any aliased/device memory.
237	- What happens: the Phase-5 interconnect watch was never built. Writes to
238	  MMIO ranges either vanish or hit RAM as if they were normal memory.
239	- Where: no allowlist/watch in the platform interconnect.
240	- Status: OPEN.
241	
242	---
243	
244	## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits
245	
246	### L10. The whole pipeline is hard-wired to one CPU
247	
248	- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU other than
249	  `andes-ax45mpv`, or any VLEN other than 512.
250	- What happens: the QEMU spawn passes `-machine andes_ae350` and
251	  `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` literally (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`).
252	  The V-register scratch address is the constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000`
253	  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), which is only correct when RAM base is 0 (true
254	  for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt` where it would need 0x80FF0000).
255	  The shared-memory base defaults to 0 in `spawn.py`. Nothing parameterizes
256	  these per machine.
257	- Where: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:38-42`.
258	- Status: by design for now; blocks porting to another core.
259	
260	### L11. VLEN is fixed at 512 bits, and a mismatch is silent  (F-T3.4)
261	
262	- When it bites: a fixture built for a different VLEN than the vsim config,
263	  or any future config change to VLEN.
264	- What happens: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per vector register
265	  (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`). There is no runtime check
266	  that `vlenb` from QEMU equals `vlenb` in vsim. If they differ, the upper
267	  bytes of each V register are uninitialized scratch -> garbage in the V
268	  regfile. The constant is also duplicated in `checkpoint.py:44`
269	  (`LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`) and can drift from `spawn.py`.
270	- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `checkpoint.py:44`.
271	- Status: OPEN.
272	
273	### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0
274	
275	- When it bites: a workload that legitimately writes CSR `0x7C0` with
276	  immediate 0 or 1.
277	- What happens: the default (CSR) mode treats `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` as ROI entry
278	  and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` as exit. A real write to that CSR would false-trigger
279	  a handoff. (0x7C0 is a benign vendor CSR on ax45mp, so this is unlikely in
280	  practice, but it is a hard assumption.)
281	- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` CSR matcher; `csr_trigger.hpp`.
282	- Status: inherent to CSR mode. Workaround: use `--mode pc` or `--mode icount`.
283	
284	### L13. CSR marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18, documented)
285	
286	- When it bites: never today, but worth knowing.
287	- What happens: the matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes
288	  (`hybrid_handoff.c:505-506`). RV32C has no compressed `csrwi`, so this is
289	  correct now; if a future extension adds a 16-bit CSR write the marker and
290	  this gate must change together.
291	- Where: `hybrid_handoff.c:499-506`.
292	- Status: documented limit, no action needed now.
293	
294	### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement
295	
296	- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you read
297	  the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
298	- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
299	  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
300	  (`hsim.py:1188-1193`), and the whole-program figure is
301	  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
302	  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
303	     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
304	     CPI is biased high.
305	  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
306	     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
307	- Where: `hsim.py:1122-1202` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
308	- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.
309	
310	### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)
311	
312	- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
313	  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
314	  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
315	- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
316	  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
317	  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
318	  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
319	  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
320	  CSR `0x7C0` is also actively repurposed by the trigger matcher (L12)
321	  instead of being preserved.
322	- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
323	  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
324	  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
325	- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
326	  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
327	  software-visible (must round-trip).
328	
329	---
330	
331	## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps
332	
333	### L15. No value-level check that the handoff copied state correctly  (F-T3.1)
334	
335	- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
336	  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
337	- What happens: those paths only assert exit code and PC range. A wrong
338	  register value passes silently. There is no `g`-packet readback compared
339	  against the drained state.
340	- Where: `hsim.py` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
341	- Status: OPEN. This is the cheapest high-value fix (see
342	  `docs/archive/TODO.md` "next moves", or `ROADMAP.md` F-ENG-01).
343	
344	### L16. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] CSR restore to QEMU2 is silently skipped if the stub omits the name
345	
346	- When it bites: a QEMU build whose feature XML does not advertise some CSR
347	  (e.g. `medeleg`, `satp`, `mie`).
348	- What happens: GPRs and PC hard-fail if missing, but every CSR/PMP/V write
349	  goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns quietly when the name is not
350	  found (`gdbstub.py:251-258`). That CSR keeps QEMU2's reset value with no
351	  warning. The asymmetry (hard-fail GPR vs silent-skip CSR) is the hazard.
352	- Where: `gdbstub.py:251-258`, used at `gdbstub.py:299-305`.
353	- Status: REMOVED - the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09.
354	
355	### L17. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] gdbstub handback uses a fixed 10 s timeout and a racy port pick
356	
357	- When it bites: QEMU2 slow to answer under host load; or many parallel runs
358	  (the `JOBS=8` e2e runner) picking ports at the same time.
359	- What happens: `RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0` is hardcoded (`gdbstub.py:135`); a slow
360	  reply raises mid-restore and the run dies. `pick_free_port` binds port 0,
361	  reads the number, closes, then QEMU binds it later - a TOCTOU window where
362	  another process can grab the port (`spawn.py`, acknowledged in its
363	  comment). Wrong-port connect = hang until timeout.
364	- Where: `gdbstub.py:135`, `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`.
365	- Status: REMOVED - the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09.
366	
367	### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only
368	
369	- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing hosts
370	  with different struct alignment.
371	- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no byte-swap
372	  path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror uses a native-endian
373	  `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:30`), so a BE host would mis-parse the body
374	  while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent mis-read.
375	- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:30`.
376	- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).
377	
378	### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)
379	
380	- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
381	  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
382	- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
383	  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
384	- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
385	  mid-run are not covered.
386	- [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] A QEMU2 that
387	  launches but never answers the gdbstub can be left as a zombie (no
388	  SIGALRM watchdog around the handshake).
389	- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.
390	
391	---
392	
393	## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)
394	
395	The QEMU2 handback leg has been removed entirely (2026-06-09). The
396	simulator is now 2-phase: QEMU1 drains architectural state to the
397	`hybrid_state_v1` file and exits; vsim resumes from that file, runs the
398	ROI cycle-accurately, and drains again. There is no third phase. Any
399	docs (`CLAUDE.md`, older architecture notes) that still describe
400	`verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`, a QEMU2 spawn, or a gdbstub
401	P-packet restore are stale - that code path no longer exists.
402	
403	---
404	
405	## Quick reference
406	
407	| ID  | Limitation                              | Severity | Status |
408	|-----|-----------------------------------------|----------|--------|
409	| L1  | No syscalls/semihosting in ROI          | blocker  | open   |
410	| L2  | PMP not restored to vsim                | high     | open   |
411	| L3  | Paging (satp) off in ROI                | high     | open   |
412	| L4  | Trap state lost across ROI              | high     | open   |
413	| L5  | LR/SC cannot cross handoff              | high     | open   |
414	| L6  | Privilege forced to M-mode              | high     | open   |
415	| L7  | 128 MB mmap, no bounds check            | medium   | open   |
416	| L8  | Single hart only                        | medium   | open   |
417	| L9  | MMIO in ROI not handled                 | medium   | open   |
418	| L10 | Hard-wired to andes_ae350 / ax45mpv     | medium   | by design |
419	| L11 | VLEN fixed at 512, mismatch silent      | medium   | open   |
420	| L12 | CSR 0x7C0 trigger collision             | low      | inherent |
421	| L13 | CSR marker must be 32-bit               | low      | documented |
422	| L14 | SimPoint estimate is approximate        | medium   | by design |
423	| L15 | No value-level handoff check            | medium   | open   |
424	| L16 | CSR restore silently skipped if missing | medium   | removed |
425	| L17 | Fixed gdbstub timeout + racy port       | low      | removed |
426	| L18 | Little-endian / same-arch only          | low      | by design |
427	| L19 | Determinism / drift / fault-injection   | low      | open   |
428	| L20 | fcsr/frm/fflags not transported         | high     | open   |
429	| L21 | Andes vendor CSRs not transported       | high     | open   |
430	
431	---
432	
433	## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)
434	
435	Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
436	Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
437	gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.
438	
439	**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
440	/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**
441	
442	### Axis breakdown
443	
444	| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
445	|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
446	| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
447	| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, candid `limitation.md`. |
448	| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
449	| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static, no syscalls (L1-L6). |
450	| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
451	| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
452	| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
453	| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, `limitation.md` are unusually honest. |
454	| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |
455	| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |
456	
457	### What blocks commercial shipping
458	
459	1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip (L20)
460	   - an FP workload that touches rounding mode will look numerically
461	   fine but be wrong. `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR restore
462	   is observable only through a private counter
463	   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
464	2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** "M-mode only, no traps, no paging,
465	   no syscalls inside the window" (L1-L6) rules out every real
466	   OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything
467	   with page faults.
468	3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
469	   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
470	   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
471	   controls shape the cycle count.
472	4. **Only 4 CSRs restored into vsim.** `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,
473	   `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into
474	   vsim (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`). They exist in the wire format
475	   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
476	   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
477	5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
478	   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata already ate 16 bytes;
479	   `state_abi.h:85-88`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
480	   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
481	6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
482	   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
483	   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
484	   commercial CI matrix.
485	
486	### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)
487	
488	- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
489	- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
490	- The team writes down what does NOT work (this file, 21 entries plus
491	  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
492	  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
493	- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
494	  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.
495	
496	### Bottom line
497	
498	Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
499	release you need:
500	
501	- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
502	- S-mode + traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4, L6)
503	- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
504	- `fcsr` fix (close L20)
505	- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
506	- A value-level handoff checker (close L15) wired into CI
507	
508	Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.
509

# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. Written 2026-05-28 from a direct read of
the current code (not just the older audit notes).

How this file relates to the others:

- `ROADMAP.md` (top level) - the master feature roadmap. Every open
  limitation below is absorbed there as an `F-ENG-*` feature; that file is
  the *plan to fix*. This file stays the *plain-English "do not do this"
  list* and the source of the L-ids.
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - the older failure-mode backlog (`F-T*`) and the
  gem5-parity bug-audit wave (`B1-B20`, fully closed), both superseded by
  `ROADMAP.md`. Kept for history.

Each entry below was checked against the code on 2026-05-28. The `Where`
line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.

---

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:60-145`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`) MUST
be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No system calls / semihosting
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO (UART, PLIC, timer, ROM)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

---

## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- `fcsr / frm / fflags` (FP rounding mode + sticky flags). See L20.
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only four CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret` (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[216]` fits about 27 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set (`fcsr`, S-mode trap
CSRs, a chosen Andes microarch subset) in a v2 layout is feasible.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).

---

## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg, before the
  ROI). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:292-295`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:32-42` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN, and only partly documented (CLAUDE.md mentions trap-free +
  PMP-static but not paging).

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values. Also `mepc`/
  trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap handling inside
  the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:71-109` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside.
- What happens: `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and `fflags[4:0]`) is not
  in `hybrid_state_v1`. The plugin does not drain it; the resume step
  does not restore it; the drain does not read it back. vsim sees the
  reset value (RNE, no flags). FP results inside the ROI use the
  wrong rounding;
  sticky flags after the ROI are wrong.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no `fcsr` field);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no `fcsr` handle in `VcpuRegs`);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no `fcsr` restore).
- Status: OPEN. Concrete next move: add `uint64_t fcsr` from
  `reserved[]`, drain alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is
  enabled, and drain it back at vsim exit.

---

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at the
  trigger boundary.
- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
  `state_drain.hpp:51` and `hybrid_handoff.c:264`. On the vsim side DCSR.prv
  is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. S/U code then raises
  illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:51`, `hybrid_handoff.c:264`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)

- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default 128 MB
  shared memory.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
  corruption.
- Where: orchestrator mmap sizing; `--mmap-size` exists but nothing validates
  ELF size against it.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mmap-size` large enough by hand.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
  both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI is not handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches UART (`putchar`), PLIC, the timer, ROM, or
  any aliased/device memory.
- What happens: the Phase-5 interconnect watch was never built. Writes to
  MMIO ranges either vanish or hit RAM as if they were normal memory.
- Where: no allowlist/watch in the platform interconnect.
- Status: OPEN.

---

## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. The whole pipeline is hard-wired to one CPU

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU other than
  `andes-ax45mpv`, or any VLEN other than 512.
- What happens: the QEMU spawn passes `-machine andes_ae350` and
  `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` literally (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`).
  The V-register scratch address is the constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000`
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), which is only correct when RAM base is 0 (true
  for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt` where it would need 0x80FF0000).
  The shared-memory base defaults to 0 in `spawn.py`. Nothing parameterizes
  these per machine.
- Where: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:38-42`.
- Status: by design for now; blocks porting to another core.

### L11. VLEN is fixed at 512 bits, and a mismatch is silent  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: a fixture built for a different VLEN than the vsim config,
  or any future config change to VLEN.
- What happens: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per vector register
  (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`). There is no runtime check
  that `vlenb` from QEMU equals `vlenb` in vsim. If they differ, the upper
  bytes of each V register are uninitialized scratch -> garbage in the V
  regfile. The constant is also duplicated in `checkpoint.py:44`
  (`LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`) and can drift from `spawn.py`.
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `checkpoint.py:44`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0

- When it bites: a workload that legitimately writes CSR `0x7C0` with
  immediate 0 or 1.
- What happens: the default (CSR) mode treats `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` as ROI entry
  and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` as exit. A real write to that CSR would false-trigger
  a handoff. (0x7C0 is a benign vendor CSR on ax45mp, so this is unlikely in
  practice, but it is a hard assumption.)
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` CSR matcher; `csr_trigger.hpp`.
- Status: inherent to CSR mode. Workaround: use `--mode pc` or `--mode icount`.

### L13. CSR marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18, documented)

- When it bites: never today, but worth knowing.
- What happens: the matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:505-506`). RV32C has no compressed `csrwi`, so this is
  correct now; if a future extension adds a 16-bit CSR write the marker and
  this gate must change together.
- Where: `hybrid_handoff.c:499-506`.
- Status: documented limit, no action needed now.

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you read
  the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
  (`hsim.py:1188-1193`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
     CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py:1122-1202` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
  CSR `0x7C0` is also actively repurposed by the trigger matcher (L12)
  instead of being preserved.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
  software-visible (must round-trip).

---

## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. No value-level check that the handoff copied state correctly  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: those paths only assert exit code and PC range. A wrong
  register value passes silently. There is no `g`-packet readback compared
  against the drained state.
- Where: `hsim.py` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: OPEN. This is the cheapest high-value fix (see
  `docs/archive/TODO.md` "next moves", or `ROADMAP.md` F-ENG-01).

### L16. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] CSR restore to QEMU2 is silently skipped if the stub omits the name

- When it bites: a QEMU build whose feature XML does not advertise some CSR
  (e.g. `medeleg`, `satp`, `mie`).
- What happens: GPRs and PC hard-fail if missing, but every CSR/PMP/V write
  goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns quietly when the name is not
  found (`gdbstub.py:251-258`). That CSR keeps QEMU2's reset value with no
  warning. The asymmetry (hard-fail GPR vs silent-skip CSR) is the hazard.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:251-258`, used at `gdbstub.py:299-305`.
- Status: REMOVED - the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09.

### L17. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] gdbstub handback uses a fixed 10 s timeout and a racy port pick

- When it bites: QEMU2 slow to answer under host load; or many parallel runs
  (the `JOBS=8` e2e runner) picking ports at the same time.
- What happens: `RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0` is hardcoded (`gdbstub.py:135`); a slow
  reply raises mid-restore and the run dies. `pick_free_port` binds port 0,
  reads the number, closes, then QEMU binds it later - a TOCTOU window where
  another process can grab the port (`spawn.py`, acknowledged in its
  comment). Wrong-port connect = hang until timeout.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:135`, `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`.
- Status: REMOVED - the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing hosts
  with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no byte-swap
  path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror uses a native-endian
  `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:30`), so a BE host would mis-parse the body
  while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:30`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] A QEMU2 that
  launches but never answers the gdbstub can be left as a zombie (no
  SIGALRM watchdog around the handshake).
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

---

## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)

The QEMU2 handback leg has been removed entirely (2026-06-09). The
simulator is now 2-phase: QEMU1 drains architectural state to the
`hybrid_state_v1` file and exits; vsim resumes from that file, runs the
ROI cycle-accurately, and drains again. There is no third phase. Any
docs (`CLAUDE.md`, older architecture notes) that still describe
`verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`, a QEMU2 spawn, or a gdbstub
P-packet restore are stale - that code path no longer exists.

---

## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, candid `limitation.md`. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static, no syscalls (L1-L6). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, `limitation.md` are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip (L20)
   - an FP workload that touches rounding mode will look numerically
   fine but be wrong. `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR restore
   is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** "M-mode only, no traps, no paging,
   no syscalls inside the window" (L1-L6) rules out every real
   OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything
   with page faults.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 4 CSRs restored into vsim.** `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,
   `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into
   vsim (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`). They exist in the wire format
   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata already ate 16 bytes;
   `state_abi.h:85-88`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this file, 21 entries plus
  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- S-mode + traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4, L6)
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- `fcsr` fix (close L20)
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- A value-level handoff checker (close L15) wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.

input.old_string:
### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg, before the
  ROI). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.
input.new_string:

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`,
  when linked against the default semihosting runtime (`-lgloss_vh`).
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple

- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);

- Status: MITIGATED (2026-06). Semihosting inside the ROI is still fatal,

  `runtime/`, link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`) routes

  `tests/vplat/`). For semihosting-linked binaries the old rule stands:
  keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg, before the ROI).

input.old_string:
### L11. VLEN is fixed at 512 bits, and a mismatch is silent  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: a fixture built for a different VLEN than the vsim config,
  or any future config change to VLEN.
- What happens: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per vector register
  (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`). There is no runtime check
  that `vlenb` from QEMU equals `vlenb` in vsim. If they differ, the upper
  bytes of each V register are uninitialized scratch -> garbage in the V
  regfile. The constant is also duplicated in `checkpoint.py:44`
  (`LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`) and can drift from `spawn.py`.
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `checkpoint.py:44`.
- Status: OPEN.
input.new_string:
### L11. VLEN ceiling is 512 bits, and an over-limit vlenb truncates silently  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: an engine whose VLEN exceeds 512, or a run outside the
  driver where the two legs' VLEN configs are set by hand.
- What happens: inside `andes-sim run` the QEMU leg's vlen is copied from
  the engine descriptor (the `{vlen}` template,
  `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`), so the two legs can no longer disagree
  by construction. What remains: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per
  vector register (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`) and the
  plugin CLAMPS the drained bytes to that with no warning
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:375-377`) - a VLEN > 512 engine silently loses the
  upper bytes of every V register. The standalone fast model also hardcodes
  `vlen=512` (`engine_registry.cpp:54`). The retired Python golden keeps a
  duplicated constant (`checkpoint.py:44`, `LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`).
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `hybrid_handoff.c:375-377`,
  `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: leg-mismatch half CLOSED by the descriptor sync (2026-06); the
  512-bit ceiling and the silent clamp remain OPEN.

### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0

input.old_string:
### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0

- When it bites: a workload that legitimately writes CSR `0x7C0` with
  immediate 0 or 1.
- What happens: the default (CSR) mode treats `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` as ROI entry
  and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` as exit. A real write to that CSR would false-trigger
  a handoff. (0x7C0 is a benign vendor CSR on ax45mp, so this is unlikely in
  practice, but it is a hard assumption.)
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` CSR matcher; `csr_trigger.hpp`.
- Status: inherent to CSR mode. Workaround: use `--mode pc` or `--mode icount`.

### L13. CSR marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18, documented)

- When it bites: never today, but worth knowing.
- What happens: the matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:505-506`). RV32C has no compressed `csrwi`, so this is
  correct now; if a future extension adds a 16-bit CSR write the marker and
  this gate must change together.
- Where: `hybrid_handoff.c:499-506`.
- Status: documented limit, no action needed now.
input.new_string:
### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andes_sim/roi.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:663-671` (marker matcher);
  `verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:663-671`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

---
# Hybrid Simulator User Guide

Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
not study its internals. After this guide you can:

1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
3. Pick a switching mode (one of four) and run one handoff end-to-end
   with a concrete worked example.

For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.

---

## 0. The one-paragraph mental model

QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
`mmap` file. A magic trigger (CSR write, PC, instruction count, or SimPoint phase)
hands control between them. One run is two legs:

```
   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
```

The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
mode".

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb: the limitations of the hybrid
simulator as of 2026-06-12, with executed evidence cells."""
import json, os, subprocess

ROOT = "/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim"
NB = os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", "andes_sim_limitations.ipynb")

def md(text):
    return {"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {},
            "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

def code(text):
    return {"cell_type": "code", "metadata": {}, "execution_count": None,
            "outputs": [], "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

cells = []

cells.append(md("""\
# andes-sim: current limitations

What the hybrid simulator CANNOT do today, shown with live evidence from
this repo. Status date: **2026-06-12**.

This notebook is the hands-on companion to `docs/limitation.md` - that file
holds the full list (L-ids, exact `file:line` proof, and the commercial
scorecard). Here we keep the plain-English story and actually run the proof
commands for the items that matter most.

The mental model: a hybrid run is two legs. QEMU runs the boring part fast;
vsim (the RTL simulator) runs your region of interest (ROI) cycle-accurately.
At the handoff, a state file plus a shared RAM mmap carry the CPU state from
QEMU into vsim. Every limitation below comes from one fact: **only part of
the CPU state makes that jump.**"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Setup

Prerequisites: the driver, the simulators, and the test fixtures are already
built (`build/andes-sim`, `verilator/build/sim_*`, `build/qemu/...`, the QEMU
plugin, and `tests/fixtures/*.elf`). If any are missing, run
`source ./setup.sh` from the repo root."""))

cells.append(code("""\
import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andes-sim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## 1. The one rule: the measured window is narrow

The resume step writes back GPRs, FPRs, the V registers, the PC - and only
FOUR machine CSRs: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret` (plus the V
CSRs). Nothing else exists inside vsim's ROI.

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is missing: no `satp`, no `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`, no PMP, no `fcsr`."""))

cells.append(code("""\
!grep -n "static constexpr uint16_t kCsr" verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp"""))

cells.append(md("""\
So the code between `andes_sim_roi_begin()` and `andes_sim_roi_end()` must
be (the L-ids point into `docs/limitation.md`):

- **M-mode only** (L6) - both sides hardcode privilege = 3
- **no paging** (L3) - `satp` is never restored; every address is physical
- **trap-free** (L4) - the trap CSRs in the drained state are stale
  passthrough values, and trap handling inside the ROI starts from reset
- **PMP-static** (L2) - PMP is drained into the state file but never
  restored into vsim
- **no LR/SC across the boundary** (L5) - the reservation is not in the
  wire format, so a `sc` after the handoff always fails
- **default FP rounding only** (L20) - `fcsr` (frm + fflags) never
  round-trips; a non-default rounding mode is silently lost
- **no semihosting** (L1) - vsim has no semihosting handler; one `printf`
  from the semihosting runtime inside the ROI = infinite trap loop

Step outside this envelope and the result is silently wrong or the run
hangs. All of these are still OPEN - except the last one, which now has a
supported escape hatch."""))

cells.append(md("""\
## 2. The escape hatch that ships: the vplat runtime

I/O inside the ROI used to be impossible (L1 + L9). The vplat runtime
(link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`) routes stdio to a
real UART, `exit()` to the SimControl device, and file io to HTIF. Both
engines model these devices, so the SAME ELF runs on `fast`, `cycle`, AND
`hybrid` - and a `printf` inside the ROI works (it just adds the real UART
cycles to the figure). See USER_GUIDE section 5.

Proof - `vplat_hello.elf` prints from INSIDE the measured window, serviced
by the vsim leg:"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc \\
    --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"""))

cells.append(md("""\
The `hello from vplat` line was printed by cycle-accurate RTL simulation,
and the run still produced a clean `window_cycles` figure.

What this does NOT lift: only UART2 (`0xf0300000`) and SimControl/HTIF
(`0xe0080000`) are modeled by both engines. Any other device (PLIC, timer,
ROM) inside the ROI is still undefined behavior, and no device state (UART
FIFO, pending interrupts, timer compare) crosses the handoff - only RAM is
shared (L9, partial)."""))

cells.append(md("""\
## 3. Scale limits

| Limit | Today | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Privilege (L6) | M-mode forced on both sides; S/U-mode workloads trap-loop | open |
| Memory (L7) | 128 MB default mmap; `--mem-size` overrides, but nothing checks the ELF fits | open |
| Harts (L8) | one hart only; hart 1+ is rejected | open |
| MMIO (L9) | vplat device set only; device state never crosses the handoff | partial |

The M-mode hardcode is one line on each side of the handoff:"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!grep -n "priv" verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c | grep "= 3" """))

cells.append(md("""\
## 4. Configuration and accuracy

Better than the last audit (2026-05-28):

- **Engines are drop-in now.** `andes-sim list engines`, `--engine ID`,
  discovered via `--describe`. The QEMU leg copies VLEN from the chosen
  engine's descriptor, so the two legs cannot disagree by construction
  (L10/L11, partial).
- **The CSR-write trigger is gone.** ROI markers are now
  `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` HINTs - architectural NOPs, safe on every
  engine and on silicon, no CSR repurposed (L12/L13, resolved).

Still fixed in place:

- machine `andes_ae350`, CPU family `andes-ax45mpv`, and the V-scratch
  address `0x00FF0000` (assumes RAM base 0) - porting to another core is
  blocked (L10)
- VLEN ceiling is 512: the wire format holds 64 bytes per V register and
  the plugin clamps anything larger with no warning (L11)
- the SimPoint figure is a weighted estimate, not a measurement, and the
  SimPoint pipeline still runs only on the Python golden `./hsim.py` (L14)
- zero Andes vendor CSRs are transported; cache and prefetcher controls
  shape the cycle count, so this is an accuracy hazard (L21)"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## 5. How much can you trust a figure?

Cross-checks that exist today (dev tier, `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1`):

- `run --verify` (marker/pc) re-runs the ELF on a pure-QEMU oracle and
  diffs the FULL drained state field by field.
- `run --cosim [--cosim-interval N]` drains checkpoints every N retires and
  localizes a divergence to the first bad window. It suppresses the cycle
  figure (the checkpoint drains pollute it); re-run without `--cosim` to
  measure.

Remaining gaps:

- the icount trigger and the SimPoint pipeline still check only exit code
  and PC range - a wrong register value there passes silently (L15, partial)
- the wire format is little-endian, same-arch only (x86-64 host) (L18)
- no determinism, version-drift, or fault-injection gates (L19)"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Status at a glance (2026-06-12)

| Area | Status |
|---|---|
| Semihosting in ROI (L1) | fatal; the vplat runtime is the supported I/O path |
| PMP / paging / traps / LR-SC / fcsr in ROI (L2-L5, L20) | open |
| M-mode only, single hart, no mmap bounds check (L6-L8) | open |

def code(text):

            "outputs": [], "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

cells = []

cells.append(md("""\
# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. First written 2026-05-28 as
`docs/limitation.md`; re-checked entry by entry against the code and moved
into this notebook on **2026-06-12** (line references refreshed; statuses
updated where the code moved).

How this notebook relates to the other docs:

- `ROADMAP.md` (top level) - the master feature roadmap. Every open
  limitation below is absorbed there as an `F-ENG-*` feature; that file is
  the *plan to fix*. This notebook stays the *plain-English "do not do
  this" list* and the source of the L-ids.
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - the older failure-mode backlog (`F-T*`) and the
  gem5-parity bug-audit wave (`B1-B20`, fully closed), both superseded by
  `ROADMAP.md`. Kept for history.

Each `Where` line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.
The code cells run real commands against this repo, so the key claims are
shown, not just stated."""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Setup

Prerequisites: the driver, the simulators, and the test fixtures are already
built (`build/andes-sim`, `verilator/build/sim_*`, `build/qemu/...`, the
QEMU plugin, and `tests/fixtures/*.elf`). If any are missing, run
`source ./setup.sh` from the repo root."""))

cells.append(code("""\
import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andes-sim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:69-153`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is missing: no `satp`, no `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`, no PMP, no `fcsr`."""))

cells.append(code("""\
!grep -n "static constexpr uint16_t kCsr" verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp"""))

cells.append(md("""\
So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`)
MUST be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No semihosting (exception: the vplat runtime's MMIO-backed
  stdio / exit / file io is supported inside the ROI, see L1)
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO other than the vplat device set, UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (see L9)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below."""))

cells.append(md("""\
## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- `fcsr / frm / fflags` (FP rounding mode + sticky flags). See L20.
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only four CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret` (`resume_driver.hpp:69-153`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[216]` fits about 27 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set (`fcsr`, S-mode trap
CSRs, a chosen Andes microarch subset) in a v2 layout is feasible.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."""))

  (`-lgloss_vh`).
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);

## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- `fcsr / frm / fflags` (FP rounding mode + sticky flags). See L20.
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only four CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret` (`resume_driver.hpp:69-153`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[216]` fits about 27 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set (`fcsr`, S-mode trap
CSRs, a chosen Andes microarch subset) in a v2 layout is feasible.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."""))

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:343-345`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.
  Also `mepc`/trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap
  handling inside the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:73-111` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside.
- What happens: `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and `fflags[4:0]`) is not
  in `hybrid_state_v1`. The plugin does not drain it; the resume step
  does not restore it; the drain does not read it back. vsim sees the
  reset value (RNE, no flags). FP results inside the ROI use the wrong
  rounding; sticky flags after the ROI are wrong.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no `fcsr` field);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no `fcsr` handle in `VcpuRegs`);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no `fcsr` restore).
- Status: OPEN. Concrete next move: add `uint64_t fcsr` from
  `reserved[]`, drain alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is
  enabled, and drain it back at vsim exit."""))

- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to

  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them

  on its own (users get them from `<andes_sim/roi.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.

- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,

- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you
  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary (`hsim.py:1126-1225`,
  `_run_simpoint_pipeline`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at
     each window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without
     warmup the CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate
     inherits SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py:1126-1225` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`). Note: SimPoint
  still runs only on the Python golden (`./hsim.py`); the C++ port has not
  landed.
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
  software-visible (must round-trip)."""))
