name: cosim-roi
description: "Checkpoint co-sim shipped 2026-06-12: run --cosim (dev) drains vsim checkpoints every N retires, QEMU oracle drains at the same minstret deltas, state-diff per window; mmap stays Shared"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e41bc0d4-d741-42b4-ba15-e56e60fb3e8e
---

Checkpoint co-simulation (roadmap: cosim_roi.md in repo root, all F1-F4
done 2026-06-12). `run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc --cosim
[--cosim-interval N]` (dev tier, default N=10000): vsim drains a
RESUMABLE checkpoint every N retires (StateDrain::drain_checkpoint undoes
the V-sweep clobbers vtype/vl/vstart/x5-x7 before resumereq); the driver
re-runs the ELF on a pure-QEMU oracle (plugin cosim_marker/cosim_pc +
cosim_counts=minstret deltas) and diffs window by window.

Key design facts:
- window_cycles and --cosim are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE (d0b9481, PM decision
  2026-06-12): checkpoint drains pollute the mcycle delta (22530 for a
  1692-retire ROI), so the driver suppresses the figure under --cosim.
- Register-only compare is final: PM rejected per-load/store and
  per-checkpoint memory co-sim (vsim has no LSU tap; L1D write-back vs
  mmap snapshot was the open question).
- Alignment is by minstret delta, not pc (loop-safe; halt slack absorbed).
  Empirically minstret is NOT contaminated by Program Buffer execution in
  debug mode (ckpt delta exactly 1000 on a V workload).
- mmap stays MAP_SHARED. Private COW is a trap (un-COW'd pages see the
  other process's writes); the oracle simply replays from boot on its own
  RAM. See [[vsim-halt-slack]] and [[hsim-cpp-rewrite]].
- pc-trigger mode: the boundary insn counts as retire #1 on both sides
  (the pc handoff resumes AT the boundary; marker is counted by neither).
- Known edge: a checkpoint whose halt slack crosses the EXIT marker loses
  the exit retire (the run loop is blocked inside the drain) -- tiny
  intervals on tiny ROIs can crash with cmderr=4. Documented limitation.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tutorial 4f follow-up: --cosim now suppresses window_cycles.
Rewrite the limitation bullet and re-execute the --cosim cell."""
import json, os, subprocess

ROOT = "/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim"
NB = os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", "andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb")

nb = json.load(open(NB))
cells = nb["cells"]

run_cell = next(c for c in cells if c["cell_type"] == "code"
                and "--cosim --cosim-interval 500" in "".join(c["source"]))
md_after = next(c for c in cells if c["cell_type"] == "markdown"
                and "The cycle figure is polluted." in "".join(c["source"]))

old = """- **The cycle figure is polluted.** Every checkpoint adds a DMI
  halt + drain + resume on the vsim leg, so `window_cycles` under
  `--cosim` is approximate. Re-measure without `--cosim` for the real
  figure.
"""
new = """- **No cycle figure.** Every checkpoint adds a DMI halt + drain + resume
  on the vsim leg, which pollutes the vsim `mcycle` delta, so `--cosim`
  suppresses `window_cycles` entirely. Re-run without `--cosim` to
  measure.
"""
src = "".join(md_after["source"])
assert old in src, "bullet not found"
md_after["source"] = src.replace(old, new).splitlines(keepends=True)

env = dict(os.environ)
env["PATH"] = f"{ROOT}/build:" + env["PATH"]
script = "".join(run_cell["source"]).lstrip()[1:]
proc = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script], cwd=ROOT, env=env, text=True,
                      timeout=600, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                      stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
if proc.returncode != 0:
    raise SystemExit(f"cosim cell failed (rc={proc.returncode}):\n{proc.stdout}")
assert "[cosim] PASS: 3 checkpoint(s)" in proc.stdout, proc.stdout
assert "window_cycles" not in proc.stdout, proc.stdout
run_cell["outputs"] = [{"name": "stdout", "output_type": "stream",
                        "text": proc.stdout.splitlines(keepends=True)}]

with open(NB, "w") as f:
    json.dump(nb, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    f.write("\n")
print(f"bullet rewritten; cosim cell re-run, {len(proc.stdout)} bytes, "
      "no window_cycles")

# cosim_roi -- checkpoint co-simulation between QEMU and vsim inside the ROI

Status: ACCEPTED (PM decision, 2026-06-12): Option A (checkpoint co-sim).
  1. Dev tier (debug tool, hidden from release help like state-diff).
  2. Default checkpoint interval N=10000; `--cosim-interval <N>` overrides.
  3. Trigger scope: marker|pc only (same as --verify).

## Problem

`--verify` (verify_oracle.md) compares only the FINAL state at the ROI exit.
When it fails, we know the vsim leg diverged somewhere inside the ROI, but not
where. Checkpoint co-sim drains and compares the architectural state every N
retired instructions, so a divergence is localized to the first bad
N-instruction window. Rerun with smaller N to narrow it.

## Flow

```
Run 1 (hybrid):  QEMU1 -> vsim: ..N insns..|..N insns..|.. exit
                                  ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final drain
Run 2 (oracle):  pure QEMU from boot: arm at ROI entry, drain at the SAME
                 retire counts ->     ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final
diff ckpt k vs ckpt k (existing state_diff policy); first mismatch = window k.
```

Alignment is by RETIRE COUNT, not pc: vsim's DMI halt overshoots 0-3
instructions (halt slack, see verify_oracle.md "Boundary semantics"), and pc
alignment is ambiguous inside loops. vsim restores minstret from QEMU1's
drained value at entry, so `ckpt.minstret - entry.minstret` is the exact
number of post-entry retires; the oracle plugin counts exec callbacks after
arming and drains at those exact deltas. pc then matches by construction
when execution is correct, and diverges loudly when it is not.

## Memory: keep the mmap Shared, do NOT flip to Private

- Today: QEMU writes guest RAM through `-object memory-backend-file,share=on`;
  vsim maps the same file `MAP_SHARED | MAP_POPULATE`
  (verilator/src/platform/mmap_backing.hpp:34). This stays unchanged.
- vsim Private, QEMU shared: Linux private file mappings are copy-on-write
  PER PAGE; un-written pages still show the live file, so the other engine's
  stores leak in until the first local write. Nondeterministic contamination.
- QEMU Private (share=off): pre-ROI writes never reach the file; vsim resumes
  on stale memory. The handoff breaks.
- Resolution: the two runs never share memory at all. The oracle is a
  separate QEMU process re-running the same ELF from boot on its own RAM
  (exactly like --verify); pre-ROI determinism is already proven by the
  VERIFY=1 gate (35/35 identical entry states).

## Design notes (from code reading)

- vsim exit drain today: simulator.hpp check_hybrid_handoff -> on_retire(pc)
  -> StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough -> write file -> exit 200. Abstract
  reads are non-destructive, BUT the trailing V data sweep (vse8.v via the
  Program Buffer) clobbers vtype/vl/vstart and x5/x6/x7. The exit drain never
  resumes, so the clobbers are free. A CHECKPOINT drain resumes, so it must
  undo them from the freshly drained values (vsetvl restore staging x5/x6,
  then vstart, then rewrite x5/x6/x7), then resumereq + poll allresumeack.
  All primitives exist (resume_driver.hpp, program_buffer.hpp).
- Known risks (empirical, the F4 gate decides):
  - minstret during debug mode: if Program Buffer instructions (V sweep +
    clobber undo) increment minstret, later checkpoints' deltas inflate and
    the oracle drains late. Fix if observed: set dcsr.stopcount at halt.
    Non-V fixtures are clean either way (abstract commands only).
  - mcycle during the checkpoint halts inflates window_cycles (observed:
    22530 for a 1692-retire ROI); the driver therefore suppresses the
    window_cycles line under --cosim -- the two are mutually exclusive
    (PM decision 2026-06-12). Re-run without --cosim to measure.

## F1: vsim resumable checkpoint drain
State: done
Description: `StateDrain::drain_checkpoint(input)` -- drain_with_passthrough,
then (V flag only) undo the sweep clobbers using the drained values:
stage x5=vl, x6=vtype, exec `vsetvl x0,x5,x6` in the Program Buffer, write
vstart (after vsetvl: vsetvl zeroes it), rewrite x5/x6/x7 from the drained
GPRs; finally resumereq + poll allresumeack. Hart continues where it halted
(DPC untouched). Unit tests on the recording-bus double assert the write
sequence and that the returned state equals the plain drain.
Key files: verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp,
verilator/tests/hybrid/state_drain.test.cpp
Dependencies: none

## F2: vsim --hybrid-cosim N (checkpoint loop + numbered files)
State: done
Description: HandoffController counts retires; every N (monotonic target, not
modulo) it calls drain_checkpoint and hands the state to a sink callback;
the exit trigger still wins on the same retire and keeps today's semantics.
simulator.hpp provides the sink: V-merge from scratch (read_v_from_scratch)
then write `<handoff_out>.ckpt<k>` (k from 1). New CLI arg `--hybrid-cosim
<N>` (main.cpp), valid only with --resume-from-qemu + marker/pc trigger
(error with --hybrid-icount). Controller unit tests with a fake trigger +
recording bus; manual two-leg smoke (QEMU1 then vsim --hybrid-cosim) checks
.ckpt files appear with ascending minstret.
Key files: verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp, verilator/src/simulator.hpp,
verilator/src/main.cpp, verilator/tests/hybrid/handoff_controller.test.cpp
Dependencies: F1

## F3: plugin cosim oracle mode (counted multi-drain)
State: done
Description: new plugin args, exclusive with all other trigger modes:
  cosim_marker=1      arm on the ENTER marker `slti x0,x0,0x5A0`
  cosim_pc=0x...      arm on an explicit entry boundary vaddr
  cosim_counts=a:b:c  ascending post-entry retire deltas (colon-separated);
                      each but the last drains to `<outfile>.ckpt<k>` and
                      continues; the LAST drains to `<outfile>` and exits 200
Counting: exec callbacks fire pre-execution; at the m-th post-arm callback
exactly m-1 post-entry instructions have retired, so drain when the running
count equals the target (check-then-increment), capturing pc = next-insn
vaddr -- the same point as vsim's DPC. The entry marker itself is counted by
NEITHER side (QEMU1 drains pre-marker, vsim resumes past it).
Key files: qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c,
tests/plugin/test_plugin_cosim_drain.sh (new)
Dependencies: none

## F4: andes-sim run --cosim (default off, Dev)
State: done
Description: `--cosim` on `run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc` (+
`--cosim-interval <N>`, default 10000; --cosim-interval without --cosim,
--cosim with fast/cycle/icount, and --cosim with --verify are usage errors;
--cosim already subsumes the final-state check). Flow: hybrid plan runs with
the vsim leg carrying `--hybrid-cosim N` (Trigger param -> leg_trigger_args);
run_plan collects `<outfile>.ckpt<k>` into PhaseResult.checkpoints before
workdir cleanup; the driver computes minstret deltas vs the entry state,
runs the one-step oracle plan (fresh mmap, cosim_marker/cosim_pc +
cosim_counts), diffs ckpt k vs ckpt k then final vs final via diff_states,
and reports `[cosim] PASS: <K> checkpoints + final state match` or the first
diverging window `[cosim] FAIL: divergence in window <k> (retires <lo>..<hi>
after entry)` plus the field diffs, rc 1.
Gate: cosim e2e green on rt_c_hello (no V), rt_c_matmul (FP), rt_c_v_regs +
rt_c_v_matmul (V) -- this empirically settles the minstret/debug-mode risk.
Key files: driver/cli.hpp/.cpp, driver/plan.hpp, driver/run_plan.cpp,
driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/main.cpp (dev help),
tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_cosim.sh (new)
Dependencies: F1, F2, F3 (and F2's state-diff core from verify_oracle)

## Docs
Each feature updates docs/USER_GUIDE.md in its own change set: F3 adds the
plugin-arg rows (2.3), F4 adds the dev-facing --cosim subsection next to
--verify (what it localizes, the masking rule, why window_cycles is
approximate under --cosim).

## Rejected: Option B (streaming trace-compare)
Both engines stream per-retire records into shm rings; exact localization but
vsim's retire hook is pc-only (`on_retire(uint64_t pc)`, simulator.hpp:504; no
RVFI/writeback trace), so full value compare needs new RTL probing. Revisit
only if window-bracketing proves too coarse.

content.text:
Mostly right, with one nuance. The vplat runtime (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) implements the full newlib syscall surface engine-blind: stdio goes to UART2, `exit` to SimControl, and file io (open/read/write/stat/seek/unlink/rename/getcwd/gettimeofday...) to HTIF magicmem - all devices both engines model. `sbrk` is pure local memory. So a vplat-linked binary can call any libc function inside the ROI and it works on fast, cycle, and hybrid.

Two reasons L1 stays in the doc as "mitigated", not "gone":

1. **It is opt-in by link choice.** Only binaries linked with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs` get vplat. The older `rt_c_*` fixtures (and any user binary linked with `-lgloss_vh`) still use semihosting, and a semihosting call inside the ROI still traps in vsim. The rule still protects those users.
2. **Cost, not correctness.** A syscall inside the ROI now works, but its real cycles (UART polling loop, dcache flush, HTIF handshake) land in `window_cycles`. Fine for debugging, noise for measurement.

So the practical guidance is: link vplat and L1 stops being a blocker; it only remains a rule for legacy semihosting-linked binaries.

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andes-sim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andes-sim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andes-sim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul

# vplat fixtures: same source runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. They link
# libandes_sim_runtime.a instead of -lgloss_vh: stdio goes out the
# ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through the SimControl device at
# 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's andes_ae350 and vsim model. No
# semihosting anywhere, so the Phase-2 "no syscalls on vsim" cliff
# disappears for these binaries.
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
# vplat: built THROUGH the shipped runtime library with the same two-flag
# command users type (-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs), so the
# suites regression-test the real artifact. No libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs.
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andes_sim/roi.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andes-sim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andes-sim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T $(LDSCRIPT) \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T $(LDSCRIPT) \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# vplat fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT_DIR).
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/roi.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same flags/libs/linker as the marked V
# fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS \
	  -T $(LDSCRIPT) $(RUNTIME_SRCS) rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

content.text: Now the e2e harness and the fixture helpers, to see how output and exit are asserted:

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
13	#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
14	#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
15	#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
16	#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
17	#                   relies on this; ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly.
18	#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
19	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
20	#   VERIFY=1        opt-in differential verification (default off): re-run
21	#                   the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at the ROI
22	#                   exit boundary (the oracle), then `andes-sim state-diff`
23	#                   the oracle state against the vsim drain. Any divergence
24	#                   in what vsim freshly drains (pc/GPRs/FPRs/V) fails the
25	#                   test; counters and passthrough CSRs are excluded.
26	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
27	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
28	#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
29	#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
30	#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
31	#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
32	#                              pair from the drained state file.
33	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
34	
35	set -euo pipefail
36	
37	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
38	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
39	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
40	
41	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
42	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
43	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
44	
45	hybrid_resolve_paths
46	
47	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
48	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
49	
50	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
51	  marker) ;;
52	  pc)
53	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
54	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
55	      exit 77
56	    fi
57	    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
58	    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
59	    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
60	    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
61	    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
62	    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
63	    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
64	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
65	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
66	      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
67	         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
68	        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
69	        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
70	        export ROI_START ROI_END
71	      fi
72	    fi
73	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
74	    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
75	    ;;
76	  *)
77	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
78	    exit 1
79	    ;;
80	esac
81	
82	# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
83	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
84	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
85	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
86	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
87	STATE_ORACLE=$(mktemp)
88	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   VERIFY=1        opt-in differential verification (default off): re-run
#                   the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at the ROI
#                   exit boundary (the oracle), then `andes-sim state-diff`
#                   the oracle state against the vsim drain. Any divergence
#                   in what vsim freshly drains (pc/GPRs/FPRs/V) fails the
#                   test; counters and passthrough CSRs are excluded.
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
#                              pair from the drained state file.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
STATE_ORACLE=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$STATE_ORACLE" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13):
  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@3392, minstret_at_measure_start@3400.
  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 3392 "$STATE_VSIM")
    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 3400 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

# verify_oracle F3 (opt-in, default off): differential check against a
# pure-QEMU oracle. The same ELF re-runs on QEMU alone -- clean memory, so
# NO shared mmap (reusing it would leak the hybrid run's post-ROI bytes
# into the oracle's boot) -- with the plugin draining at the ROI exit
# boundary. state-diff then compares everything vsim freshly drains.
if [ "${VERIFY:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  ANDES_SIM_BIN="${ANDES_SIM_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/build/andes-sim}"
  if [ ! -x "$ANDES_SIM_BIN" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: VERIFY=1 needs $ANDES_SIM_BIN (run scripts/build_driver.sh)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ORACLE_TRIG="exit_marker=1"
  [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ] && ORACLE_TRIG="exit_pc=0x$EXIT_PC"
  # Sample at vsim's ACTUAL halt point: the DMI halt lands a variable 0-3
  # insns past the trigger, so the oracle must drain at the pc vsim's state
  # file reports (offset 16, locked by state_abi_check.h), not at trigger+1.
  VSIM_PC=$(printf '0x%x' "$(read_u64_le 16 "$STATE_VSIM")")
  ORACLE_TRIG="$ORACLE_TRIG,drain_pc=$VSIM_PC"

  echo "[$FIXTURE verify mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] oracle: pure QEMU drains at ROI exit (pc=$VSIM_PC)"
  set +e
  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -machine andes_ae350 \
    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_ORACLE,$ORACLE_TRIG" \
    </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
  ORACLE_RC=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$ORACLE_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: oracle QEMU expected exit 200 on drain, got $ORACLE_RC"
    exit 1
  fi

  set +e
  DIFF_OUT=$("$ANDES_SIM_BIN" state-diff "$STATE_ORACLE" "$STATE_VSIM" 2>&1)
  DIFF_RC=$?
  set -e
  printf '%s\n' "$DIFF_OUT"
  if [ "$DIFF_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim drain diverges from the QEMU oracle"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "[$FIXTURE verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle"
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

1	/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
2	 *
3	 * Phase rule:
4	 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
5	 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
6	 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
7	 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
8	 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
9	 *   to register/memory work only.
10	 *
11	 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
12	 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
13	 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
14	 */
15	
16	#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
17	#define RT_C_HELPERS_H
18	
19	/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers: the HINT pair
20	 * `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (ENTER) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (EXIT). Match
21	 * insn_match.h. rd=x0 makes each marker an architectural NOP, so marked
22	 * binaries also run standalone on every engine.
23	 *
24	 * marker mode pattern-matches the HINT insns directly; the helpers do not
25	 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
26	 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
27	 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */
28	/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
29	 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
30	 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
31	 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
32	 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
33	 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
34	 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
35	 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
36	/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
37	 *
38	 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
39	 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
40	 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
41	 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
42	 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
43	 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
44	 * consumes the value.)
45	 *
46	 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
47	 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
48	 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
49	 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
50	 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
51	 *     between the markers.
52	 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
53	 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
54	 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
55	 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
56	 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
57	 * attribution. */

/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
 *
 * Phase rule:
 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
 *   to register/memory work only.
 *
 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
 */

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers: the HINT pair
 * `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (ENTER) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (EXIT). Match
 * insn_match.h. rd=x0 makes each marker an architectural NOP, so marked
 * binaries also run standalone on every engine.
 *
 * marker mode pattern-matches the HINT insns directly; the helpers do not
 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

/* A pure compiler memory barrier (emits no instructions): forces pending
 * memory writes to complete and bars reordering across it. enter_vsim /
 * exit_vsim already carry this clobber on their marker insn, so the markers
 * anchor a kernel's output stores; markerless builds (-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS)
 * call roi_anchor() to pin those stores instead. */
static inline void roi_anchor(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F6 contract: `scripts/run_e2e.sh` works out of the box -- its default
# VSIM_BIN must be the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine
# (sim_ax45mpv_premium, the same default ./andes-sim pins), NOT the
# alphabetically-first verilator/build/sim_* (sim_ax45mpv_mp2, a 2-core
# config where crt0's secondary-hart SKIPPED write stops the sim before
# hart 0 drains and every C fixture fails).
#
# The probe: one marker e2e fixture with NO VSIM_BIN in the environment.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

[ -x "$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium" ] || fail "premium engine not built"
[ -x "$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_mp2" ] \
  || echo "[note] mp2 engine absent; default-pick ambiguity not present on this host"
[ -x "$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not built"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_c_hello.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

unset VSIM_BIN
FILTER='^rt_c_hello$' MODE=marker JOBS=1 bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh" \
  >/tmp/vplat_f6_run.log 2>&1 \
  || fail "default-engine e2e rt_c_hello[marker] failed (picked a multi-hart engine?): $(tail -4 /tmp/vplat_f6_run.log)"

ok "F6 run_e2e.sh default engine is single-hart (rt_c_hello[marker] passes untouched)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED test for F14: `./hsim.py estimate <elf>` always runs the workload to
# its natural exit (semihosting EXIT), drains state in the plugin's
# atexit callback, and uses the plugin-counted retired-insn count as
# N_total in the SimPoint aggregation formula. Run-to-exit is the only
# behavior -- there is no --icount knob to cap the profile.
#
# Workload: tests/fixtures/rt_c_no_trigger_exit.elf. ~50K-100K insns total,
# no ROI markers, exits via libgloss_vh semihosting EXIT.
#
# Pipeline (profile + cluster + per-phase drains) caps at 120s for headroom.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
HSIM="$ROOT/hsim.py"

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_no_trigger_exit.elf"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF (run ./hsim.py build first)"

cd "$ROOT"

# 1. Fixture sanity: must contain zero ROI marker insns
#    (5a002013 = slti x0,x0,0x5A0 enter / 5a102013 = exit).
# Locate the riscv64 objdump (mirrors fixtures/Makefile TOOLCHAIN lookup).
OBJDUMP=""
if [ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -x "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump" ]; then
  OBJDUMP="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"
elif command -v riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  OBJDUMP=$(command -v riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump)
fi
if [ -n "$OBJDUMP" ]; then
  count=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$ELF" 2>/dev/null | grep -cwE '5a002013|5a102013' || true)
  [ "${count:-0}" -eq 0 ] \
    || fail "fixture $ELF has $count ROI marker insn(s); F14 needs zero"
  ok "fixture has zero ROI marker insns"
else
  echo "[skip] objdump not found; skipping marker check"
fi

# 2. estimate --help describes the natural-program-exit profile pass and
#    no longer advertises a --icount flag.
out=$("$HSIM" estimate --help 2>&1) || fail "estimate --help non-zero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -qiE 'natural program exit|exit.*plugin atexit|run to (program )?exit' \
  || fail "estimate --help missing 'natural program exit' hint:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qE -- '--icount' \
  && fail "estimate --help still mentions removed --icount:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimate --help documents run-to-exit profile (no --icount)"

# 3. Real estimate run uses run-to-exit path (no --icount knob to pass).
set +e
out=$(timeout 120 "$HSIM" estimate "$ELF" --slice 1000 --max-k 2 2>&1)
rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "estimate (no --icount) rc=$rc:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimate run exits 0 (no --icount, always run-to-exit)"

# 4. Output has estimated_cycles=<int>, > 0.
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'estimated_cycles=<int>' line:"$'\n'"$out"
EST=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
[ "${EST:-0}" -gt 0 ] \
  || fail "estimated_cycles must be > 0, got '$EST':"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimated_cycles=$EST"

# 5. N_total surfaced in the report line must be > 0 and >> 2000
# (loop iters lower bound; libgloss startup adds more).
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'N=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'N=<int>' in summary line:"$'\n'"$out"
NTOT=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'N=[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
[ "${NTOT:-0}" -gt 2000 ] \
  || fail "N_total must reflect real insn count (>2000), got '$NTOT':"$'\n'"$out"
ok "N_total=$NTOT (from plugin atexit minstret counter)"

# 6. Per-phase rows show delta_mcycle > 0.
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'delta_mcycle=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing per-phase 'delta_mcycle=<int>' rows:"$'\n'"$out"
N_PHASES=$(echo "$out" | grep -cE 'delta_mcycle=[0-9]+')
[ "$N_PHASES" -ge 1 ] \
  || fail "need at least 1 per-phase row, got $N_PHASES:"$'\n'"$out"
while IFS= read -r delta; do
  [ "$delta" -gt 0 ] \
    || fail "delta_mcycle must be > 0, got '$delta':"$'\n'"$out"
done < <(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'delta_mcycle=[0-9]+' | cut -d= -f2)
ok "$N_PHASES per-phase row(s) with delta_mcycle > 0"

# 7. weighted_CPI is sensible (positive, < 100).
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'weighted_CPI=[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'weighted_CPI=<float>' in summary:"$'\n'"$out"
CPI=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'weighted_CPI=[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
awk -v c="$CPI" 'BEGIN { exit (c > 0 && c < 100) ? 0 : 1 }' \
  || fail "weighted_CPI=$CPI out of plausible range:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "weighted_CPI=$CPI in plausible range"

echo "PASS test_hsim_estimate_drain_at_exit"

def _run_drain_at_exit_profile(elf: Path, artifacts: dict[str, Path],
                                bbv: Path, slice_n: int,
                                mmap_size: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Run a profile pass that drains at program exit (no icount cap).

    Returns (rc, n_total_insns). On rc != 0, n_total_insns is 0.

    The plugin's drain_at_exit=1 mode counts every retired insn via a
    per-insn exec cb and overrides the drained state file's `minstret`
    field with that count (QEMU's PMU minstret is host-tick-derived on
    system-mode without -icount, which is why we use the plugin counter).
    """
    shm_path = _load_hsim_shm().allocate(
        mmap_size, prefix="hsim-profile-shm.",
    )
    state_fd, state_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="hsim-profile-state.")
    os.close(state_fd)
    state_out = Path(state_name)
    try:
        argv = _qemu_drain_argv(
            artifacts["qemu"], elf, artifacts["plugin"],
            shm_path, mmap_size, state_out,
            plugin_extras=(
                f"bbv_out={bbv}",
                f"slice={slice_n}",
                "drain_at_exit=1",
            ),
        )
        proc = subprocess.run(
            argv, cwd=REPO_ROOT,
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            timeout=_PROFILE_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        if proc.returncode != _QEMU_DRAIN_RC:
            tail = proc.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()[-20:]
            print(f"hsim: QEMU profile expected exit {_QEMU_DRAIN_RC}, "
                  f"got {proc.returncode}", file=sys.stderr)
            for line in tail:
                print(line, file=sys.stderr)
            return 1, 0

        if not bbv.is_file() or bbv.stat().st_size == 0:
            print(f"hsim: profile produced empty BBV: {bbv}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1, 0

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul

# vplat fixtures: same source runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. They link
# libandes_sim_runtime.a instead of -lgloss_vh: stdio goes out the
# ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through the SimControl device at
# 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's andes_ae350 and vsim model. No
# semihosting anywhere, so the Phase-2 "no syscalls on vsim" cliff
# disappears for these binaries.
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
# vplat: built THROUGH the shipped runtime library with the same two-flag
# command users type (-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs), so the
# suites regression-test the real artifact. No libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs.
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andes_sim/roi.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andes-sim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andes-sim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andes-sim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andes-sim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andes-sim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.

# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andes-sim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andes-sim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andes-sim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandes_sim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime

# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).

                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit

RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \

VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andes_sim/roi.h

VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Oracle exit-drain contract (verify_oracle F1): a pure-QEMU run drains
# hybrid_state_v1 at the ROI EXIT boundary, producing the reference state the
# differential verifier compares against the vsim drain.
#
# Semantics: arm on the exit boundary's exec callback, drain on the NEXT exec
# callback. That callback fires before its own insn executes, so the captured
# state is "after the boundary insn retired" -- exactly what vsim's exit drain
# records (DPC = next insn to execute) -- and the reported pc is the next
# insn's vaddr, correct even for a branching boundary insn.
#
# Cases:
#   1. exit_marker=1  -- arm on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`; pc must be marker+4
#                        (NOT enter-marker+4: the ENTER marker must not drain).
#   2. exit_pc=0x...  -- arm on the boundary vaddr; same expectation when the
#                        boundary is the (fall-through) exit marker.
#   3. drain_pc=0x... -- sample at a later, caller-chosen pc instead of the
#                        very next insn. The differential harness passes
#                        vsim's actual halt pc here: vsim's DMI halt lands a
#                        variable 0-3 insns past the trigger, and both sides
#                        must sample the SAME architectural point.
#   4. exit_marker=1,icount=N -- install error: oracle mode is exclusive with
#                        the other trigger modes; drain_pc requires oracle
#                        mode.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   FIXTURE      a marker-carrying fixture (default: rt_c_hello)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# drain_at_exit contract (F14): when the guest exits NATURALLY (no ROI
# trigger), the plugin's atexit callback writes a count record and exits
# 200. The record's only meaningful payload is minstret = the plugin-side
# per-insn retire counter (N_total for the SimPoint estimate pipeline);
# pc=0 marks "the atexit path drained, no insn context".
#
# The guest exit path must NOT matter. vplat binaries exit through the
# SimControl device (a board shutdown REQUEST serviced on QEMU's main
# loop), so the atexit callback runs on the MAIN thread where there is no
# vCPU context: reading architectural registers there aborts QEMU
# (api.c: assertion failed: (current_cpu)). The drain must therefore be
# context-free -- counter only, no register reads.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   FIXTURE      a marker-less, naturally-exiting fixture
#                (default: rt_c_no_trigger_exit, vplat exit)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_no_trigger_exit}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT

set +e
timeout 60 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -machine andes_ae350 \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,drain_at_exit=1" \
  </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_drain_at_exit]: expected QEMU exit=200 on atexit drain, got $RC"
  echo "--- qemu log ---"
  cat "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_drain_at_exit]: state file is empty"
  exit 1
fi

# Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h: pc@16, minstret@632.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
PC=$(read_u64_le 16 "$STATE_QEMU")
MINSTRET=$(read_u64_le 632 "$STATE_QEMU")

if [ "$PC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_drain_at_exit]: pc must be 0 (atexit marker), got $PC"
  exit 1
fi

# The fixture's main loop alone retires > 2000 insns; crt0/newlib add more.
if [ "$MINSTRET" -le 2000 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_drain_at_exit]: minstret (plugin counter) must be > 2000, got $MINSTRET"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[plugin_drain_at_exit] PASS: QEMU exit=$RC, pc=0, minstret=$MINSTRET"

content.content:
### Test Fixtures

All fixtures run on the unified `tests/e2e.sh` harness, which
sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. Three fixture families:

| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | linked against vsim-demo C runtime. Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- vsim resumes on QEMU1's memory, so the stack/heap and `main()`'s frame must survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. |
| vplat    | `vplat_hello`, `vplat_exit41`, `vplat_file`                 | engine-portable runtime, shipped as `build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a` (sources in `runtime/`; build with `make -C runtime` or `--what runtime`): UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io, NO semihosting -- the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`. See docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`. |

The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.

Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`; the shared runtime sources live at the repo root in `runtime/`. C-level fixtures link `runtime/{crt0.S, trap.S, handler.c}` plus the Andes toolchain's `-lgloss_vh` (semihosting-backed libgloss), using `runtime/andes-sim.ld`. V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. **Phase-2 rule:** the span between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()` runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall (no `printf`, `fopen`, semihosting ebreak, etc.) -- vsim does not implement semihosting, so any libgloss-routed call inside the ROI traps. Phase 1 (before the ROI) prints via standard newlib stdio (QEMU1 is launched with `-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native`); there is no phase 3.

-----
 *   -O1..-O3. If a future toolchain rematerializes x past the drain, the
 *   kernel would recompute instead of transport (silent coverage loss);
 *   re-add an asm volatile("" : : "vr"(x)) force-live guard before enter_vsim
 *   then.
 *
 * VLEN contract: VLEN=512, e32 m1 -> 16 lanes per V reg. N=16.
 *
 * Phase-2 rule: no syscalls between enter_vsim and exit_vsim (vsim does
 * not implement semihosting).
 */
#include "runtime/rt_c_helpers.h"

#include <riscv_vector.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#define N 16
-----
/* Tier-2 C-level fixture: newlib vfprintf format-specifier coverage.
 *
 * The format coverage runs in QEMU1 (phase 1) via libgloss_vh's
 * semihosting _write -- it used to run in the QEMU2 phase, which was
 * removed, so it moved before the ROI. Phase 2 (vsim) is an empty,
 * syscall-free ROI; vsim drains at the exit marker and exits 200.
 *
 * Covered: signed int, hex, string, char, pointer, width/zero-pad/
 * left-align, octal, unsigned, long. No floating-point format
 * specifiers: %f drags soft-float / iprintf and is unnecessary here.
 */
#include "runtime/rt_c_helpers.h"

 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in

 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers: the HINT pair
 * `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (ENTER) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (EXIT). Match
 * insn_match.h. rd=x0 makes each marker an architectural NOP, so marked
 * binaries also run standalone on every engine.
 *
 * marker mode pattern-matches the HINT insns directly; the helpers do not
 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

/* A pure compiler memory barrier (emits no instructions): forces pending
 * memory writes to complete and bars reordering across it. enter_vsim /
 * exit_vsim already carry this clobber on their marker insn, so the markers
 * anchor a kernel's output stores; markerless builds (-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS)
 * call roi_anchor() to pin those stores instead. */
static inline void roi_anchor(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

| `bbv_out=PATH`       | SimPoint: emit one BBV row per `slice=N` insns into PATH.              |
| `slice=N`            | Insns per slice (used by the SimPoint stages). Must be > 0.            |
| `slice_at=K`         | SimPoint slice stage: drain at the end of the K-th slice (needs `slice=N`). |

libgloss_vh semihosting EXIT). The plugin counts every retired insn via a
per-insn TCG callback and writes that count into the drained state file's
`minstret` field; hsim uses it as `N_total` in:

CPI_i           = delta_mcycle_i / vsim_icount

## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)

Fixtures linked with `-lgloss_vh` (semihosting) can print only where a QEMU
intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no semihosting, which is
why the Phase-2 "no syscalls inside the ROI" rule exists. The **vplat
runtime** removes the per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff.

| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |

The runtime ships prebuilt as `libandes_sim_runtime.a`. Build it once
(`./andes-sim build --what runtime`, or any fixture build does it implicitly),
then compile with two extra flags (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`,
no `-lgloss_vh`):

```sh
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

`-B` points gcc at the built artifacts (use the absolute path to
`<repo>/build/runtime` when compiling outside the repo);
`-specs=andes-sim.specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`,
adds `-T andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
list to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
libgloss or semihosting can leak into the link.

--- cell 5 (markdown) ---
So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`)
MUST be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No semihosting (exception: the vplat runtime's MMIO-backed
  stdio / exit / file io is supported inside the ROI, see L1)
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO other than the vplat device set, UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (see L9)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

--- cell 7 (markdown) ---
## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No semihosting inside the ROI; vplat is the supported I/O path  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and
  `exit_vsim()`, when linked against the default semihosting runtime
  (`-lgloss_vh`).
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}` (the semihosting runtime).
- Status: MITIGATED (2026-06). Semihosting inside the ROI is still fatal,
  but the vplat runtime (`build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`, sources in
  `runtime/`, link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`) routes
  stdio to UART2, exit to SimControl, and file io to HTIF -- MMIO devices
  both engines model -- so `printf` / `exit` / `fopen` inside the ROI work
  on fast, cycle AND hybrid (see USER_GUIDE section 5; smoke tests in
  `tests/vplat/`). For semihosting-linked binaries the old rule stands:
  keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg, before the ROI).

Live proof of the vplat path - `vplat_hello.elf` prints from INSIDE the
measured window, serviced by the cycle-accurate vsim leg, and the run
still produces a clean `window_cycles`

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andes-sim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's

  where it would need 0x80FF0000). The retired Python golden

- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`.

## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. Value-level handoff check: shipped for marker/pc, missing for icount/simpoint  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or

- Status: PARTIALLY CLOSED (2026-06): marker/pc covered by

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F18: PC mode + --vsim-warmup-icount round-trip on rt_c_v_matmul.
#
# Same ROI as F17 (CSR-mode) but the switch boundaries are explicit
# PC addresses passed via the plugin's `enter_pc=` arg and vsim's
# `--hybrid-exit-pc` flag. The warmup snapshot is a vsim-side commit
# counter so its semantics must be IDENTICAL to F17 -- the trigger
# source only changes when drain fires, not when the snapshot fires.
#
# Manual TDD smoke; not auto-wired into scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul}"
WARMUP_K="${WARMUP_K:-1000}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-120}"
TOL="${TOL:-5}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-/usr/bin/riscv64-elf-nm}"
command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "$NM not found"

# Pick any RISC-V objdump on PATH. Marker parsing relies on raw opcode
# bytes (7c005073 / 7c00d073) so the choice of disassembler does not
# matter. Prefer the toolchain version when accessible; fall back to
# the system /usr/bin variant (handles sandboxed CI hosts that cannot
# read /local/* shipped toolchain trees).
OBJDUMP=""
for cand in \
  "${OBJDUMP_OVERRIDE:-}" \
  "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}" \
  /usr/bin/riscv64-elf-objdump \
  /usr/bin/riscv64-linux-gnu-objdump; do
  [ -n "$cand" ] && [ -x "$cand" ] && OBJDUMP="$cand" && break
done
[ -n "$OBJDUMP" ] || fail "no RISC-V objdump available"

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-warmup-pc-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
DISASM_TMP=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$DISASM_TMP"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

# Locate the two csrwi 0x7c0 instruction PCs in the binary. Match the raw
# opcode bytes so the lookup is robust across vendor toolchains (the Andes
# toolchain renames CSR 0x7c0 to its symbolic name "milmb" in disassembly,
# while upstream binutils prints "0x7c0"). Opcodes:
#   csrwi 0x7c0, 0 -> 0x7c005073
#   csrwi 0x7c0, 1 -> 0x7c00d073
# Dump to a temp file (objdump output can be MBs; avoids SIGPIPE under
# pipefail when awk exits on the first match).
"$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF" > "$DISASM_TMP"
ENTER_PC=$(awk '$2=="7c005073"{ sub(/:/,"",$1); print $1; exit }' "$DISASM_TMP")
EXIT_PC=$(awk '$2=="7c00d073"{ sub(/:/,"",$1); print $1; exit }'  "$DISASM_TMP")
[ -n "$ENTER_PC" ] || fail "no csrwi 0x7c0,0 found in $VSIM_ELF (PC mode needs an entry PC)"
[ -n "$EXIT_PC"  ] || fail "no csrwi 0x7c0,1 found in $VSIM_ELF (PC mode needs an exit PC)"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e
[ "$QEMU1_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on PC-mode drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]    || fail "QEMU 1 produced no state"

set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC" \
  --vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_K" >/dev/null 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e
[ "$VSIM_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "vsim expected exit 200 (PC-mode drain), got $VSIM_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ]   || fail "vsim produced no state"

python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/warmup_assert.py" \
  "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" --k "$WARMUP_K" --tol "$TOL" \

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
3	#
4	# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
5	# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
6	# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
7	# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
8	# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.
9	
10	# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
11	#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
12	#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
13	# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
14	# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
15	resolve_pc() {
16	  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
17	  case "$boundary" in
18	    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
19	    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
20	  esac
21	}
22	
23	# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
