#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
#
# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.

# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
resolve_pc() {
  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
  case "$boundary" in
    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
  esac
}

# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (both REQUIRED), resolves
#   each against <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare
#   hex). Returns 1 and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if
#   either is unset or does not resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message.
roi_resolve_pair() {
  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
  local start="${ROI_START:-}"
  local end="${ROI_END:-}"
  if [ -z "$start" ] || [ -z "$end" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set (0x address or symbol name)"
    return 1
  fi
  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

# roi_markers_from_disasm <objdump_disasm>
#   Derives the two pc-mode switch PCs from the ROI marker HINTs a fixture
#   embeds, scanning `objdump -d` text:
#     ENTER = the entry marker     `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`  (encoding 5a002013)
#     EXIT  = the LAST exit marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`  (encoding 5a102013)
#   Both are the marker PCs themselves: the plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
#   (--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the trigger
#   (compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so feeding the marker PC reproduces
#   marker mode's switch points exactly -- no offset arithmetic here. EXIT
#   keeps the LAST marker so a fixture that jumps over poison exit-marker
#   padding (rt_pc_jump) resolves to the real, reachable exit, not the first
#   dead one. The raw-bytes match is mnemonic-independent, so no objdump
#   decode table is needed.
#   Prints "ENTER EXIT" as bare hex; returns 1 (prints nothing) if either
#   marker is absent. This lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no
#   per-fixture config; ./andes-sim run still passes explicit boundaries.
roi_markers_from_disasm() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
    $2 == "5a002013" && enter == "" { e = $1; sub(/:$/, "", e); enter = e }
    $2 == "5a102013"                { x = $1; sub(/:$/, "", x); exit_pc = x }
    END {
      if (enter != "" && exit_pc != "") { print enter, exit_pc }
      else                              { exit 1 }
    }
  '
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F19: icount mode + --vsim-warmup-icount on the markerless rt_c_v_matmul_free.
#
# Both boundaries are insn-count thresholds (CSR-less workload):
#   plugin arg `icount=Q` drains QEMU 1 after Q committed insns.
#   `--hybrid-icount M` drains vsim after M committed insns.
#   `--vsim-warmup-icount K` snapshots (mcycle, minstret) at the K-th
#   vsim-side commit.
#
# Precondition K < M. Then measured-region insn count must equal M - K
# within +-TOL (the K-th-commit boundary timing tolerance).
#
# Manual TDD smoke; not auto-wired into scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul_free}"
QEMU_ICOUNT="${QEMU_ICOUNT:-2000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-5000}"
WARMUP_K="${WARMUP_K:-1000}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-120}"
# icount-vs-minstret drift: in CSR/PC mode the snapshot lands on minstret = K
# exactly (the QEMU drain at the csrwi marker pins the pre-vsim minstret
# value, and vsim's per-commit observer is 1:1 with retired insns). In icount
# mode there is no marker; ResumeDriver injects PB instructions that bump the
# hart-side minstret without going through the trigger's observe_commit hook,
# producing a small constant offset that grows linearly with M. The observed
# drift on rt_c_v_matmul_free at K=1000, M=5000 is ~0.4% (under 20 insns).
TOL="${TOL:-25}"

[ "$WARMUP_K" -lt "$VSIM_ICOUNT" ] \
  || fail "precondition K < M violated: K=$WARMUP_K M=$VSIM_ICOUNT"

hybrid_resolve_paths

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-warmup-icount-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e
[ "$QEMU1_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on icount drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]    || fail "QEMU 1 produced no state"

set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --hybrid-icount "$VSIM_ICOUNT" \
  --vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_K" >/dev/null 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e
[ "$VSIM_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "vsim expected exit 200 (icount drain), got $VSIM_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ]   || fail "vsim produced no state"

python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/warmup_assert.py" \
  "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" --k "$WARMUP_K" --m "$VSIM_ICOUNT" --tol "$TOL" \
  || fail "F19 icount-mode warmup invariants violated"

ok "F19 icount-mode warmup invariants hold (K=$WARMUP_K M=$VSIM_ICOUNT)"
echo "PASS e2e_warmup_icount"

    """vsim drain argv with --hybrid-icount trigger.

    No --shared-mem-* flags: the CSR-less workloads re-derive their tight
    loop from the resumed state alone. `warmup_icount` is forwarded only

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F18: PC mode + --vsim-warmup-icount round-trip on rt_c_v_matmul.
#
# Same ROI as F17 (CSR-mode) but the switch boundaries are explicit
# PC addresses passed via the plugin's `enter_pc=` arg and vsim's
# `--hybrid-exit-pc` flag. The warmup snapshot is a vsim-side commit
# counter so its semantics must be IDENTICAL to F17 -- the trigger
# source only changes when drain fires, not when the snapshot fires.
#
# Manual TDD smoke; not auto-wired into scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul}"
WARMUP_K="${WARMUP_K:-1000}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-120}"
TOL="${TOL:-5}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-/usr/bin/riscv64-elf-nm}"
command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "$NM not found"

# Pick any RISC-V objdump on PATH. Marker parsing relies on raw opcode
# bytes (7c005073 / 7c00d073) so the choice of disassembler does not
# matter. Prefer the toolchain version when accessible; fall back to
# the system /usr/bin variant (handles sandboxed CI hosts that cannot
# read /local/* shipped toolchain trees).
OBJDUMP=""
for cand in \
  "${OBJDUMP_OVERRIDE:-}" \
  "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}" \
  /usr/bin/riscv64-elf-objdump \
  /usr/bin/riscv64-linux-gnu-objdump; do
  [ -n "$cand" ] && [ -x "$cand" ] && OBJDUMP="$cand" && break
done
[ -n "$OBJDUMP" ] || fail "no RISC-V objdump available"

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-warmup-pc-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
DISASM_TMP=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$DISASM_TMP"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

# Locate the two csrwi 0x7c0 instruction PCs in the binary. Match the raw
# opcode bytes so the lookup is robust across vendor toolchains (the Andes
# toolchain renames CSR 0x7c0 to its symbolic name "milmb" in disassembly,
# while upstream binutils prints "0x7c0"). Opcodes:
#   csrwi 0x7c0, 0 -> 0x7c005073
#   csrwi 0x7c0, 1 -> 0x7c00d073
# Dump to a temp file (objdump output can be MBs; avoids SIGPIPE under
# pipefail when awk exits on the first match).
"$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF" > "$DISASM_TMP"
ENTER_PC=$(awk '$2=="7c005073"{ sub(/:/,"",$1); print $1; exit }' "$DISASM_TMP")
EXIT_PC=$(awk '$2=="7c00d073"{ sub(/:/,"",$1); print $1; exit }'  "$DISASM_TMP")
[ -n "$ENTER_PC" ] || fail "no csrwi 0x7c0,0 found in $VSIM_ELF (PC mode needs an entry PC)"
[ -n "$EXIT_PC"  ] || fail "no csrwi 0x7c0,1 found in $VSIM_ELF (PC mode needs an exit PC)"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e
[ "$QEMU1_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on PC-mode drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]    || fail "QEMU 1 produced no state"

set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC" \
  --vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_K" >/dev/null 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e
[ "$VSIM_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "vsim expected exit 200 (PC-mode drain), got $VSIM_RC"

content.text:
All 3 fixed and committed as `96f9de5`. And to answer the question: icount mode IS supported - it's one of the four shipped trigger modes (`--trigger icount`). What's missing for icount is only `--verify`/`--cosim` value checking (L15) and the C++ SimPoint port. The icount trigger itself works fine; the test had rotted constants.

Root causes, one per test:

1. **`e2e_warmup_pc.sh`** - still scanned for the retired `csrwi 0x7c0` marker opcodes from before the slti HINT redesign. Now it reuses `roi_markers_from_disasm` from `tests/lib/roi.sh`, the same resolver the bulk runner uses.

2. **`e2e_warmup_icount.sh`** - the real bug was test geometry, not the trigger. The fixture reaches `_exit` at ~insn 2900 (I bisected with the plugin: pc is still in `vmatmul_kernel` at 2800, in the `_exit` spin at 3000), so `QEMU_ICOUNT=2000 + VSIM_ICOUNT=5000` overshot program end and vsim hit the SimControl exit before the drain could fire. The misleading "14155 total insns" figure is inflated by the `_exit` `for(;;)` spin ticking while QEMU services the shutdown request. New geometry Q=500, M=2000, K=500 fits with ~400 insns margin; warmup invariants verified (window = 1481 insns vs M-K = 1500, inside TOL=25). A comment + a pointed failure message now explain the fixture-length constraint.

3. **`test_hsim_run_smoke.sh`** - expected the pre-F14 `./hsim.py build` doctor hint; the hint deliberately says `./andes-sim build` since the driver swap. Test updated.

All three pass, plus `e2e_warmup_marker.sh` re-run green as the sibling guard.

One finding worth your attention (not fixed, out of scope): hsim.py's icount leg (`_vsim_drain_argv`) passes no `--shared-mem-*` flags by design ("workloads re-derive from the resumed state alone"). On rt_c_v_matmul_free that assumption fails - the resumed code reads its stack, which a fresh ELF image does not contain, so the program traps and the icount window measures trap-handler/fprintf execution. `test_icount_window_cycles.sh` "passes" but its cycle figure may be measuring the wrong code. If you want, I can make the hsim icount leg use the shared mmap like the marker path.

content.text:
Because two things still depend on it - but it is removable once the SimPoint port lands.

1. **SimPoint only exists there.** `profile`, `cluster`, `estimate`, `run --mode simpoint`, `archive`/`replay` are implemented only in hsim.py. In `driver/ROADMAP.md`, the C++ ports (F10 `profile`+`cluster`, F11 `estimate`/`--trigger simpoint`) are both **NOT STARTED**. Deleting hsim.py today deletes a shipped feature with no replacement.

2. **It is the parity golden.** `tests/andes_sim/parity.sh` and several `test_andes_sim_*` tests validate the C++ driver byte-for-byte against hsim.py. That was the F14 cutover contract. This value expires once the port is complete and trusted, but today ~17 `tests/hsim/*` scripts, `parity.sh`, and 3 top-level tests (`test_icount_window_cycles.sh`, `test_kernel_cycles.sh`, `test_simpoint_estimated_cycles.sh`) all drive it.

My recommendation: port F10+F11 to `andes-sim` first, then remove hsim.py, `tests/hsim/`, and the parity machinery in one removal change. Two extra benefits of doing it in that order:

- The port can fix the icount/no-shared-mmap flaw I flagged earlier at the root (the C++ icount leg would pass the shared mmap like the marker path does), instead of patching a file that is supposed to stay frozen.
- The hsim tests become the acceptance suite for the port (same outputs, new binary) before they are deleted with it.

If you want, I can start the F10 port next - say the word.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED test for F3: `./hsim.py run <elf-path> --mode marker|pc`.
#
# Path-only contract (no bare-fixture-name shortcut). The positional
# argument is always an ELF path -- relative resolves against CWD,
# absolute is honored as-is. Wraps tests/e2e.sh with FIXTURE,
# TRIGGER_MODE, VSIM_ELF env vars.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
HSIM="$ROOT/hsim.py"

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"

cd "$ROOT"

# 1. --help mentions run + --mode + --verbose surface.
out=$("$HSIM" run --help 2>&1) || fail "run --help exit nonzero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--mode"    || fail "run --help missing --mode:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--verbose" || fail "run --help missing --verbose:\n$out"
ok "run --help lists --mode and --verbose"

# 2. No positional -> argparse error, rc != 0.
set +e
out=$("$HSIM" run 2>&1); rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "run (no args) should exit non-zero, got 0; output: $out"
ok "run (no args) exits non-zero (rc=$rc)"

# 3. Missing --mode -> rc=2 with mode hint.
set +e
out=$("$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf 2>&1); rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "run without --mode should rc=2, got $rc; output: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mode" || fail "missing --mode should hint at --mode:\n$out"
ok "run without --mode exits 2 with mode hint"

# 4. ELF path does not exist -> rc=2 with the offending path quoted.
set +e
out=$("$HSIM" run /no/such/foo.elf --mode marker 2>&1); rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "run nonexistent ELF should rc=2, got $rc; output: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "/no/such/foo.elf" || fail "missing ELF hint should mention the path:\n$out"
ok "run nonexistent ELF exits 2 with path hint"

# 5. vsim binary missing -> rc=2 with `vsim not built -- run ./andes-sim
#    build` (doctor hints point at the C++ entry point since the F14 swap;
#    hsim.py is the frozen parity golden).
set +e
out=$(VSIM_BIN=/no/such/vsim "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode marker 2>&1); rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "run with missing VSIM_BIN should rc=2, got $rc; output: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "vsim not built" || fail "missing vsim hint required:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- "./andes-sim build" || fail "hint should mention './andes-sim build':\n$out"
ok "run with VSIM_BIN missing exits 2 with build hint"

# 6. Smoke: real marker 2-phase handoff on rt_c_hello (artifacts assumed built).
#    ROADMAP requires <30s; cap higher to absorb host load variance.
SMOKE_TIMEOUT=60
set +e
out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode marker 2>&1); rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "smoke run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "rt_c_hello 2/2" || fail "smoke output missing vsim-drain line:\n$out"
ok "smoke run rt_c_hello --mode marker passes"

echo "PASS test_hsim_run_smoke"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F18: PC mode + --vsim-warmup-icount round-trip on rt_c_v_matmul.
#
# Same ROI as F17 (marker mode) but the switch boundaries are explicit
# PC addresses passed via the plugin's `enter_pc=` arg and vsim's
# `--hybrid-exit-pc` flag. The warmup snapshot is a vsim-side commit
# counter so its semantics must be IDENTICAL to F17 -- the trigger
# source only changes when drain fires, not when the snapshot fires.
#
# Manual TDD smoke; not auto-wired into scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul}"
WARMUP_K="${WARMUP_K:-1000}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-120}"
TOL="${TOL:-5}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

# Pick any RISC-V objdump on PATH. Marker parsing relies on raw opcode
# bytes (5a002013 / 5a102013, the slti ROI marker HINTs) so the choice
# of disassembler does not matter. Prefer the toolchain version when
# accessible; fall back to the system /usr/bin variant (handles
# sandboxed CI hosts that cannot read /local/* shipped toolchain trees).
OBJDUMP=""
for cand in \
  "${OBJDUMP_OVERRIDE:-}" \
  "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}" \
  /usr/bin/riscv64-elf-objdump \
  /usr/bin/riscv64-linux-gnu-objdump; do
  [ -n "$cand" ] && [ -x "$cand" ] && OBJDUMP="$cand" && break
done
[ -n "$OBJDUMP" ] || fail "no RISC-V objdump available"

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-warmup-pc-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
DISASM_TMP=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$DISASM_TMP"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

# Locate the two ROI marker HINT PCs in the binary via the shared
# resolver (tests/lib/roi.sh, same derivation the bulk runner uses):
#   enter marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` -> 5a002013
#   exit  marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` -> 5a102013
# Dump to a temp file (objdump output can be MBs; avoids SIGPIPE under
# pipefail when the reader exits early).
"$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF" > "$DISASM_TMP"
MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$(cat "$DISASM_TMP")") \
  || fail "no ROI marker HINTs (slti x0,x0,0x5A0/0x5A1) in $VSIM_ELF (PC mode needs both)"
ENTER_PC=${MARKERS%% *}
EXIT_PC=${MARKERS##* }

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e
[ "$QEMU1_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on PC-mode drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]    || fail "QEMU 1 produced no state"

set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC" \
  --vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_K" >/dev/null 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e
[ "$VSIM_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "vsim expected exit 200 (PC-mode drain), got $VSIM_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ]   || fail "vsim produced no state"

python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/warmup_assert.py" \
  "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" --k "$WARMUP_K" --tol "$TOL" \
  || fail "F18 PC-mode warmup invariants violated"

ok "F18 PC-mode warmup invariants hold (enter=0x$ENTER_PC exit=0x$EXIT_PC)"
echo "PASS e2e_warmup_pc"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F19: icount mode + --vsim-warmup-icount on the markerless rt_c_v_matmul_free.
#
# Both boundaries are insn-count thresholds (CSR-less workload):
#   plugin arg `icount=Q` drains QEMU 1 after Q committed insns.
#   `--hybrid-icount M` drains vsim after M committed insns.
#   `--vsim-warmup-icount K` snapshots (mcycle, minstret) at the K-th
#   vsim-side commit.
#
# Precondition K < M. Then measured-region insn count must equal M - K
# within +-TOL (the K-th-commit boundary timing tolerance).
#
# Manual TDD smoke; not auto-wired into scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul_free}"
# Count geometry: Q + M must fit INSIDE the fixture's real execution
# length, or vsim reaches the program's SimControl exit before the icount
# drain and returns the guest exit code instead of 200. rt_c_v_matmul_free
# reaches _exit at ~insn 2900 (everything after is the _exit spin loop,
# which QEMU-side counters still tick while the shutdown request is
# serviced -- do NOT size Q/M from a drain_at_exit total). Q=500 resumes
# inside crt0/kernel setup; Q+M=2500 leaves ~400 insns of margin.
QEMU_ICOUNT="${QEMU_ICOUNT:-500}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-2000}"
WARMUP_K="${WARMUP_K:-500}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-120}"
# icount-vs-minstret drift: in marker/PC mode the snapshot lands on
# minstret = K exactly (the QEMU drain at the marker pins the pre-vsim
# minstret value, and vsim's per-commit observer is 1:1 with retired
# insns). In icount mode there is no marker; ResumeDriver injects PB
# instructions that bump the hart-side minstret without going through the
# trigger's observe_commit hook, producing a small constant offset that
# grows with M (observed: 19 insns at K=500, M=2000).
TOL="${TOL:-25}"

[ "$WARMUP_K" -lt "$VSIM_ICOUNT" ] \
  || fail "precondition K < M violated: K=$WARMUP_K M=$VSIM_ICOUNT"

hybrid_resolve_paths

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-warmup-icount-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e
[ "$QEMU1_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on icount drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]    || fail "QEMU 1 produced no state"

set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --hybrid-icount "$VSIM_ICOUNT" \
  --vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_K" >/dev/null 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e
[ "$VSIM_RC" -eq 200 ] \
  || fail "vsim expected exit 200 (icount drain), got $VSIM_RC -- if this is the guest exit code, Q+M=$((QEMU_ICOUNT + VSIM_ICOUNT)) no longer fits inside the fixture (see count geometry note above)"
[ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ]   || fail "vsim produced no state"

python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/warmup_assert.py" \
  "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" --k "$WARMUP_K" --m "$VSIM_ICOUNT" --tol "$TOL" \
  || fail "F19 icount-mode warmup invariants violated"

ok "F19 icount-mode warmup invariants hold (K=$WARMUP_K M=$VSIM_ICOUNT)"
echo "PASS e2e_warmup_icount"

1	# ROADMAP - `andes-sim`: a multi-engine simulation framework
2	
3	> Scope of this file: building the `andes-sim` C++ framework. It supersedes the
4	> earlier "rewrite hsim (CoSIM-ready)" content in this file. It does NOT replace
5	> the repo-root `ROADMAP.md` (the master FR tracker). One feature per session;
6	> update each feature's **State** as you go.
7	
8	## Goal
9	
10	Turn the Python `hsim` driver into a single compiled C++20 executable named
11	**`andes-sim`** that is a *framework* hosting multiple simulator backends behind
12	one clear, self-describing interface - so QEMU (fast), Verilator (accurate),
13	Hybrid, and future simulators (alioth, sid) are all first-class, and new
14	Verilator builds can be added at runtime with no framework rebuild.
15	
16	## Vocabulary (three orthogonal concepts)
17	
18	- **Engine** = one simulator *process* the framework drives: `qemu`,
19	  `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`, `verilator:ax66_makatau`, later `alioth`, `sid`.
20	  This is the *pluggable* unit. Verilator has many engine instances (one per HW
21	  config); QEMU has one.
22	- **Model** = how chosen engines compose for a run:
23	  - `fast`     = QEMU alone (functional).
24	  - `accurate` = one Verilator alone, **pure - from reset, no QEMU** (cycle-accurate).
25	  - `hybrid`   = QEMU fast-forward -> Verilator measures the ROI (+ a trigger).
26	- **Trigger** = the ROI delimiter, used by `hybrid`: `marker` | `pc` | `icount` | `simpoint`.
27	
28	A run is `(model) x (engine) x (trigger)`.
29	
30	## Locked decisions
31	
32	- **Name:** the binary is `andes-sim` (the `hsim` "hybrid-sim" name retires).
33	- **Language: C++20**, existing clang++ toolchain; `#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"`
34	  directly (no hand-copied struct, no offsets).
35	- **Runtime = pure C++** (no Python, no shell on the run path). **Build and test
36	  infrastructure may stay shell/Python.**
37	- **Plugins are drop-in binaries, not linked libraries.** Engines are external
38	  processes; `andes-sim` is never recompiled to add one. No `dlopen`, no
39	  compiled-in engine list.
40	- **Discovery = scan + `--describe`.** The framework scans an engines directory
41	  and asks each binary to self-report its capabilities as JSON. A sidecar
42	  `<bin>.json` is the fallback for binaries that cannot add the flag. This is the
43	  hot-plug query mechanism.
44	- **Transparent passthrough for `fast`/`accurate`.** The framework parses only its
45	  selection flags; everything after `--` forwards verbatim to the engine. In these
46	  modes it inherits stdin/stdout/stderr, applies **no timeout**, and propagates the
47	  engine's exit code (exec-style). All native engine behavior is preserved - e.g.
48	  QEMU can hold a gdbstub and wait for a debugger. Users experience one simulator.
49	- **`accurate` = pure Verilator from reset, no QEMU.** vsim already supports this
50	  (default path; hybrid is gated by `--resume-from-qemu`). Cycles come from vsim's
51	  own output, not a drained state file.
52	- **No QEMU2 handback.** No gdbstub state-restore into a second QEMU. The `hybrid`
53	  cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta. The QEMU2 leg was removed from the repo
54	  entirely (`tests/e2e.sh` is a 2-phase harness now); see `remove_qemu2.md`.
55	- **No CoSIM.** Dropped from this design.
56	
57	## Architecture (three layers)
58	
59	```
60	 andes-sim  (one C++20 binary; libc++ + include/hybrid/state_abi.h only)
61	   |
62	 [1] ENGINE REGISTRY  -- discover at runtime (the hot-plug seam)
63	   |     scan engines dir -> run `<bin> --describe` -> EngineDescriptor (JSON)
64	   |     qemu (built-in descriptor) | verilator:<cfg> (self-describe) | alioth/sid (self-describe)
65	   |
66	 [2] MODEL = composition  -- how chosen engines combine
67	   |     fast      = [ qemu ]                      transparent passthrough
68	   |     accurate  = [ verilator:<cfg> ]           transparent passthrough (from reset)
69	   |     hybrid    = [ qemu --ff--> verilator ]    orchestrated, + trigger
70	   |
71	 [3] PLAN EXECUTOR  -- (hybrid only) spawn legs, thread hybrid_state_v1, read mcycle
72	         run_plan(steps): per step -> registry invoke template -> spawn+timeout -> drain
73	```
74	
75	`fast`/`accurate` bypass layer [3] entirely (exec-passthrough). Only `hybrid`
76	orchestrates.
77	
78	## Engine interface (the contract alioth/sid follow)
79	
80	A simulator joins the framework by doing two things:
81	
82	**1. Self-describe.** Answer `--describe` with one JSON object:
83	
84	```json
85	{
86	  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
87	  "type":     "verilator",            // qemu | verilator | alioth | sid | ...
88	  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",       // functional | cycle-accurate
89	  "vlen":     512, "xlen": 64,        // optional HW params
90	  "triggers": ["marker","pc","icount"],  // ROI delimiters understood
91	  "roles":    ["standalone","accurate-leg"],  // standalone | fast-leg | accurate-leg
92	  "state":    ["resume","drain"],     // hybrid_state_v1 capabilities (omit if none)
93	  "invoke": {                         // argv prefix per role; {placeholders} filled by the framework
94	     "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
95	     "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
96	                      "--handoff-out", "{state_out}", "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}"]
97	  },
98	  "result":   "stderr:cycles"         // where the measurement is: stderr:<re> | state.mcycle
99	}
100	```
101	
102	**2. Speak the ABI for any role it claims.** Any engine listing `resume`/`drain`
103	in `state` must read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte
104	(`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) and honor the shared-mmap convention. A
105	functional-only engine (`fast-leg`/`standalone`, no `state`) needs none of this.
106	
107	The framework needs **zero per-engine code** - everything it must know comes back

# ROADMAP - `andes-sim`: a multi-engine simulation framework

> Scope of this file: building the `andes-sim` C++ framework. It supersedes the
> earlier "rewrite hsim (CoSIM-ready)" content in this file. It does NOT replace
> the repo-root `ROADMAP.md` (the master FR tracker). One feature per session;
> update each feature's **State** as you go.

## Goal

Turn the Python `hsim` driver into a single compiled C++20 executable named
**`andes-sim`** that is a *framework* hosting multiple simulator backends behind
one clear, self-describing interface - so QEMU (fast), Verilator (accurate),
Hybrid, and future simulators (alioth, sid) are all first-class, and new
Verilator builds can be added at runtime with no framework rebuild.

## Vocabulary (three orthogonal concepts)

- **Engine** = one simulator *process* the framework drives: `qemu`,
  `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`, `verilator:ax66_makatau`, later `alioth`, `sid`.
  This is the *pluggable* unit. Verilator has many engine instances (one per HW
  config); QEMU has one.
- **Model** = how chosen engines compose for a run:
  - `fast`     = QEMU alone (functional).
  - `accurate` = one Verilator alone, **pure - from reset, no QEMU** (cycle-accurate).
  - `hybrid`   = QEMU fast-forward -> Verilator measures the ROI (+ a trigger).
- **Trigger** = the ROI delimiter, used by `hybrid`: `marker` | `pc` | `icount` | `simpoint`.

A run is `(model) x (engine) x (trigger)`.

## Locked decisions

- **Name:** the binary is `andes-sim` (the `hsim` "hybrid-sim" name retires).
- **Language: C++20**, existing clang++ toolchain; `#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"`
  directly (no hand-copied struct, no offsets).
- **Runtime = pure C++** (no Python, no shell on the run path). **Build and test
  infrastructure may stay shell/Python.**
- **Plugins are drop-in binaries, not linked libraries.** Engines are external
  processes; `andes-sim` is never recompiled to add one. No `dlopen`, no
  compiled-in engine list.
- **Discovery = scan + `--describe`.** The framework scans an engines directory
  and asks each binary to self-report its capabilities as JSON. A sidecar
  `<bin>.json` is the fallback for binaries that cannot add the flag. This is the
  hot-plug query mechanism.
- **Transparent passthrough for `fast`/`accurate`.** The framework parses only its
  selection flags; everything after `--` forwards verbatim to the engine. In these
  modes it inherits stdin/stdout/stderr, applies **no timeout**, and propagates the
  engine's exit code (exec-style). All native engine behavior is preserved - e.g.
  QEMU can hold a gdbstub and wait for a debugger. Users experience one simulator.
- **`accurate` = pure Verilator from reset, no QEMU.** vsim already supports this
  (default path; hybrid is gated by `--resume-from-qemu`). Cycles come from vsim's
  own output, not a drained state file.
- **No QEMU2 handback.** No gdbstub state-restore into a second QEMU. The `hybrid`
  cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta. The QEMU2 leg was removed from the repo
  entirely (`tests/e2e.sh` is a 2-phase harness now); see `remove_qemu2.md`.
- **No CoSIM.** Dropped from this design.

## Architecture (three layers)

```
 andes-sim  (one C++20 binary; libc++ + include/hybrid/state_abi.h only)
   |
 [1] ENGINE REGISTRY  -- discover at runtime (the hot-plug seam)
   |     scan engines dir -> run `<bin> --describe` -> EngineDescriptor (JSON)
   |     qemu (built-in descriptor) | verilator:<cfg> (self-describe) | alioth/sid (self-describe)
   |
 [2] MODEL = composition  -- how chosen engines combine
   |     fast      = [ qemu ]                      transparent passthrough
   |     accurate  = [ verilator:<cfg> ]           transparent passthrough (from reset)
   |     hybrid    = [ qemu --ff--> verilator ]    orchestrated, + trigger
   |
 [3] PLAN EXECUTOR  -- (hybrid only) spawn legs, thread hybrid_state_v1, read mcycle
         run_plan(steps): per step -> registry invoke template -> spawn+timeout -> drain
```

`fast`/`accurate` bypass layer [3] entirely (exec-passthrough). Only `hybrid`
orchestrates.

## Engine interface (the contract alioth/sid follow)

A simulator joins the framework by doing two things:

**1. Self-describe.** Answer `--describe` with one JSON object:

```json
{
  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
  "type":     "verilator",            // qemu | verilator | alioth | sid | ...
  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",       // functional | cycle-accurate
  "vlen":     512, "xlen": 64,        // optional HW params
  "triggers": ["marker","pc","icount"],  // ROI delimiters understood
  "roles":    ["standalone","accurate-leg"],  // standalone | fast-leg | accurate-leg
  "state":    ["resume","drain"],     // hybrid_state_v1 capabilities (omit if none)
  "invoke": {                         // argv prefix per role; {placeholders} filled by the framework
     "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
     "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
                      "--handoff-out", "{state_out}", "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}"]
  },
  "result":   "stderr:cycles"         // where the measurement is: stderr:<re> | state.mcycle
}
```

**2. Speak the ABI for any role it claims.** Any engine listing `resume`/`drain`
in `state` must read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte
(`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) and honor the shared-mmap convention. A
functional-only engine (`fast-leg`/`standalone`, no `state`) needs none of this.

The framework needs **zero per-engine code** - everything it must know comes back
from `--describe`. Spec lives in `docs/engine_interface.md` (delivered in F2).

## Conventions

- **TDD.** Each feature: failing test first (RED), smallest code to pass (GREEN),
  refactor. Run all fast tests each time.
- **Parity flywheel for carried-over behavior.** `tests/andes_sim/parity.sh` runs
  the same args through `python3 hsim.py` (golden) and `build/andes-sim` and diffs
  stdout/stderr/rc. Parity covers behavior that survives unchanged: `list
  fixtures`, `doctor`, `build --dry-run`, `hybrid` cycle figures, `profile`/
  `cluster`/`simpoint`/`estimate`, `archive`. Byte-exact where output is fixed;
  cycle-figure equivalence for hybrid/estimate.
- **New surface gets fresh acceptance tests** (no python golden exists for it):
  `--model fast|accurate`, `--` passthrough, `list engines`, self-describe.
- **Existing smoke tests** `tests/hsim/test_hsim_*.sh` are binary-agnostic; reuse
  as acceptance tests, migrate names in F14.
- During development the binary is `build/andes-sim`; Python `hsim` stays at repo
  root as the golden reference until F14 swaps it.
- **State** values: `NOT STARTED` -> `IN PROGRESS` -> `DONE`.

## Reuse (do not reinvent)

- `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - read drained files into `struct hybrid_state_v1`.
- `hsim` (Python) - authoritative behavior spec for carried-over subcommands.
- `tools/orchestrator/plan.py` - Session/Step model -> the C++ phase-plan engine.
- `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` - argv builders (QEMU drain, vsim) minus QEMU2.
- `tools/hsim_shm.py` - `parse_size`/`select_mmap_dir`/`allocate` (port).
- `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py::write_archive` + `_build_meta` (port).
- `tests/lib/roi.sh` + `tests/e2e.sh` PC resolution - port symbol lookup by reading
  the ELF `.symtab` in C++.
- vsim arg surface `verilator/src/main.cpp:189-304` (optparse) - where `--describe`
  is added; `--print-config:197-200` is the model to copy; `NDS_VLEN` is the source.

---

- **Dependencies:** none.

def _qemu_drain_argv(qemu: Path, elf: Path, plugin: Path,
                     shm_path: Path, shm_size: int, state_out: Path,
                     plugin_extras: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> list[str]:
    """Build the QEMU + plugin drain argv.

    `plugin_extras` are `key=value` strings appended after `outfile=`.
    Same base flags as orchestrator.spawn.qemu_drain_argv; inlined here
    because that helper bakes only `outfile=` and does not yet accept
    extra plugin params.
    """
    _reject_comma("shm_path", str(shm_path))
    _reject_comma("state_out", str(state_out))
    _reject_comma("plugin", str(plugin))
    for extra in plugin_extras:
        _reject_comma("plugin_extras", extra.split("=", 1)[-1])

    mem_obj = (
        f"memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,"
        f"mem-path={shm_path},size={shm_size}"
    )
    plugin_pairs = [f"outfile={state_out}", *plugin_extras]
    return [
        str(qemu),
        "-object", mem_obj,
        "-machine", "andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem",
        "-cpu", "andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512",
        "-nographic",
        "-semihosting-config", "enable=on,target=native",
        "-bios", str(elf),
        "-plugin", f"{plugin}," + ",".join(plugin_pairs),
    ]


def _qemu_profile_argv(qemu: Path, elf: Path, plugin: Path,
                       shm_path: Path, shm_size: int, state_out: Path,

    """M4 profile pass argv: `_qemu_drain_argv` + the BBV plugin extras."""

def cmd_profile(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    elf = Path(args.elf)
    if not elf.is_absolute():
        elf = (Path.cwd() / elf).resolve()
    if not elf.is_file():
        print(f"hsim: ELF not found: {args.elf}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    artifacts = _resolve_artifacts()
    # Profile pass uses qemu + plugin only; vsim is not invoked.
    for label in ("qemu", "plugin"):
        if not artifacts[label].is_file():
            print(f"hsim: {label} not built -- run ./andes-sim build",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2

    bbv = Path(args.output)
    bbv.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    try:
        shm_path = _load_hsim_shm().allocate(
            args.mmap_size, prefix="hsim-profile-shm.",
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"hsim: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    state_fd, state_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="hsim-profile-state.")
    os.close(state_fd)
    state_out = Path(state_name)

    try:
        argv = _qemu_profile_argv(
            qemu=artifacts["qemu"], elf=elf, plugin=artifacts["plugin"],
            shm_path=shm_path, shm_size=args.mmap_size, state_out=state_out,
            bbv_out=bbv, slice_n=args.slice, icount=args.icount,
        )

        if args.dry_run:
            print(f"exec: {shlex.join(argv)}")
            return 0

        proc = subprocess.run(
            argv, cwd=REPO_ROOT,
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            timeout=_PROFILE_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        if proc.returncode != _QEMU_DRAIN_RC:
            tail = proc.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()[-20:]
            print(f"hsim: QEMU profile expected exit {_QEMU_DRAIN_RC}, "
                  f"got {proc.returncode}", file=sys.stderr)
            for line in tail:
                print(line, file=sys.stderr)
            return 1

        if not bbv.is_file() or bbv.stat().st_size == 0:
            print(f"hsim: profile produced empty BBV: {bbv}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        with bbv.open() as fh:
            rows = sum(1 for _ in fh)
        print(f"profile: {rows} BBV rows -> {bbv}")
        return 0
    finally:
        for p in (shm_path, state_out):
            try:
                p.unlink()
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass


def cmd_cluster(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    bbv = Path(args.bbv)
    if not bbv.is_file():
        print(f"hsim: BBV file not found: {args.bbv}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if not _SIMPOINT_BIN.is_file():
        print(f"hsim: simpoint not built -- run ./andes-sim build", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    simpts  = Path(args.simpts)
    weights = Path(args.weights)
    simpts.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    weights.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # -dim 2 fits small BBVs with simple control flow; expose --dim as a
    # flag if larger workloads need a different projection.
    argv = [
        str(_SIMPOINT_BIN),
        "-loadFVFile", str(bbv),
        "-maxK", str(args.max_k),
        "-dim", "2",
        "-saveSimpoints", str(simpts),
        "-saveSimpointWeights", str(weights),
    ]
    if args.dry_run:
        print(f"exec: {shlex.join(argv)}")
        return 0

    proc = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=REPO_ROOT,
                          stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                          stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        print(f"hsim: simpoint exited {proc.returncode}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.stderr.write(proc.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        return 1
    if simpts.stat().st_size == 0 or weights.stat().st_size == 0:
        print("hsim: simpoint produced empty simpts or weights",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    with simpts.open() as fh:
        n_clusters = sum(1 for _ in fh)
    print(f"cluster: {n_clusters} phases -> {simpts}, {weights}")
    return 0

return subprocess.run(argv, env=env, cwd=REPO_ROOT,

# --- estimate (SimPoint cycle aggregator) ----------------------------------

# End-to-end: profile -> SimPoint cluster -> per-phase QEMU+vsim drain.
# Aggregator math:
#     CPI_i = delta_mcycle_i / vsim_icount
#     CPI   = sum_i ( w_i * CPI_i )
#     cycles_estimate = N_total_insns * CPI


def _read_state_mcycle(state_path: Path) -> int:
    """Read the mcycle field from a hybrid_state_v1 file via orchestrator.abi.

    Lazy import keeps `./hsim.py list` etc. from paying the ctypes layout
    check at startup.
    """
    tools_dir = str(REPO_ROOT / "tools")
    if tools_dir not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, tools_dir)
    from orchestrator.abi import HybridStateV1
    state = HybridStateV1.from_buffer_copy(state_path.read_bytes())
    return int(state.mcycle)


def _estimate_one_phase(elf: Path, artifacts: dict[str, Path],
                        slice_n: int, slice_at: int,
                        vsim_icount: int,
                        mmap_size: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Drain one SimPoint phase, return (mcycle_qemu, mcycle_vsim)."""
    # slice_at (slice_consume) is the sole trigger; the profile-pass
    # icount cap is no longer exposed.
    extras: tuple[str, ...] = (f"slice={slice_n}", f"slice_at={slice_at}")
    return _drain_round_trip(
        elf, artifacts, extras, vsim_icount,
        label=f"phase{slice_at}", mmap_size=mmap_size,
    )


def _run_drain_at_exit_profile(elf: Path, artifacts: dict[str, Path],
                                bbv: Path, slice_n: int,
                                mmap_size: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Run a profile pass that drains at program exit (no icount cap).

    Returns (rc, n_total_insns). On rc != 0, n_total_insns is 0.

    The plugin's drain_at_exit=1 mode counts every retired insn via a
    per-insn exec cb and overrides the drained state file's `minstret`
    field with that count (QEMU's PMU minstret is host-tick-derived on
    system-mode without -icount, which is why we use the plugin counter).
    """
    shm_path = _load_hsim_shm().allocate(
        mmap_size, prefix="hsim-profile-shm.",
    )
    state_fd, state_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="hsim-profile-state.")
    os.close(state_fd)
    state_out = Path(state_name)
    try:
        argv = _qemu_drain_argv(
            artifacts["qemu"], elf, artifacts["plugin"],
            shm_path, mmap_size, state_out,
            plugin_extras=(
                f"bbv_out={bbv}",
                f"slice={slice_n}",
                "drain_at_exit=1",
            ),
        )
        proc = subprocess.run(
            argv, cwd=REPO_ROOT,
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            timeout=_PROFILE_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        if proc.returncode != _QEMU_DRAIN_RC:
            tail = proc.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()[-20:]
            print(f"hsim: QEMU profile expected exit {_QEMU_DRAIN_RC}, "
                  f"got {proc.returncode}", file=sys.stderr)
            for line in tail:
                print(line, file=sys.stderr)
            return 1, 0

        if not bbv.is_file() or bbv.stat().st_size == 0:
            print(f"hsim: profile produced empty BBV: {bbv}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1, 0
        with bbv.open() as fh:
            rows = sum(1 for _ in fh)

        # Read N_total from the drained state file's minstret field
        # (overridden by the plugin's atexit counter).
        tools_dir = str(REPO_ROOT / "tools")
        if tools_dir not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, tools_dir)
        from orchestrator.abi import HybridStateV1
        state = HybridStateV1.from_buffer_copy(state_out.read_bytes())
        n_total = int(state.minstret)
        if n_total <= 0:
            print(f"hsim: drain-at-exit produced minstret={n_total} "
                  f"(plugin counter unexpectedly zero)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1, 0

        print(f"profile: {rows} BBV rows -> {bbv} (N_total={n_total})")
        return 0, n_total
    finally:
        for p in (shm_path, state_out):
            try:
                p.unlink()
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass


def _read_simpoint_phases(simpts: Path,
                          weights: Path) -> list[tuple[int, float]]:
    """B15: pair SimPoint's simpts <-> weights rows by cluster id.

    Each file row is `<value> <cluster_id>`. Positional pairing (zip) is
    fragile if a future SimPoint emits the two files in different
    orderings; pair by cluster id instead so the weighted CPI math is
    invariant to row order. Returns the (K, weight) pairs.
    """
    def _parse(path: Path, val_fn):
        rows = {}
        for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) < 2:
                continue
            rows[int(parts[1])] = val_fn(parts[0])
        return rows
    k_by_cluster = _parse(simpts, int)
    w_by_cluster = _parse(weights, float)
    if set(k_by_cluster) != set(w_by_cluster):
        raise ValueError(
            f"hsim: simpts/weights cluster id mismatch "
            f"(simpts={sorted(k_by_cluster)} vs weights={sorted(w_by_cluster)})")
    # Sort by cluster id for stable iteration; the sum is commutative
    # so this is purely for predictable human output.
    return [(k_by_cluster[c], w_by_cluster[c])
            for c in sorted(k_by_cluster)]


def _run_simpoint_pipeline(elf: Path, artifacts: dict[str, Path],
                           interval: int, max_k: int,
                           vsim_icount: int, mmap_size: int) -> int:
    """Full SimPoint cycle estimator: profile -> cluster -> per-phase drain.

    Shared by `./hsim.py estimate` and `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint`. Always
    profiles to natural program exit (plugin atexit counter -> N_total).
    Returns 0 on success and prints `estimated_cycles=<int>` as the
    headline line.
    """
    # B16: explicit `--vsim-icount 0` is no longer silently coerced to
    # `interval`. The sentinel for the SimPoint-correct auto-default is
    # `None` (argparse omits the flag) or any negative value; an explicit
    # 0 is rejected to surface what the user actually requested instead
    # of producing a phase cycle figure for what they may have intended
    # as a no-op probe.
    if vsim_icount == 0:
        print("hsim: --vsim-icount=0 is not valid in --mode simpoint; "
              "omit the flag (uses --interval as auto-default) or pass "
              "an explicit positive value",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if vsim_icount is None or vsim_icount < 0:
        vsim_icount = interval

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="hsim-simpoint-") as tmpdir:
        tmp = Path(tmpdir)
        bbv = tmp / "profile.bb"
        simpts = tmp / "simpts"
        weights = tmp / "weights"

        rc, n_total = _run_drain_at_exit_profile(
            elf, artifacts, bbv, interval, mmap_size,
        )
        if rc != 0:
            return rc

        rc = cmd_cluster(argparse.Namespace(
            bbv=str(bbv), max_k=max_k,
            simpts=str(simpts), weights=str(weights), dry_run=False,
        ))
        if rc != 0:
            return rc

        try:
            pairs = _read_simpoint_phases(simpts, weights)
        except ValueError as exc:
            print(f"hsim: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1

        phases = []
        for K, w in pairs:
            print(f"[hsim simpoint] phase slice_at={K} weight={w:.3f}",
                  flush=True)
            try:
                mc_before, mc_after = _estimate_one_phase(
                    elf, artifacts, interval, K,
                    vsim_icount,
                    mmap_size=mmap_size,
                )
            except RuntimeError as exc:
                print(f"hsim: simpoint failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
            delta = mc_after - mc_before
            cpi = delta / vsim_icount if vsim_icount > 0 else 0.0
            phases.append({"K": K, "w": w, "delta": delta, "cpi": cpi})

        weighted_cpi = sum(p["w"] * p["cpi"] for p in phases)
        estimated_cycles = int(n_total * weighted_cpi)

        print(f"M4 profile: {len(pairs)} BBV rows ({bbv.name})")
        print(f"cluster: {len(phases)} phases")
        for p in phases:
            print(f"phase K={p['K']} w={p['w']:.3f} "
                  f"delta_mcycle={p['delta']} CPI={p['cpi']:.3f}")
        print(f"estimated_cycles={estimated_cycles}  "
              f"(N={n_total}, weighted_CPI={weighted_cpi:.3f})")
        return 0


def cmd_estimate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    elf = Path(args.elf)
    if not elf.is_absolute():
        elf = (Path.cwd() / elf).resolve()
    if not elf.is_file():
        print(f"hsim: ELF not found: {args.elf}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    artifacts = _resolve_artifacts()
    for label, path in artifacts.items():
        if not path.is_file():
            print(f"hsim: {label} not built -- run ./andes-sim build",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
    if not _SIMPOINT_BIN.is_file():
        print("hsim: simpoint not built -- run ./andes-sim build",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    return _run_simpoint_pipeline(
        elf=elf, artifacts=artifacts,
        interval=args.slice, max_k=args.max_k,
        vsim_icount=args.vsim_icount, mmap_size=args.mmap_size,
    )

# --- F10: archive + replay (M6 + M7) ---------------------------------------

# Default mmap size used by every e2e fixture and demo. Exposed via
# --mmap-size for unusual workloads.
_DEFAULT_MMAP_SIZE = 128 * 1024 * 1024


def _load_checkpoint_module():
    """Lazy-add tools/ to sys.path and return orchestrator.checkpoint.

    Kept lazy so an unrelated subcommand (e.g. `./hsim.py list`) does not
    pay the ctypes layout check at module load time.
    """
    tools_dir = str(REPO_ROOT / "tools")
    if tools_dir not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, tools_dir)
    from orchestrator import checkpoint
    return checkpoint


def cmd_archive(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    state = Path(args.state)
    mmap_file = Path(args.mmap)
    if not state.is_file():
        print(f"hsim: state file not found: {args.state}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if not mmap_file.is_file():
        print(f"hsim: mmap file not found: {args.mmap}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    snap = Path(args.output)
    if args.dry_run:
        print(
            f"archive: state={state} mmap={mmap_file} elf={args.elf} "
            f"mmap_size={args.mmap_size} -> {snap}"
        )
        return 0

    # In-process import: hsim and orchestrator are both Python; a
    # subprocess wrapper would just add interpreter startup latency and
    # obscure tracebacks.
    checkpoint = _load_checkpoint_module()
    try:
        checkpoint.write_archive(
            snap,
            state_path=state,
            mmap_path=mmap_file,
            mmap_size=args.mmap_size,
            elf_path=args.elf,
            source_step_index=0,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"hsim: write_archive failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    print(f"archive: {snap}/{{state.bin,mem,meta.json}}")
    return 0


def cmd_replay(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    snap = Path(args.snap)
    if not snap.is_dir():
        print(f"hsim: snapshot directory not found: {args.snap}",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    artifacts = _resolve_artifacts()
    for label, path in artifacts.items():
        if not path.is_file():
            print(f"hsim: {label} not built -- run ./andes-sim build",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2

    argv = [
        sys.executable, "-m", "orchestrator.main", "replay-checkpoint",
        str(snap),
        "--resume-with", args.resume_with,
        "--project-root", str(REPO_ROOT),
    ]
    if args.dry_run:
        print(f"exec: {shlex.join(argv)}")
        return 0

    env = os.environ.copy()
    existing_pp = env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
    tools_dir = str(REPO_ROOT / "tools")
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = (
        tools_dir + os.pathsep + existing_pp if existing_pp else tools_dir
    )
    env["VSIM_BIN"]    = str(artifacts["vsim"])
    env["VSIM_QEMU"]   = str(artifacts["qemu"])
    env["VSIM_PLUGIN"] = str(artifacts["plugin"])
    return subprocess.run(argv, env=env, cwd=REPO_ROOT,
                          stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL).returncode

            kanata = f" KANATA_FILE={env['KANATA_FILE']}"

# Inline QEMU + vsim drain pair for the CSR-less paths (--mode icount and
# the per-phase legs of --mode simpoint). e2e.sh only knows marker/pc
# triggers; these workloads drain at the plugin's icount/slice triggers
# and vsim exits via --hybrid-icount.
_VSIM_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S = 120


def _vsim_drain_argv(vsim: Path, elf: Path, state_in: Path,
                     state_out: Path, hybrid_icount: int,
                     warmup_icount: int = 0) -> list[str]:
    """vsim drain argv with --hybrid-icount trigger.

    No --shared-mem-* flags: the CSR-less workloads re-derive their tight
    loop from the resumed state alone. `warmup_icount` is forwarded only
    when > 0 so older vsim binaries (without the flag) still accept the
    invocation -- those would error out today regardless, but keeping the
    flag out of the default argv keeps the contract narrow.
    """
    argv = [
        str(vsim), str(elf),
        "--resume-from-qemu", str(state_in),
        "--handoff-out", str(state_out),
        "--hybrid-icount", str(hybrid_icount),
    ]
    if warmup_icount > 0:
        argv += ["--vsim-warmup-icount", str(warmup_icount)]
    return argv


def _drain_round_trip(elf: Path, artifacts: dict[str, Path],
                      plugin_extras: tuple[str, ...],
                      vsim_icount: int, label: str,
                      mmap_size: int,
                      echo_phases: bool = False,
                      warmup_icount: int = 0) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Run one QEMU + vsim drain pair, return (mcycle_qemu, mcycle_vsim).

    QEMU drains at its plugin trigger -> state file. vsim resumes from
    that state, drains after `vsim_icount` retired insns. Both spawns
    must exit `_QEMU_DRAIN_RC` (200) -- otherwise raises RuntimeError
    with the last 10 lines of the failing process's output.

    Allocates shm + two state tempfiles, unlinks them on exit (even on
    raise). `echo_phases=True` prints `[hsim <label> N/2]` status lines
    for long-running single-shot invocations (--mode icount).
    """
    shm_path = _load_hsim_shm().allocate(
        mmap_size, prefix=f"hsim-{label}-shm.",
    )
    state_q_fd, state_q_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f"hsim-{label}-qstate.")
    os.close(state_q_fd)
    state_q = Path(state_q_name)
    state_v_fd, state_v_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f"hsim-{label}-vstate.")
    os.close(state_v_fd)
    state_v = Path(state_v_name)
    try:
        if echo_phases:
            print(f"[hsim {label} 1/2] QEMU drain ({','.join(plugin_extras)})",
                  flush=True)
        qemu_argv = _qemu_drain_argv(
            artifacts["qemu"], elf, artifacts["plugin"],
            shm_path, mmap_size, state_q,
            plugin_extras=plugin_extras,
        )
        proc = subprocess.run(
            qemu_argv, cwd=REPO_ROOT,
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            timeout=_PROFILE_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        if proc.returncode != _QEMU_DRAIN_RC:
            tail = proc.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()[-10:]
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"QEMU {label} expected exit {_QEMU_DRAIN_RC}, "
                f"got {proc.returncode}: " + "; ".join(tail)
            )
        mc_q = _read_state_mcycle(state_q)

        if echo_phases:
            print(f"[hsim {label} 2/2] vsim --hybrid-icount {vsim_icount} "
                  f"drain", flush=True)
        vsim_argv = _vsim_drain_argv(
            artifacts["vsim"], elf, state_q, state_v, vsim_icount,
            warmup_icount=warmup_icount,
        )
        proc = subprocess.run(
            vsim_argv, cwd=REPO_ROOT,
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            timeout=_VSIM_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        if proc.returncode != _QEMU_DRAIN_RC:
            tail = proc.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()[-10:]
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"vsim {label} expected exit {_QEMU_DRAIN_RC}, "
                f"got {proc.returncode}: " + "; ".join(tail)
            )
        mc_v = _read_state_mcycle(state_v)
        return mc_q, mc_v
    finally:
        for p in (shm_path, state_q, state_v):
            try:
                p.unlink()
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass


def _run_drain_pair(elf: Path, artifacts: dict[str, Path],
                    plugin_extras: tuple[str, ...],
                    vsim_icount: int, label: str,
                    mmap_size: int,
                    warmup_icount: int = 0) -> int:
    """Two-step QEMU + vsim drain round-trip with window-cycles print.

    Wraps _drain_round_trip: catches the RuntimeError on failure, prints
    PASS / window_cycles line on success. Used by --mode icount.
    """
    try:
        mc_q, mc_v = _drain_round_trip(
            elf, artifacts, plugin_extras, vsim_icount,
            label, mmap_size, echo_phases=True,
            warmup_icount=warmup_icount,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"hsim: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

1	// andes-sim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andes-sim <cmd> [--model M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
9	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
10	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
11	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
12	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
13	#define ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
14	
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	struct Cli {
21	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
22	  std::string model;                      // --model fast|cycle|hybrid
23	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
24	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc|icount|simpoint
25	  std::string what;                       // --what <target> (build)
26	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
27	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the icounts/sizes stay strings here and
28	  // are parsed where they are used.
29	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
30	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
31	  std::string qemu_icount;                // --qemu-icount (trigger icount)
32	  std::string vsim_icount;                // --vsim-icount (trigger icount)
33	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
34	  std::string vsim_warmup_icount;         // --vsim-warmup-icount (vsim leg)
35	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
36	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
37	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
38	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
39	  std::string cosim_interval;             // --cosim-interval (run --cosim)
40	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
41	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
42	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --model hybrid)
43	  bool cosim = false;                     // --cosim (run --model hybrid, dev)
44	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
45	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
46	};
47	
48	// Parse argv[1..] (program name skipped). The vector overload is the testable
49	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().
50	Cli parse_cli(const std::vector<std::string>& args);
51	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
52	
53	}  // namespace andes_sim
54	
55	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
56

1	// The phase-plan grammar driven by run_plan (F6) -- the C++ analog of
2	// orchestrator/plan.py's Session/Step model, minus the dropped QEMU2 step.
3	//
4	// A Plan is a list of Steps; each Step names an engine (by id, resolved against
5	// the F2 registry), the role to invoke it in (its `invoke` template key, e.g.
6	// "fast-leg" / "accurate-leg"), and a Trigger. run_plan spawns each leg in
7	// order, threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward, and returns each
8	// leg's mcycle/minstret. Under the no-QEMU2-handback design every F6 step
9	// drains, so the hybrid cycle figure is the vsim-leg mcycle minus the qemu-leg
10	// mcycle.
11	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_PLAN_HPP
12	#define ANDES_SIM_PLAN_HPP
13	
14	#include <map>
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	// The ROI delimiter for a step. `kind` is marker|pc|icount|simpoint; `params`
23	// carries kind-specific values (e.g. icount=N, enter_pc, exit_pc) that F9 maps
24	// onto trigger args. F6 only exercises the default marker case (no params).
25	struct Trigger {
26	  std::string kind;
27	  std::map<std::string, std::string> params;
28	};
29	
30	// One leg of a plan: which engine, which invoke role, under which trigger.
31	// `extra_args` are verbatim tokens appended after the filled template and the
32	// trigger args -- the seam for user-forwarded per-leg flags (e.g. the vsim
33	// leg's --vsim-warmup-icount / --kanata), which are orthogonal to the trigger.
34	struct Step {
35	  std::string engine_id;  // "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"
36	  std::string role;       // invoke-template key: "fast-leg" | "accurate-leg"
37	  Trigger trigger;
38	  std::vector<std::string> extra_args{};  // default-init: keeps 3-field Step{} literals warning-free
39	};
40	
41	// A whole hybrid run. Every step loads `elf`; the shared mmap (`mem_size`
42	// bytes, at `mmap_path` or allocated by run_plan when empty) survives across
43	// every leg so memory threads through.
44	struct Plan {
45	  std::string elf;          // path to the ELF every leg launches
46	  long long mem_size = 0;   // shared-mmap size in bytes
47	  std::string mmap_path;    // "" => run_plan allocates one (F5) and owns it
48	  std::vector<Step> steps;
49	};
50	
51	// What one drain step measured (read back from its state file), plus the
52	// leg's captured stdout -- the guest program's own output (UART/semihosting)
53	// rides the engine's stdout and must flow through to the user. `st` is the
54	// full drained record (verify_oracle F4: run --verify diffs the vsim drain
55	// against the oracle leg's in-process, after run_plan removed the files).
56	struct PhaseResult {
57	  unsigned long long mcycle = 0;
58	  unsigned long long minstret = 0;
59	  std::string out;
60	  hybrid_state_v1 st{};
61	  // cosim_roi F4: in-ROI checkpoint drains (`<state_out>.ckpt<k>`, k from 1),
62	  // read back in order before run_plan removes the workdir. Empty unless the
63	  // leg ran with checkpointing enabled.
64	  std::vector<hybrid_state_v1> checkpoints{};
65	};
66	
67	// Aggregate outcome. `error` empty => every step matched its expected exit and
68	// drained a valid state file; `phases` then holds one entry per step in order.
69	struct PlanResult {
70	  std::string error;
71	  std::vector<PhaseResult> phases;
72	  bool ok() const { return error.empty(); }
73	};
74	
75	}  // namespace andes_sim
76	
77	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_PLAN_HPP
78

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- the C++ analog of runner.run_session, minus
2	// the dropped QEMU2 handback. run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
21	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
22	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
23	struct RuntimeCtx {
24	  std::string mmap_path;
25	  long long mem_size = 0;
26	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
27	  std::string plugin_path;
28	};
29	
30	// hw-config sync: the QEMU fast leg models the hardware the accurate-leg
31	// engine measures, so its -cpu vlen follows that engine's descriptor. 512 is
32	// the fallback for engines that report none. One definition, used by both the
33	// plan executor ({vlen} fill) and the hybrid banner.
34	inline long synced_vlen(long engine_vlen) {
35	  return engine_vlen > 0 ? engine_vlen : 512;
36	}
37	
38	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
39	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
40	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
41	// appended to its argv. marker contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
42	// themselves).
43	struct LegTriggerArgs {
44	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
45	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
46	};
47	
48	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. marker -> empty. pc -> qemu
49	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. icount -> qemu
50	// `,icount=<qemu_icount>` / vsim `--hybrid-icount <vsim_icount>`. Roles other
51	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
52	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
53	//
54	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
55	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
56	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
57	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
58	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
59	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
60	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
61	                                std::string& err);
62	
63	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
64	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
65	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
66	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
67	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
68	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
69	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
70	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
71	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
72	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
73	
74	struct PlanOptions {
75	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
76	  int expect_rc = 200;        // drain success code (kExitHandoffToQemu)
77	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
78	};
79	
80	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
81	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
82	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
83	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
84	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
85	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
86	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
87	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
88	
89	}  // namespace andes_sim
90	
91	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED test: `./hsim.py estimate <elf> --slice N [--max-k K]` argparse surface.
# End-to-end SimPoint cycle estimator -- equivalent to
# `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint`. Always profiles to natural program exit
# (no --icount knob).
#
# Argparse-surface assertions only. Full-pipeline regression lives in
# tests/test_simpoint_estimated_cycles.sh and the run-to-exit semantics
# in tests/hsim/test_hsim_estimate_drain_at_exit.sh.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
HSIM="$ROOT/hsim.py"

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF (run ./hsim.py build first)"

cd "$ROOT"

# 1. estimate --help mentions the key flags (and NOT --icount: simpoint
#    always profiles to natural program exit).
out=$("$HSIM" estimate --help 2>&1) || fail "estimate --help non-zero: $out"
for flag in --slice --max-k --vsim-icount; do
  echo "$out" | grep -qE -- "$flag" \
    || fail "estimate --help missing $flag:"$'\n'"$out"
done
echo "$out" | grep -qE -- "--icount" \
  && fail "estimate --help still mentions removed --icount:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimate --help mentions --slice, --max-k, --vsim-icount (no --icount)"

# 2. estimate with no ELF -> rc=2 (argparse required positional).
set +e
out=$("$HSIM" estimate 2>&1)
rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "estimate (no arg) rc=$rc (expected 2):"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimate without ELF -> rc=2"

# 3. Bogus ELF -> rc=2 with hint.
set +e
out=$("$HSIM" estimate "/no/such/foo.elf" 2>&1)
rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "estimate bogus rc=$rc (expected 2):"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qiE 'not found|no such' \
  || fail "estimate bogus missing 'not found' hint:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimate bogus ELF -> rc=2 with hint"

# 4. Missing vsim artifact -> rc=2 with 'not built' hint.
set +e
out=$(VSIM_BIN=/no/such/vsim "$HSIM" estimate "$ELF" 2>&1)
rc=$?

echo "$out" | grep -qE 'vsim.*not built' \
  || fail "missing-vsim no 'not built' hint:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "missing vsim artifact -> rc=2 with 'not built' hint"

# 5. --icount is rejected by argparse (the knob no longer exists).
set +e
out=$("$HSIM" estimate "$ELF" --slice 20 --icount 5000 2>&1)
rc=$?
set -e

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Differential parity harness: the closed-loop flywheel for the rewrite.
3	#
4	# Runs the same args through the Python golden (hsim) and the C++ driver
5	# (build/andes-sim), then diffs stdout+stderr and the exit code. As each
6	# later feature ports a subcommand, it adds its cases below; a green parity
7	# run is the evidence the C++ path matches the reference it replaces.
8	#
9	# F0 ships the harness skeleton with zero cases, so it exits 0 vacuously.
10	# Override the two binaries via the GOLDEN / NEW env vars if needed.
11	set -uo pipefail
12	
13	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
14	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
15	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
16	
17	GOLDEN="${GOLDEN:-$ROOT/hsim.py}"        # Python reference driver
18	NEW="${NEW:-$ROOT/build/andes-sim}"   # C++ driver under test
19	
20	# Parity compares the full developer surface against the golden (which exposes
21	# everything), so run the C++ driver in dev mode -- e.g. so the dev-only
22	# `list fixtures` target resolves on both sides.
23	export ANDES_SIM_DEV=1
24	
25	pass=0
26	fail=0
27	
28	# compare <case-name> -- <args...>
29	# Invoke GOLDEN and NEW with identical args; require matching stdout+stderr
30	# and exit code. Records a pass/fail; never aborts so all cases report.
31	compare() {
32	  local name="$1"
33	  shift
34	  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
35	  local g_out g_rc n_out n_rc
36	  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
37	  g_rc=$?
38	  n_out=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
39	  n_rc=$?
40	  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
41	    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
42	    fail=$((fail + 1))
43	    return
44	  fi
45	  pass=$((pass + 1))
46	}
47	
48	# compare_carried <case-name> -- <args...>
49	# Like compare, but the C++ driver appends sections the Python golden lacks
50	# (doctor's engines readout). Scope parity to the carried-over report by
51	# truncating NEW at (and including) the `Summary:` line before diffing.
52	compare_carried() {
53	  local name="$1"
54	  shift
55	  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
56	  local g_out g_rc n_full n_rc n_out
57	  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
58	  g_rc=$?
59	  n_full=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
60	  n_rc=$?
61	  n_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$n_full" | awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}')
62	  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
63	    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
64	    fail=$((fail + 1))
65	    return
66	  fi
67	  pass=$((pass + 1))
68	}
69	
70	# --- parity cases (populated per feature) ---
71	compare "list fixtures" -- list fixtures      # F1
72	compare_carried "doctor" -- doctor            # F3
73	compare "build dry default" -- build --dry-run                  # F4
74	for w in all qemu vsim plugin simpoint fixtures; do
75	  compare "build dry $w" -- build --dry-run --what "$w"
76	done
77	
78	echo "parity: $pass matched, $fail differed"
79	[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]
80

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

GOLDEN="${GOLDEN:-$ROOT/hsim.py}"        # Python reference driver
NEW="${NEW:-$ROOT/build/andes-sim}"   # C++ driver under test

# Parity compares the full developer surface against the golden (which exposes
# everything), so run the C++ driver in dev mode -- e.g. so the dev-only
# `list fixtures` target resolves on both sides.
export ANDES_SIM_DEV=1

pass=0
fail=0

# compare <case-name> -- <args...>
# Invoke GOLDEN and NEW with identical args; require matching stdout+stderr
# and exit code. Records a pass/fail; never aborts so all cases report.
compare() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_out n_rc
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_out=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# compare_carried <case-name> -- <args...>
# Like compare, but the C++ driver appends sections the Python golden lacks
# (doctor's engines readout). Scope parity to the carried-over report by
# truncating NEW at (and including) the `Summary:` line before diffing.
compare_carried() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_full n_rc n_out
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_full=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  n_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$n_full" | awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}')
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# --- parity cases (populated per feature) ---
compare "list fixtures" -- list fixtures      # F1
compare_carried "doctor" -- doctor            # F3
compare "build dry default" -- build --dry-run                  # F4
for w in all qemu vsim plugin simpoint fixtures; do
  compare "build dry $w" -- build --dry-run --what "$w"
done

echo "parity: $pass matched, $fail differed"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]
