1	// Shared-mmap allocation for andes-sim.
2	//
3	// The caller asks for `size` bytes; we resolve a backing directory over a
4	// tier list (first fit wins, fit = size + 256 MiB free), allocate a sparse
5	// file with mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line that always names
6	// the chosen tier -- and, when we fell past /dev/shm, why. HSIM_MMAP_DIR
7	// pins a single tier (hard error if it does not fit; no fallback past it).
8	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_SHM_HPP
9	#define ANDES_SIM_SHM_HPP
10	
11	#include <functional>
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	// Free-space headroom a tier must have beyond the requested size.
18	inline constexpr long long kMmapSafetyMargin = 256LL * 1024 * 1024;
19	
20	// One backing-store candidate: the directory plus the label used in
21	// status/error messages ("/dev/shm", "~/.cache/andes-sim", "HSIM_MMAP_DIR=..").
22	struct MmapTier {
23	  std::string dir;
24	  std::string label;
25	};
26	
27	// resolve_mmap_dir result: the chosen dir ("" on failure) and, when a tier
28	// was skipped, a human note saying which and why ("" when tiers[0] fit).
29	struct MmapDirChoice {
30	  std::string dir;
31	  std::string note;
32	};
33	
34	// Parse "8G" / "512M" / "1024" / "1.5G" into a positive byte count. On success
35	// returns the count and leaves `err` empty; on failure returns 0 and sets `err`
36	// to the argparse-style message. Mirrors hsim_shm.parse_size (fractional values
37	// truncate, like Python int(float(num) * mult)).
38	long long parse_size(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
39	
40	// First-fit resolver over `tiers`. `probe(dir)` returns the dir's free bytes,
41	// or -1 when it does not exist. A tier fits when probe >= size + margin.
42	// On success `err` is empty; when nothing fits, returns {"", ""} and `err`
43	// names every tier's reason plus the HSIM_MMAP_DIR hint. Pure: no env, no
44	// filesystem -- testable with a fake probe.
45	MmapDirChoice resolve_mmap_dir(
46	    const std::vector<MmapTier>& tiers, long long size,
47	    const std::function<long long(const std::string&)>& probe,
48	    std::string& err);
49	
50	// Build the real tier list from the environment:
51	//   HSIM_MMAP_DIR set -> that single pinned tier;
52	//   else            -> /dev/shm, then $XDG_CACHE_HOME|~/.cache + /andes-sim
53	//                      (created here so the free-space probe can see it).
54	std::vector<MmapTier> mmap_tiers();
55	
56	// WSL2 advice for `doctor`: given /proc/version contents, the repo dir, and
57	// the mmap tier list, return warning lines. Empty when not on WSL2. On WSL2:
58	// always the .wslconfig memory= hint (tmpfs is capped by the WSL VM), plus a
59	// drvfs warning for the repo or any tier dir under /mnt/ (slow, and
60	// MAP_SHARED is not coherent across the 9p boundary). Pure -- testable.
61	std::vector<std::string> wsl_warnings(const std::string& proc_version,
62	                                      const std::string& repo_dir,
63	                                      const std::vector<MmapTier>& tiers);
64	
65	// Convert a --mem-size spec into the fast leg's plain QEMU `-m` argv:
66	// {"-m", "<MiB>M"}. Empty spec -> {} with no error (QEMU as-is). Malformed
67	// specs and sizes that are not a whole MiB (QEMU's -m granularity) return {}
68	// and set `err`.
69	std::vector<std::string> qemu_m_args(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
70	
71	// Allocate a sparse mmap file of `size` bytes in the resolved dir (mkstemp +
72	// truncate), print one "[hsim mmap] <size> at <dir> (free: <free>)" line
73	// (plus "; fallback: <why>" when /dev/shm was skipped), and return its path.
74	// On failure returns "" and sets `err`. Caller owns the file (unlink when
75	// done).
76	std::string allocate(long long size, std::string& err,
77	                     const std::string& prefix = "hsim-shm.");
78	
79	}  // namespace andes_sim
80	
81	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_SHM_HPP
82

#    --interval and --max-k are present.
help_out=$("$HSIM" run --help 2>&1) || fail "run --help non-zero: $help_out"

  echo "$help_out" | grep -qE "\\b$choice\\b" \

  && fail "run --help still mentions removed --slice-at:"$'\n'"$help_out"

# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andes-sim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

add_executable(andes-sim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_build.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  hybrid.cpp
  elf_syms.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
  state_diff.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.
target_include_directories(andes-sim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(andes-sim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andes-sim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-plan-test plan_test.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
# F6 integration acceptance: spawns real qemu+vsim, so it also needs the registry.
add_executable(andes-sim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp engine_registry.cpp)
# F7 transparent-passthrough argv assembly (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andes-sim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)

# F9 hybrid trigger build (pure; resolves pc boundaries against a fixture ELF).
add_executable(andes-sim-hybrid-test hybrid_test.cpp hybrid.cpp elf_syms.cpp cli.cpp)
# verify_oracle F2: the oracle differential compare (pure; synthetic states).
add_executable(andes-sim-state-diff-test state_diff_test.cpp state_diff.cpp)
foreach(_t andes-sim-cli-test andes-sim-json-test andes-sim-infra-test andes-sim-plan-test andes-sim-plan-itest andes-sim-run-test andes-sim-elf-syms-test andes-sim-hybrid-test andes-sim-state-diff-test)

target_include_directories(andes-sim-infra-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andes-sim-plan-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2c RED->GREEN: `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` must print a positive
# estimated_cycles -- the whole-program weighted-CPI cycle estimate -- so
# the SimPoint mode shows the whole-program cycle figure required by the
# 4-mode model.
#
# Workload: rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf (markerless GEMM; exits naturally so
# the plugin's atexit drain reports the true N_total). simpoint mode
# always profiles to natural program exit -- no --icount knob.
#
# Manual TDD smoke test (runs the full SimPoint pipeline + estimate,
# ~1-2 min); not wired into scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)
HSIM="$ROOT/hsim.py"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf"
SIMPOINT_BIN="$ROOT/tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint"

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/log.sh"

[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"
[ -f "$ELF" ]  || fail "missing fixture: $ELF (run ./hsim.py build)"
if [ ! -x "$SIMPOINT_BIN" ]; then
  echo "[skip] $SIMPOINT_BIN not built"
  exit 0
fi

out=$(timeout 240 "$HSIM" run "$ELF" --mode simpoint \
        --interval 100 --max-k 2 2>&1)
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$out"; fail "--mode simpoint did not exit 0 (rc=$rc)"; }

n=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
{ [ -n "$n" ] && [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; } \
  || { echo "$out"; fail "estimated_cycles not a positive integer (got '${n:-}')"; }

echo "[ok] --mode simpoint printed estimated_cycles=$n"
echo "PASS test_simpoint_estimated_cycles"

done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"

ok "release --help: run/list only, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/doctor; hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list build test doctor state-diff; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done

done

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the

RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"

has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"

--- cell 3 (markdown) ---
## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:69-153`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is missing: no `satp`, no `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`, no PMP, no `fcsr`.
--- cell 6 (markdown) ---
## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`

content.text:
**L20 is easy - it is the easiest open Tier-1 item.** And yes, your hardware-config-driven state design is right; half of it already exists in the repo.

**Why L20 is easy** (I checked: `fcsr`/`frm`/`fflags` appear nowhere in `state_abi.h`, `hybrid_handoff.c`, `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`):

- `fcsr` is a plain read/write CSR with no side effects - no WARL traps, no ordering hazard like `vtype`/`vl` (which need `vsetvl`), no TLB flush like `satp`.
- Every transport surface already supports it: QEMU's gdbstub advertises `fcsr` by name next to the FPRs the plugin already reads; vsim's DMI Abstract Commands read/write CSR 0x003 directly - same Tier A path `vxsat`/`vxrm`/`vcsr` already use. It is a copy of an existing pattern.
- The wire format has room: carve 8 bytes from `reserved[216]`, same way the warmup metadata fields were added. Old state files read `fcsr=0` = reset value, so no version break.
- One ordering rule: restore after `mstatus` (FS must be on, which the FPR restore already guarantees); gate on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`.

Work: ~4 small edits (ABI field, plugin drain, resume write, drain read-back) plus the tests - an FP fixture that sets `frm=RTZ` before the ROI and checks the result and sticky `fflags` after. One feature-sized session.

**On config-driven state selection - agree, and the seams exist:**

What is already there:
- The wire format has exactly this gate: `HYBRID_FLAG_FP` / `HYBRID_FLAG_V` decide which state blocks are live, and `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` already honor them.
- The engine self-describes its hardware (`--describe` reports `vlen/dlen/elen/xlen` from the NDS config), and andes-sim already syncs `vlen` into the QEMU leg's `-cpu` line and rejects `xlen != 64`.

What is missing - the bridge you are describing:
- `--describe` does not report the ISA extension set (F, V, PMP present or not), so andes-sim assumes both legs are ax45mpv-shaped. If you drop in a no-V verilator config today, QEMU still drains V state and the resume would try to write V registers into a hart that has none.

My recommendation when you want it: add an extension list to the descriptor (one line in vsim's `describe_engine()`, read from the same config blob as `vlen`), have andes-sim derive the QEMU `-cpu` features from it the way `vlen` is derived now, and make `hybrid_hw_check` reject a state file whose flags demand a block the engine lacks. That is a small feature, not a redesign - the flag-gated ABI was built for exactly this.

---
name: reference-hybrid-unit-test-host-build
description: Fast host g++ build+run command for hybrid doctest unit tests (no container)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 170e2aea-625a-4764-89fa-e0722f44012b
---

The `verilator/tests/hybrid/*.test.cpp` doctest unit tests are header-only
(C++20 + ABI header) and run directly on the host - no podman/Verilator needed.
Build+run one with:

```sh
cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
g++ -std=c++20 -I verilator/src -I verilator/tests/hybrid -I include \
    -I verilator/external/doctest/doctest \
    verilator/tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp -o /tmp/t && /tmp/t
```

`-I verilator/tests/hybrid` is only needed for tests that include the shared
`recording_bus.hpp` (e.g. state_drain). This is the fast RED/GREEN loop; the
canonical container/ctest path is only required for the e2e suite.

Exceptions that do NOT link on the host: `qemu_handback.test.cpp` (needs libfmt:
`undefined reference to fmt::v11::...`), and the SystemC-dependent ones
(`*_smoke.cpp`, `shared_mem_offset.test.cpp`). Skip those on host.

vsim rebuild after editing `src/hybrid/*.hpp` or `src/simulator.hpp`:
`bash scripts/build_vsim.sh` (podman; incremental, recompiles `main.cpp.o` only,
RTL is cached - ~30s). Then e2e: `JOBS=8 FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.

1	/* rt_c_v_csrs.c - Round-trip fixture: V scalar CSR setup + drain
2	 * (2-phase: QEMU1 -> vsim).
3	 *
4	 * Configures vxsat, vxrm, vstart, vtype, and vl in the vsim ROI, then
5	 * drains -- exercising StateDrain's V-CSR capture path.
6	 *
7	 * Phase 1 (QEMU1): drain marker only (no V instructions; plugin PC
8	 *   drain constraint).
9	 * Phase 2 (vsim):  configure known V CSR values, then drain.
10	 *   - vsetvli: vl=8, vtype=e32/m1/ta/ma (0xD0)
11	 *   - csrw vxsat=1, vxrm=2, vstart=3 (vstart last: vsetvli resets it to 0)
12	 *
13	 * (The old phase-3 QEMU2 read-back + verify was removed with the QEMU2 leg;
14	 * the V CSRs now land in the drained hybrid_state_v1 only.)
15	 */
16	#include "runtime/rt_c_helpers.h"
17	
18	int main(void)
19	{
20	  /* Phase 1 (QEMU1): no V instructions before the drain marker. */
21	  enter_vsim();
22	
23	  /* Phase 2 (vsim): set known V CSR values.
24	   * crt0.S already set mstatus.VS=non-Off so vsetvli doesn't trap.
25	   * vstart must be written last: vsetvli resets vstart to 0. */
26	  asm volatile(
27	    "li     a0, 8\n"
28	    "vsetvli t0, a0, e32, m1, ta, ma\n"  /* vl=8, vtype=0xD0 */
29	    "li     t1, 1\n"
30	    "csrw   vxsat, t1\n"
31	    "li     t1, 2\n"
32	    "csrw   vxrm,  t1\n"
33	    "li     t1, 3\n"
34	    "csrw   vstart, t1\n"
35	    ::: "t0", "t1", "a0", "memory");
36	
37	  exit_vsim();
38	
39	  return 0;
40	}

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13):
  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@3392, minstret_at_measure_start@3400.
  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 3392 "$STATE_VSIM")
    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 3400 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

 *
 * Syscalls: all C-level fixtures link the vplat runtime
 * (build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a, no semihosting): newlib stdio
 * bottoms out in the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io in the SimControl
 * device, which BOTH engines model. A syscall inside the
 * enter_vsim()/exit_vsim() span therefore works on vsim too -- it just
 * adds its real cycles (UART polling, dcache flush) to the measured
 * figure, so cycle-measuring fixtures keep the span syscall-free by
 * choice, not by rule.

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers: the HINT pair
 * `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (ENTER) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (EXIT). Match
 * insn_match.h. rd=x0 makes each marker an architectural NOP, so marked
 * binaries also run standalone on every engine.
 *
 * marker mode pattern-matches the HINT insns directly; the helpers do not
 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

/* A pure compiler memory barrier (emits no instructions): forces pending
 * memory writes to complete and bars reordering across it. enter_vsim /
 * exit_vsim already carry this clobber on their marker insn, so the markers
 * anchor a kernel's output stores; markerless builds (-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS)
 * call roi_anchor() to pin those stores instead. */
static inline void roi_anchor(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

# to bypass the env var.

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)

LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# user-facing andes-sim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andes-sim.ld, same content).

LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall

# All fixtures share andes-sim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandes_sim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andes-sim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).

                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andes_sim/roi.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).

     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for

	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andes-sim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o

# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).

	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/roi.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andes-sim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem

--- cell 3 ---
## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:69-153`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note

  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.

  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.

## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)

> Re-check 2026-06-12: four areas moved since this assessment. The vplat
> runtime gives a supported I/O path inside the ROI (L1/L9; every in-tree
> C fixture now links it, so L1 is resolved in-tree); `--verify` and
> `--cosim` add a value-level oracle check for marker/pc runs (L15); engines
> are drop-in with VLEN synced from the descriptor (L10/L11); the marker

> overall scores below still stand.

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static (L1-L6). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip (L20)
   - an FP workload that touches rounding mode will look numerically
   fine but be wrong. `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR restore
   is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** "M-mode only, no traps, no paging,
   no semihosting inside the window" (L1-L6) rules out every real
   OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything
   with page faults. The vplat runtime covers bare-metal I/O only.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 4 CSRs restored into vsim.** `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,
   `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into
   vsim (`resume_driver.hpp:69-153`). They exist in the wire format
   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata already ate 16 bytes;
   `state_abi.h:85-88`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook, 21 entries plus
  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- S-mode + traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4, L6)
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- `fcsr` fix (close L20)
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- The existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to
  icount/simpoint and wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. First written 2026-05-28 as
`docs/limitation.md`; re-checked entry by entry against the code and moved
into this notebook on **2026-06-12** (line references refreshed; statuses
updated where the code moved).

How this notebook relates to the other docs:

- `ROADMAP.md` (top level) - the master feature roadmap. Every open
  limitation below is absorbed there as an `F-ENG-*` feature; that file is
  the *plan to fix*. This notebook stays the *plain-English "do not do
  this" list* and the source of the L-ids.
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - the older failure-mode backlog (`F-T*`) and the
  gem5-parity bug-audit wave (`B1-B20`, fully closed), both superseded by
  `ROADMAP.md`. Kept for history.

Each `Where` line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.

<cell id="cell-3"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:69-153`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is missing: no `satp`, no `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`, no PMP, no `fcsr`.</cell id="cell-3">

<cell id="cell-5"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`)
MUST be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No semihosting (exception: the vplat runtime's MMIO-backed
  stdio / exit / file io is supported inside the ROI, see L1)
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO other than the vplat device set, UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (see L9)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.</cell id="cell-5">
<cell id="cell-6"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- `fcsr / frm / fflags` (FP rounding mode + sticky flags). See L20.
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only four CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret` (`resume_driver.hpp:69-153`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[216]` fits about 27 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set (`fcsr`, S-mode trap
CSRs, a chosen Andes microarch subset) in a v2 layout is feasible.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).</cell id="cell-6">
<cell id="cell-7"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No semihosting inside the ROI; vplat is the supported I/O path  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and
  `exit_vsim()`, when linked against a semihosting runtime (`-lgloss_vh`)
  instead of the shipped vplat runtime.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}` (the semihosting runtime).
- Status: RESOLVED IN-TREE (2026-06-12). The vplat runtime
  (`build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`, sources in `runtime/`, link with
  `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`) routes stdio to UART2, exit to
  SimControl, and file io to HTIF -- MMIO devices both engines model -- so
  `printf` / `exit` / `fopen` inside the ROI work on fast, cycle AND hybrid
  (see USER_GUIDE section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`). Every C fixture
  in the repo now links it (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`); nothing in-tree
  uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore, and the plugin's drain-at-exit record became
  context-free so the SimPoint profile pass works with the SimControl exit
  path (`tests/plugin/test_plugin_drain_at_exit.sh`). The limitation
  survives only for EXTERNAL binaries linked with a semihosting libgloss:
  there the old rule stands -- keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg,
  before the ROI), or relink with the vplat runtime.

Live proof of the vplat path - `vplat_hello.elf` prints from INSIDE the
measured window, serviced by the cycle-accurate vsim leg, and the run

<cell id="cell-9"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:343-345`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.
  Also `mepc`/trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap
  handling inside the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:73-111` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside.
- What happens: `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and `fflags[4:0]`) is not
  in `hybrid_state_v1`. The plugin does not drain it; the resume step
  does not restore it; the drain does not read it back. vsim sees the
  reset value (RNE, no flags). FP results inside the ROI use the wrong
  rounding; sticky flags after the ROI are wrong.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no `fcsr` field);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no `fcsr` handle in `VcpuRegs`);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no `fcsr` restore).
- Status: OPEN. Concrete next move: add `uint64_t fcsr` from
  `reserved[]`, drain alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is
  enabled, and drain it back at vsim exit.</cell id="cell-9">
<cell id="cell-10"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at
  the trigger boundary.
- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
  `state_drain.hpp:53` and `hybrid_handoff.c:314`. On the vsim side
  DCSR.prv is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. S/U code
  then raises illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:53`, `hybrid_handoff.c:314`.
- Status: OPEN.

The hardcode is one line on each side of the handoff:</cell id="cell-10">

<cell id="cell-12"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)

- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default
  128 MB shared memory.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
  corruption.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:175` (128 MB default); `--mem-size` exists and
  its syntax is validated, but nothing validates ELF size against it.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mem-size` large enough by hand.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
  both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI: only the vplat device set is handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches any device OTHER than the vplat set - PLIC,
  the timer (`mtime`/`mtimecmp`), ROM, or aliased/device memory - or expects
  device STATE to survive the handoff.
- What happens: UART2 (`0xf0300000`) and SimControl/HTIF (`0xe0080000`) are
  modeled by BOTH engines (QEMU: `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` + the ae350
  memmap; vsim: the AE350 RTL platform natively), so vplat stdio / exit /
  file io inside the ROI work and the hybrid leg relays vsim's UART output.
  Any other device range is engine-specific behavior. And no device state
  (UART FIFO contents, pending interrupts, timer compare) crosses the
  handoff - only RAM is shared; each engine has its own device instances.
- Where: `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:95,107` (SimControl + UART2 memmap);
  `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`.
- Status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (2026-06): vplat device set works; everything
  else and cross-handoff device state still OPEN.</cell id="cell-12">
<cell id="cell-13"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andes-sim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`), and the V-register scratch address is the
  constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), only
  correct when RAM base is 0 (true for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt`
  where it would need 0x80FF0000). The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED (2026-06): engine variant + VLEN are pluggable;
  the machine, the CPU family, and the scratch GPA still block porting to
  another core.

### L11. VLEN ceiling is 512 bits, and an over-limit vlenb truncates silently  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: an engine whose VLEN exceeds 512, or a run outside the
  driver where the two legs' VLEN configs are set by hand.
- What happens: inside `andes-sim run` the QEMU leg's vlen is copied from
  the engine descriptor (the `{vlen}` template,
  `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`), so the two legs can no longer disagree
  by construction. What remains: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per
  vector register (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`) and the
  plugin CLAMPS the drained bytes to that with no warning
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:375-377`) - a VLEN > 512 engine silently loses the
  upper bytes of every V register. The standalone fast model also hardcodes
  `vlen=512` (`engine_registry.cpp:54`). The retired Python golden keeps a
  duplicated constant (`checkpoint.py:44`, `LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`).
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `hybrid_handoff.c:375-377`,
  `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: leg-mismatch half CLOSED by the descriptor sync (2026-06); the
  512-bit ceiling and the silent clamp remain OPEN.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andes_sim/roi.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:663-671` (marker matcher);
  `verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:663-671`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you
  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary (`hsim.py:1126-1225`,
  `_run_simpoint_pipeline`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at
     each window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without
     warmup the CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate
     inherits SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py:1126-1225` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`). Note: SimPoint
  still runs only on the Python golden (`./hsim.py`); the C++ port has not
  landed.
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
  software-visible (must round-trip).</cell id="cell-13">
<cell id="cell-14"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. Value-level handoff check: shipped for marker/pc, missing for icount/simpoint  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: `run --verify` (marker/pc only, dev tier) re-runs the ELF
  on a pure-QEMU oracle and diffs the FULL drained state field by field
  (`driver/cmd_run.cpp:245-282`); `--cosim [--cosim-interval N]` goes
  further and localizes a divergence to the first bad N-retire window
  (it suppresses the cycle figure - the checkpoint drains pollute it; rerun
  without `--cosim` to measure). Both are manual, not CI-wired. The icount
  trigger and the SimPoint pipeline (`hsim.py`) still assert only exit code
  and PC range - a wrong register value there passes silently.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:156` (marker/pc gate), `:245-282` (oracle);
  `hsim.py` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`) - unchecked.
- Status: PARTIALLY CLOSED (2026-06): marker/pc covered by
  `--verify`/`--cosim`; icount + simpoint coverage and CI wiring still OPEN.

### L16. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] CSR restore to QEMU2 silently skipped

- The QEMU2 leg restored CSRs by gdbstub name and skipped quietly when the
  stub did not advertise one. The leg no longer exists.
- Status: REMOVED.

### L17. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] gdbstub timeout + racy port pick

- The handback's fixed 10 s gdbstub timeout and TOCTOU port pick died with
  the leg.
- Status: REMOVED.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing
  hosts with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no
  byte-swap path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror (golden only) uses
  a native-endian `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:28-31`), so a BE host would
  mis-parse the body while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent
  mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:28-31`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.</cell id="cell-14">
<cell id="cell-15"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)

The QEMU2 handback leg has been removed entirely (2026-06-09). The
simulator is now 2-phase: QEMU1 drains architectural state to the
`hybrid_state_v1` file and exits; vsim resumes from that file, runs the
ROI cycle-accurately, and drains again. There is no third phase.
`CLAUDE.md` and `USER_GUIDE.md` have been updated to match; only older
architecture notes that still describe a QEMU2 spawn or a gdbstub
P-packet restore are stale - that code path no longer exists.</cell id="cell-15">

| ID  | Limitation                              | Severity | Status |

<cell id="cell-17"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)

> Re-check 2026-06-12: four areas moved since this assessment. The vplat
> runtime gives a supported I/O path inside the ROI (L1/L9; every in-tree
> C fixture now links it, so L1 is resolved in-tree); `--verify` and
> `--cosim` add a value-level oracle check for marker/pc runs (L15); engines
> are drop-in with VLEN synced from the descriptor (L10/L11); the marker
> HINT trigger retired the CSR-collision caveats (L12/L13). The state
> coverage and ROI envelope items (L2-L6, L20, L21) are unchanged, so the
> overall scores below still stand.

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static (L1-L6). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip (L20)
   - an FP workload that touches rounding mode will look numerically
   fine but be wrong. `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR restore
   is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** "M-mode only, no traps, no paging,
   no semihosting inside the window" (L1-L6) rules out every real
   OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything
   with page faults. The vplat runtime covers bare-metal I/O only.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 4 CSRs restored into vsim.** `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,
   `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into
   vsim (`resume_driver.hpp:69-153`). They exist in the wire format
   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata already ate 16 bytes;
   `state_abi.h:85-88`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook, 21 entries plus
  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- S-mode + traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4, L6)
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- `fcsr` fix (close L20)
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- The existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to
  icount/simpoint and wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.</cell id="cell-17">

# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. First written 2026-05-28 as
`docs/limitation.md`; re-checked entry by entry against the code and moved
into this notebook on **2026-06-12** (line references refreshed; statuses
updated where the code moved).

How this notebook relates to the other docs:

- `ROADMAP.md` (top level) - the master feature roadmap. Every open
  limitation below is absorbed there as an `F-ENG-*` feature; that file is
  the *plan to fix*. This notebook stays the *plain-English "do not do
  this" list* and the source of the L-ids.
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - the older failure-mode backlog (`F-T*`) and the
  gem5-parity bug-audit wave (`B1-B20`, fully closed), both superseded by
  `ROADMAP.md`. Kept for history.

Each `Where` line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.
The code cells run real commands against this repo, so the key claims are
shown, not just stated.

## Setup

Prerequisites: the driver, the simulators, and the test fixtures are already
built (`build/andes-sim`, `verilator/build/sim_*`, `build/qemu/...`, the
QEMU plugin, and `tests/fixtures/*.elf`). If any are missing, run
`source ./setup.sh` from the repo root.

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:69-153`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is missing: no `satp`, no `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`, no PMP, no `fcsr`.
!grep -n "static constexpr uint16_t kCsr" verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp

So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`)
MUST be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No semihosting (exception: the vplat runtime's MMIO-backed
  stdio / exit / file io is supported inside the ROI, see L1)
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO other than the vplat device set, UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (see L9)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- `fcsr / frm / fflags` (FP rounding mode + sticky flags). See L20.
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only four CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret` (`resume_driver.hpp:69-153`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[216]` fits about 27 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set (`fcsr`, S-mode trap
CSRs, a chosen Andes microarch subset) in a v2 layout is feasible.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).

## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No semihosting inside the ROI; vplat is the supported I/O path  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and
  `exit_vsim()`, when linked against a semihosting runtime (`-lgloss_vh`)
  instead of the shipped vplat runtime.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}` (the semihosting runtime).
- Status: RESOLVED IN-TREE (2026-06-12). The vplat runtime
  (`build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`, sources in `runtime/`, link with
  `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`) routes stdio to UART2, exit to
  SimControl, and file io to HTIF -- MMIO devices both engines model -- so
  `printf` / `exit` / `fopen` inside the ROI work on fast, cycle AND hybrid
  (see USER_GUIDE section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`). Every C fixture
  in the repo now links it (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`); nothing in-tree
  uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore, and the plugin's drain-at-exit record became
  context-free so the SimPoint profile pass works with the SimControl exit
  path (`tests/plugin/test_plugin_drain_at_exit.sh`). The limitation
  survives only for EXTERNAL binaries linked with a semihosting libgloss:
  there the old rule stands -- keep all I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg,
  before the ROI), or relink with the vplat runtime.

Live proof of the vplat path - `vplat_hello.elf` prints from INSIDE the
measured window, serviced by the cycle-accurate vsim leg, and the run
still produces a clean `window_cycles` figure:

!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
    --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf

outputs.text:
[andes-sim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=pc fixture=vplat_hello
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.7 GiB)
Copyright (C) 2013-2026 Andes Technology Corporation. All rights reserved.
Version : unknown

hello from vplat
[pc window_cycles] 15938  (vsim mcycle=1013220539018694 - qemu mcycle=1013220539002756)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger pc (vplat_hello)

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:343-345`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.
  Also `mepc`/trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap
  handling inside the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:73-111` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside.
- What happens: `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and `fflags[4:0]`) is not
  in `hybrid_state_v1`. The plugin does not drain it; the resume step
  does not restore it; the drain does not read it back. vsim sees the
  reset value (RNE, no flags). FP results inside the ROI use the wrong
  rounding; sticky flags after the ROI are wrong.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no `fcsr` field);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no `fcsr` handle in `VcpuRegs`);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no `fcsr` restore).
- Status: OPEN. Concrete next move: add `uint64_t fcsr` from
  `reserved[]`, drain alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is
  enabled, and drain it back at vsim exit.

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at
  the trigger boundary.
- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
  `state_drain.hpp:53` and `hybrid_handoff.c:314`. On the vsim side
  DCSR.prv is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. S/U code
  then raises illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:53`, `hybrid_handoff.c:314`.
- Status: OPEN.

The hardcode is one line on each side of the handoff:
!grep -n "priv" verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c | grep "= 3"

outputs.text:
verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp:53:    state.priv    = 3;
qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:314:    s.priv    = 3;
