### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)

- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default
  128 MB shared memory.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
  corruption.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:175` (128 MB default); `--mem-size` exists and
  its syntax is validated, but nothing validates ELF size against it.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mem-size` large enough by hand.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
  both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI: only the vplat device set is handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches any device OTHER than the vplat set - PLIC,
  the timer (`mtime`/`mtimecmp`), ROM, or aliased/device memory - or expects
  device STATE to survive the handoff.
- What happens: UART2 (`0xf0300000`) and SimControl/HTIF (`0xe0080000`) are
  modeled by BOTH engines (QEMU: `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` + the ae350
  memmap; vsim: the AE350 RTL platform natively), so vplat stdio / exit /
  file io inside the ROI work and the hybrid leg relays vsim's UART output.
  Any other device range is engine-specific behavior. And no device state
  (UART FIFO contents, pending interrupts, timer compare) crosses the
  handoff - only RAM is shared; each engine has its own device instances.
- Where: `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:95,107` (SimControl + UART2 memmap);
  `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`.
- Status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (2026-06): vplat device set works; everything
  else and cross-handoff device state still OPEN.

## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andes-sim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`), and the V-register scratch address is the
  constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), only
  correct when RAM base is 0 (true for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt`
  where it would need 0x80FF0000). The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED (2026-06): engine variant + VLEN are pluggable;
  the machine, the CPU family, and the scratch GPA still block porting to
  another core.

### L11. VLEN ceiling is 512 bits, and an over-limit vlenb truncates silently  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: an engine whose VLEN exceeds 512, or a run outside the
  driver where the two legs' VLEN configs are set by hand.
- What happens: inside `andes-sim run` the QEMU leg's vlen is copied from
  the engine descriptor (the `{vlen}` template,
  `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`), so the two legs can no longer disagree
  by construction. What remains: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per
  vector register (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`) and the
  plugin CLAMPS the drained bytes to that with no warning
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:375-377`) - a VLEN > 512 engine silently loses the
  upper bytes of every V register. The standalone fast model also hardcodes
  `vlen=512` (`engine_registry.cpp:54`). The retired Python golden keeps a
  duplicated constant (`checkpoint.py:44`, `LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`).
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `hybrid_handoff.c:375-377`,
  `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: leg-mismatch half CLOSED by the descriptor sync (2026-06); the
  512-bit ceiling and the silent clamp remain OPEN.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andes_sim/roi.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:663-671` (marker matcher);
  `verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:663-671`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you
  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary (`hsim.py:1126-1225`,
  `_run_simpoint_pipeline`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at
     each window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without
     warmup the CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate
     inherits SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py:1126-1225` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`). Note: SimPoint
  still runs only on the Python golden (`./hsim.py`); the C++ port has not
  landed.
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
  software-visible (must round-trip).

## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. Value-level handoff check: shipped for marker/pc, missing for icount/simpoint  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: `run --verify` (marker/pc only, dev tier) re-runs the ELF
  on a pure-QEMU oracle and diffs the FULL drained state field by field
  (`driver/cmd_run.cpp:245-282`); `--cosim [--cosim-interval N]` goes
  further and localizes a divergence to the first bad N-retire window
  (it suppresses the cycle figure - the checkpoint drains pollute it; rerun
  without `--cosim` to measure). Both are manual, not CI-wired. The icount
  trigger and the SimPoint pipeline (`hsim.py`) still assert only exit code
  and PC range - a wrong register value there passes silently.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:156` (marker/pc gate), `:245-282` (oracle);
  `hsim.py` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`) - unchecked.
- Status: PARTIALLY CLOSED (2026-06): marker/pc covered by
  `--verify`/`--cosim`; icount + simpoint coverage and CI wiring still OPEN.

### L16. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] CSR restore to QEMU2 silently skipped

- The QEMU2 leg restored CSRs by gdbstub name and skipped quietly when the
  stub did not advertise one. The leg no longer exists.
- Status: REMOVED.

### L17. [REMOVED: the QEMU2 handback leg was deleted 2026-06-09] gdbstub timeout + racy port pick

- The handback's fixed 10 s gdbstub timeout and TOCTOU port pick died with
  the leg.
- Status: REMOVED.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing
  hosts with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no
  byte-swap path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror (golden only) uses
  a native-endian `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:28-31`), so a BE host would
  mis-parse the body while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent
  mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:28-31`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)

The QEMU2 handback leg has been removed entirely (2026-06-09). The
simulator is now 2-phase: QEMU1 drains architectural state to the
`hybrid_state_v1` file and exits; vsim resumes from that file, runs the
ROI cycle-accurately, and drains again. There is no third phase.
`CLAUDE.md` and `USER_GUIDE.md` have been updated to match; only older
architecture notes that still describe a QEMU2 spawn or a gdbstub
P-packet restore are stale - that code path no longer exists.

## Quick reference

| ID  | Limitation                              | Severity | Status |
|-----|-----------------------------------------|----------|--------|
| L1  | Semihosting in ROI fatal; vplat is the supported I/O path | blocker | resolved in-tree |
| L2  | PMP not restored to vsim                | high     | open   |
| L3  | Paging (satp) off in ROI                | high     | open   |
| L4  | Trap state lost across ROI              | high     | open   |
| L5  | LR/SC cannot cross handoff              | high     | open   |
| L6  | Privilege forced to M-mode              | high     | open   |
| L7  | 128 MB mmap, no bounds check            | medium   | open   |
| L8  | Single hart only                        | medium   | open   |
| L9  | MMIO in ROI: vplat device set only      | medium   | partial |
| L10 | Engines pluggable; machine + scratch GPA fixed | medium | partial |
| L11 | VLEN ceiling 512, over-limit clamp silent | medium | partial |
| L12 | CSR 0x7C0 trigger collision             | low      | resolved |
| L13 | Marker must be 32-bit                   | low      | resolved |
| L14 | SimPoint estimate is approximate        | medium   | by design |
| L15 | Value-level check: marker/pc only       | medium   | partial |
| L16 | CSR restore silently skipped if missing | medium   | removed |
| L17 | Fixed gdbstub timeout + racy port       | low      | removed |
| L18 | Little-endian / same-arch only          | low      | by design |
| L19 | Determinism / drift / fault-injection   | low      | open   |
| L20 | fcsr/frm/fflags not transported         | high     | open   |
| L21 | Andes vendor CSRs not transported       | high     | open   |

## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)

> Re-check 2026-06-12: four areas moved since this assessment. The vplat
> runtime gives a supported I/O path inside the ROI (L1/L9; every in-tree
> C fixture now links it, so L1 is resolved in-tree); `--verify` and
> `--cosim` add a value-level oracle check for marker/pc runs (L15); engines
> are drop-in with VLEN synced from the descriptor (L10/L11); the marker
> HINT trigger retired the CSR-collision caveats (L12/L13). The state
> coverage and ROI envelope items (L2-L6, L20, L21) are unchanged, so the
> overall scores below still stand.

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static (L1-L6). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip (L20)
   - an FP workload that touches rounding mode will look numerically
   fine but be wrong. `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR restore
   is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** "M-mode only, no traps, no paging,
   no semihosting inside the window" (L1-L6) rules out every real
   OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything
   with page faults. The vplat runtime covers bare-metal I/O only.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 4 CSRs restored into vsim.** `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,
   `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into
   vsim (`resume_driver.hpp:69-153`). They exist in the wire format
   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata already ate 16 bytes;
   `state_abi.h:85-88`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook, 21 entries plus
  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- S-mode + traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4, L6)
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- `fcsr` fix (close L20)
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- The existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to
  icount/simpoint and wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.

    "\n",

    "\n",
    "> Re-check 2026-06-12: four areas moved since this assessment. The vplat\n",
    "> runtime gives a supported I/O path inside the ROI (L1/L9; every in-tree\n",
    "> C fixture now links it, so L1 is resolved in-tree); `--verify` and\n",
    "> `--cosim` add a value-level oracle check for marker/pc runs (L15); engines\n",
    "> are drop-in with VLEN synced from the descriptor (L10/L11); the marker\n",
    "> HINT trigger retired the CSR-collision caveats (L12/L13). The state\n",
    "> coverage and ROI envelope items (L2-L6, L20, L21) are unchanged, so the\n",
    "> overall scores below still stand.\n",
    "\n",
    "Honest scorecard for \"is this a shippable commercial product today?\".\n",
    "Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,\n",
    "gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.\n",
    "\n",
    "**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal\n",
    "/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**\n",
    "\n",
    "### Axis breakdown\n",
    "\n",
    "| Axis                                  | Score | Note |\n",
    "|---------------------------------------|-------|------|\n",
    "| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |\n",
    "| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |\n",
    "| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |\n",
    "| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static (L1-L6). |\n",
    "| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |\n",
    "| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |\n",
    "| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |\n",
    "| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |\n",
    "| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |\n",
    "| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |\n",
    "\n",
    "### What blocks commercial shipping\n",
    "\n",
    "1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip (L20)\n",
    "   - an FP workload that touches rounding mode will look numerically\n",
    "   fine but be wrong. `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR restore\n",
    "   is observable only through a private counter\n",
    "   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).\n",
    "2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** \"M-mode only, no traps, no paging,\n",
    "   no semihosting inside the window\" (L1-L6) rules out every real\n",
    "   OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything\n",
    "   with page faults. The vplat runtime covers bare-metal I/O only.\n",
    "3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero\n",
    "   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a\n",
    "   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher\n",
    "   controls shape the cycle count.\n",
    "4. **Only 4 CSRs restored into vsim.** `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,\n",
    "   `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into\n",
    "   vsim (`resume_driver.hpp:69-153`). They exist in the wire format\n",
    "   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic\n",
    "   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.\n",
    "5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field\n",
    "   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata already ate 16 bytes;\n",
    "   `state_abi.h:85-88`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond\n",
    "   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.\n",
    "6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim\n",
    "   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,\n",
    "   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a\n",
    "   commercial CI matrix.\n",
    "\n",
    "### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)\n",
    "\n",
    "- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.\n",
    "- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.\n",
    "- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook, 21 entries plus\n",
    "  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that\n",
    "  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.\n",
    "- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a\n",
    "  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.\n",
    "\n",
    "### Bottom line\n",
    "\n",
    "Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial\n",
    "release you need:\n",
    "\n",
    "- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path\n",
    "- S-mode + traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4, L6)\n",
    "- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)\n",
    "- `fcsr` fix (close L20)\n",
    "- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing\n",
    "- The existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to\n",
    "  icount/simpoint and wired into CI\n",
    "\n",
    "Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks."
   ]
  }

## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:343-345`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.
  Also `mepc`/trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap
  handling inside the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:73-111` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bit: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside. `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and
  `fflags[4:0]`) was not in `hybrid_state_v1`, so vsim ran the ROI with
  the reset value (RNE, no flags): FP results inside the ROI used the
  wrong rounding, and sticky flags after the ROI were wrong.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12). `fcsr` now round-trips end to end,
  gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`:
  - wire format: `uint64_t fcsr` carved from `reserved[]`
    (`state_abi.h`; offset locked by `state_abi_check.h`; pre-fix state
    files read back 0 = the old reset-value behavior, so no version bump);
  - QEMU1 drain: the plugin reads the `fcsr` gdbstub register alongside
    the FPRs (`hybrid_handoff.c`);
  - vsim resume: written via the abstract-or-PB CSR path right after the
    FPRs, under the same `mstatus.FS` enable (`resume_driver.hpp`);
  - vsim drain: re-read into the drained file, and `--verify` /
    `state-diff` now compare it (`state_drain.hpp`,
    `driver/state_diff.cpp`).
  Proven by `tests/fixtures/rt_c_fcsr.c` (frm=RTZ + sticky NX set before
  the enter marker, in-ROI self-check, distinct sentinel captured at the
  exit drain) - run via `tests/hybrid/e2e_fcsr_roundtrip.sh` and the
  regular marker/pc e2e suite (`scripts/run_e2e.sh`).

   "source": "## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only five CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret, fcsr` (`resume_driver.hpp`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."

   "source": "### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:343-345`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.
  Also `mepc`/trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap
  handling inside the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:73-111` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bit: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside. `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and
  `fflags[4:0]`) was not in `hybrid_state_v1`, so vsim ran the ROI with
  the reset value (RNE, no flags): FP results inside the ROI used the
  wrong rounding, and sticky flags after the ROI were wrong.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12). `fcsr` now round-trips end to end,
  gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`:
  - wire format: `uint64_t fcsr` carved from `reserved[]`
    (`state_abi.h`; offset locked by `state_abi_check.h`; pre-fix state
    files read back 0 = the old reset-value behavior, so no version bump);
  - QEMU1 drain: the plugin reads the `fcsr` gdbstub register alongside
    the FPRs (`hybrid_handoff.c`);
  - vsim resume: written via the abstract-or-PB CSR path right after the
    FPRs, under the same `mstatus.FS` enable (`resume_driver.hpp`);
  - vsim drain: re-read into the drained file, and `--verify` /
    `state-diff` now compare it (`state_drain.hpp`,
    `driver/state_diff.cpp`).
  Proven by `tests/fixtures/rt_c_fcsr.c` (frm=RTZ + sticky NX set before
  the enter marker, in-ROI self-check, distinct sentinel captured at the
  exit drain) - run via `tests/hybrid/e2e_fcsr_roundtrip.sh` and the
  regular marker/pc e2e suite (`scripts/run_e2e.sh`)."

  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only five CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret, fcsr` (`resume_driver.hpp`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."

   "source": "### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:343-345`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.
  Also `mepc`/trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap
  handling inside the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:73-111` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bit: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside. `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and
  `fflags[4:0]`) was not in `hybrid_state_v1`, so vsim ran the ROI with
  the reset value (RNE, no flags): FP results inside the ROI used the
  wrong rounding, and sticky flags after the ROI were wrong.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12). `fcsr` now round-trips end to end,

  - wire format: `uint64_t fcsr` carved from `reserved[]`

- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |

  silently disappears.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.
  Also `mepc`/trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap
  handling inside the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:73-111` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation

## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)

> Re-check 2026-06-12: five areas moved since this assessment. The vplat
> runtime gives a supported I/O path inside the ROI (L1/L9; every in-tree
> C fixture now links it, so L1 is resolved in-tree); `--verify` and
> `--cosim` add a value-level oracle check for marker/pc runs (L15); engines
> are drop-in with VLEN synced from the descriptor (L10/L11); the marker
> HINT trigger retired the CSR-collision caveats (L12/L13); and `fcsr`
> now round-trips with an FP-rounding fixture in the e2e suite (L20
> resolved - five CSRs restore into vsim now, and the silent FP-rounding
> gap in blocker 1 below is closed). The remaining state coverage and ROI
> envelope items (L2-L6, L21) are unchanged, so the overall scores below
> still stand.

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static (L1-L6). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** ~~`fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip
   (L20)~~ - resolved 2026-06-12; `fcsr` now transports and `--verify`
   compares it. Still standing: `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR
   restore is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** "M-mode only, no traps, no paging,
   no semihosting inside the window" (L1-L6) rules out every real
   OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything
   with page faults. The vplat runtime covers bare-metal I/O only.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 5 CSRs restored into vsim** (mstatus, mtvec, mcycle,
   minstret, fcsr). `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,
   `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into
   vsim (`resume_driver.hpp`). They exist in the wire format
   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata ate 16 bytes, fcsr another
   8; `state_abi.h`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook, 21 entries plus
  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- S-mode + traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4, L6)
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- ~~`fcsr` fix (close L20)~~ done 2026-06-12
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- The existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to
  icount/simpoint and wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.

   "source": "## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

   "source": "## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only five CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret, fcsr` (`resume_driver.hpp`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload
",
    "
",
    "### L1. No semihosting inside the ROI; vplat is the supported I/O path  (F-T1.1)

   "source": "### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:343-345`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.
  Also `mepc`/trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap
  handling inside the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:73-111` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bit: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside. `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and
  `fflags[4:0]`) was not in `hybrid_state_v1`, so vsim ran the ROI with
  the reset value (RNE, no flags): FP results inside the ROI used the
  wrong rounding, and sticky flags after the ROI were wrong.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12). `fcsr` now round-trips end to end,
  gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`:
  - wire format: `uint64_t fcsr` carved from `reserved[]`
    (`state_abi.h`; offset locked by `state_abi_check.h`; pre-fix state
    files read back 0 = the old reset-value behavior, so no version bump);
  - QEMU1 drain: the plugin reads the `fcsr` gdbstub register alongside
    the FPRs (`hybrid_handoff.c`);
  - vsim resume: written via the abstract-or-PB CSR path right after the
    FPRs, under the same `mstatus.FS` enable (`resume_driver.hpp`);
  - vsim drain: re-read into the drained file, and `--verify` /
    `state-diff` now compare it (`state_drain.hpp`,
    `driver/state_diff.cpp`).

  exit drain) - run via `tests/hybrid/e2e_fcsr_roundtrip.sh` and the
  regular marker/pc e2e suite (`scripts/run_e2e.sh`)."

",

",

",
    "> runtime gives a supported I/O path inside the ROI (L1/L9; every in-tree

",

",
    "> overall scores below still stand.
",

",
    "Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
",
    "Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
",
    "gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.
",
    "
",
    "**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
",
    "/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**
",
    "
",
    "### Axis breakdown
",
    "
",
    "| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
",
    "|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
",
    "| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
",
    "| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
",
    "| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
",
    "| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static (L1-L6). |
",
    "| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
",

",

",

",

",

",

",

   "source": "## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only five CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret, fcsr` (`resume_driver.hpp`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."

   "source": "### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:343-345`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:34-44` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through into the drained state
  file. Any trap-diagnostic logic reading that state sees wrong values.
  Also `mepc`/trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap
  handling inside the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:73-111` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.

**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`. The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but with the QEMU2 leg removed those extra CSRs are no longer restored anywhere -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

### Trigger Modes

The repo ships 4 switching modes, split by what they profile.

Kernel modes (measure one region you choose):
- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andes_sim/roi.h>` (`andes_sim_roi_begin()/end()`).
- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.

Whole-program modes (sample by instruction count):
- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for marker-less workloads.
- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices (interval = insns per slice), cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate. Drive via `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` (or the equivalent `./hsim.py estimate`) -- Python golden only until the C++ port lands. The bbv-profile / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.

`./andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc|icount` is the unified orchestrator (`./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` for SimPoint); `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.

### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)

`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64` supports VLEN up to 512 bits. Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.

Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `verilator/tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`.

### V-State Transport

1	// V-register transport staging: the host<->guest-RAM half of the V data
2	// regfile transfer. The Debug Module abstract-command space has no slots for
3	// v0..v31 (the RISC-V Debug Spec leaves V to the Program Buffer or
4	// implementation-specific extensions), so vsim moves v0..v31 by executing a
5	// vle8.v/vse8.v sweep on the halted hart through the Program Buffer (see
6	// pb_v_data_sweep in program_buffer.hpp, driven by ResumeDriver on resume and
7	// StateDrain at drain). That sweep loads/stores a fixed scratch region of
8	// guest RAM (kVScratchGpa); this header provides the matching host-side copy:
9	//
10	//   - stage_v_to_scratch: state.vreg[] -> scratch RAM, called before resume so
11	//     the ResumeDriver vle8.v sweep reads QEMU 1's V values.
12	//   - read_v_from_scratch: scratch RAM -> state.vreg[], called after the
13	//     StateDrain vse8.v sweep so the drained v0..v31 land in state.vreg[]
14	//     (the handoff file).
15	//
16	// The transfer is transparent to the workload: benchmark binaries issue no
17	// transport code, only the enter_vsim / exit_vsim markers. rt_c_v_regs.c is
18	// the reference fixture.
19	//
20	// Pure logic: no SystemC, no DMI bus. Easy to unit-test.
21	
22	#pragma once
23	
24	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
25	
26	#include <cstddef>
27	#include <cstdint>
28	#include <cstring>
29	#include <span>
30	#include <stdexcept>
31	
32	namespace hybrid
33	{
34	
35	// Reserved scratch slot inside the shared mmap. Sits well above the C
36	// runtime's _stack (rt_c.ld places it at RAM_BASE + 0x700000), giving the
37	// stack ~9 MiB of headroom before colliding with this 2 KiB region. On
38	// `-M andes_ae350` RAM is at 0x00000000 and the GPA is 0x00FF0000; on
39	// `-M virt` it would be 0x80FF0000. ResumeDriver/StateDrain stage the PB
40	// sweep's base pointer (x7) directly from this constant, so it is the single
41	// source of truth -- no fixture-side literal to keep in sync.
42	inline constexpr uint64_t kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000ull;
43	
44	// Total scratch bytes needed: 32 V regs × HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX. Sized to
45	// the maximum supported VLEN; the actual per-reg byte count is `vlenb`.
46	inline constexpr std::size_t kVScratchBytes =
47	  static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX;
48	
49	namespace detail
50	{
51	
52	// Translate scratch GPA into a byte offset inside a RAM span whose first
53	// byte sits at `ram_base`. Throws if the scratch region falls outside the
54	// supplied span (i.e. the caller passed a too-small RAM mapping).
55	inline auto scratch_offset(std::size_t ram_size, uint64_t ram_base)
56	  -> std::size_t
57	{
58	  if (kVScratchGpa < ram_base)
59	    throw std::runtime_error(
60	      "v_regfile_xfer: scratch GPA below RAM base");
61	  const auto off = static_cast<std::size_t>(kVScratchGpa - ram_base);
62	  if (off + kVScratchBytes > ram_size)
63	    throw std::runtime_error(
64	      "v_regfile_xfer: scratch region exceeds RAM span");
65	  return off;
66	}
67	
68	}  // namespace detail
69	
70	// Copy state.vreg[] into ram[scratch_offset .. scratch_offset+kVScratchBytes].
71	// Called just before vsim resumes the hart so the fixture can vle8.v from
72	// scratch and pick up QEMU 1's V values.
73	inline void stage_v_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
74	                               std::span<uint8_t> ram,
75	                               uint64_t ram_base)
76	{
77	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size(), ram_base);
78	  std::memcpy(ram.data() + off, state.vreg, kVScratchBytes);
79	}
80	
81	// Copy ram[scratch_offset .. +kVScratchBytes] into state.vreg[]. Called
82	// inside the vsim drain path after the fixture's prologue vse8.v has
83	// settled the (possibly mutated) regfile bytes into RAM.
84	inline void read_v_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
85	                                std::span<const uint8_t> ram,
86	                                uint64_t ram_base)
87	{
88	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size(), ram_base);
89	  std::memcpy(state.vreg, ram.data() + off, kVScratchBytes);
90	}
91	
92	}  // namespace hybrid

/* B7: pure decision function for the QEMU plugin V-state drain gate.
 *
 * The plugin uses one `qemu_plugin_register*` handle per architectural V
 * register. Each handle is non-NULL iff the gdbstub feature XML
 * advertised that register at plugin init. The original gate at
 * hybrid_handoff.c:296 tested `if (v->vlenb && s.vlenb > 0)` which
 * silently omits the V block when:
 *   - vlenb was not advertised but vtype/vl were (partial V), or
 *   - vlenb was advertised but read as zero (V disabled at runtime).
 *
 * Mixing the "stub broke" case with the "V disabled" case loses
 * information; the partial-advertisement case should refuse rather than
 * pretend V is absent (the resume side then mis-restores).
 *
 * This header is pure C, no QEMU plugin dependency, so it can be unit-
 * tested from a host C++ doctest.
 */
#ifndef HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H
#define HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H

#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef enum {
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK = 0,      /* proceed: copy full V block into state */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP = 1,    /* no V at all; do not set HYBRID_FLAG_V */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT = 2,   /* partial advertisement; refuse to drain */
} HybridVDrainPolicy;

/* Decide whether to drain the V block.
 *
 * has_vlenb:    1 iff the stub advertised the vlenb register handle.
 * has_other_v:  1 iff ANY of vtype/vl/vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr/vreg[*] was
 *               advertised (i.e. some V state is visible).
 * vlenb_value:  the value read from vlenb (only meaningful when has_vlenb).
 */
static inline HybridVDrainPolicy
hybrid_v_drain_policy(int has_vlenb, int has_other_v, uint64_t vlenb_value)
{
    /* Truth table (see v_drain_policy.test.cpp):
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=0          -> SKIP   (no V)
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=1          -> ABORT  (partial advertisement)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=0          -> SKIP   (nothing to drain)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb=0 -> SKIP   (V disabled at runtime)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb>0 -> OK
     */
    if (!has_vlenb && has_other_v) return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT;
    if (!has_other_v)              return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    if (vlenb_value == 0)          return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK;
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif  /* HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H */

=== cell index 13 id None ===
## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andes-sim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`), and the V-register scratch address is the
  constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), only
  correct when RAM base is 0 (true for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt`
  where it would need 0x80FF0000). The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED (2026-06): engine variant + VLEN are pluggable;
  the machine, the CPU family, and the scratch GPA still block porting to
  another core.

### L11. VLEN ceiling is 512 bits, and an over-limit vlenb truncates silently  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: an engine whose VLEN exceeds 512, or a run outside the
  driver where the two legs' VLEN configs are set by hand.
- What happens: inside `andes-sim run` the QEMU leg's vlen is copied from
  the engine descriptor (the `{vlen}` template,
  `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`), so the two legs can no longer disagree
  by construction. What remains: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per
  vector register (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`) and the
  plugin CLAMPS the drained bytes to that with no warning
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:375-377`) - a VLEN > 512 engine silently loses the
  upper bytes of every V register. The standalone fast model also hardcodes
  `vlen=512` (`engine_registry.cpp:54`). The retired Python golden keeps a
  duplicated constant (`checkpoint.py:44`, `LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`).
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `hybrid_handoff.c:375-377`,
  `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: leg-mismatch half CLOSED by the descriptor sync (2026-06); the
  512-bit ceiling and the silent clamp remain OPEN.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andes_sim/roi.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:663-671` (marker matcher);
  `verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:663-671`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you
  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary (`hsim.py:1126-1225`,
  `_run_simpoint_pipeline`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at
     each window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without
     warmup the CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate
     inherits SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py:1126-1225` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`). Note: SimPoint
  still runs only on the Python golden (`./hsim.py`); the C++ port has not
  landed.
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with

/* B7: pure decision function for the QEMU plugin V-state drain gate.
 *
 * The plugin uses one `qemu_plugin_register*` handle per architectural V
 * register. Each handle is non-NULL iff the gdbstub feature XML
 * advertised that register at plugin init. The original gate at
 * hybrid_handoff.c:296 tested `if (v->vlenb && s.vlenb > 0)` which
 * silently omits the V block when:
 *   - vlenb was not advertised but vtype/vl were (partial V), or
 *   - vlenb was advertised but read as zero (V disabled at runtime).
 *
 * Mixing the "stub broke" case with the "V disabled" case loses
 * information; the partial-advertisement case should refuse rather than
 * pretend V is absent (the resume side then mis-restores).
 *
 * This header is pure C, no QEMU plugin dependency, so it can be unit-
 * tested from a host C++ doctest.
 */
#ifndef HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H
#define HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H

#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef enum {
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK = 0,      /* proceed: copy full V block into state */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP = 1,    /* no V at all; do not set HYBRID_FLAG_V */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT = 2,   /* partial advertisement; refuse to drain */
} HybridVDrainPolicy;

/* Decide whether to drain the V block.
 *
 * has_vlenb:    1 iff the stub advertised the vlenb register handle.
 * has_other_v:  1 iff ANY of vtype/vl/vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr/vreg[*] was
 *               advertised (i.e. some V state is visible).
 * vlenb_value:  the value read from vlenb (only meaningful when has_vlenb).
 */
static inline HybridVDrainPolicy
hybrid_v_drain_policy(int has_vlenb, int has_other_v, uint64_t vlenb_value)
{
    /* Truth table (see v_drain_policy.test.cpp):
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=0          -> SKIP   (no V)
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=1          -> ABORT  (partial advertisement)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=0          -> SKIP   (nothing to drain)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb=0 -> SKIP   (V disabled at runtime)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb>0 -> OK
     */
    if (!has_vlenb && has_other_v) return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT;
    if (!has_other_v)              return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    if (vlenb_value == 0)          return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK;
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif  /* HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H */
